Climate Change and Carbon
When people think of a changing climate, images
of melting glaciers and polar bears ⓐlosing their
habitat often come to mind. But this is only one
aspect of the problem. Climate change is causing
extreme weather conditions, ⓑwhich has become
more frequent and (A)[intense / mild] worldwide.
Heatwaves, droughts, floods, and wildfires are
affecting countries around the world. In the autumn
of 2019, for example, Australia was hit by ⓒone of
the worst wildfires on record. Over six months, the
wildfires burned about 10 million hectares of land,
and killed hundreds of millions of animals.
Approximately 30 percent of the koalas in the
region ⓓis said to have been killed due to the fires.
This is why the international community ⓔhas
been seeking solutions to the climate crisis. In 2015,
195 countries (B)[signed / rejected] the Paris Agreement
to limit the temperature increase to 1.5°C above
pre-industrial levels. The countries ⓕagreed upon
the fact which the increase in atmospheric carbon is
a major reason for climate change. One key
strategy to combat it is to achieve “carbon
neutrality,” which involves (C)[breaking / maintaining]
a balance between ⓖthe amount of carbon emitted
and carbon absorbed.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: intenserejected breaking
mildsigned maintaining
intensesigned breaking
mildrejected maintaining
intensesigned maintaining
solution: (A) 기후 변화가 극단적인 기상 상황을 유발한다고 했으며, 열 파[혹서], 가뭄, 홍수와 산불이 전 세계 나라들에 영향을 미치 고 있다는 내용이 이어지므로, 극단적인 기상 상황이 세계적으 로 더 빈번하고 강렬해지고 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라 서 intense(강렬한)가 알맞다. (B) 국제적인 공동체가 기후 위기에 대한 해결책을 찾고 있다는 내용에 이어지므로, 2015년에 195개 나라가 기온 상승을 산업화 이전 수준보다 섭씨 1.5도로 제한하는 파리 협정에 서명했다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 signed(~에 서명했다)가 알맞다. (C) 파리 협정에 서명한 나라들이 대기 중 탄소의 증가가 기후 변화의 주요 원인이라는 점에 동의했다고 했으며, 그것과 싸우 는 한 가지 주요 전략은 ‘탄소 중립’을 이루는 것이라고 했으 므로, 이는 배출되는 탄소량과 흡수되는 탄소량 사이에 균형을 유지하는 것을 포함한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 maintaining(~을 유지하는 것)이 알맞다.

Let’s imagine that the Earth’s atmosphere is a
large bathtub, and ⓐthe greenhouse gases emitted
into the atmosphere are like water flowing from a
tap into the bathtub. At the bottom of the bathtub,
there’s a drain ⓑthat letting the water out. If we
keep the tap running, the water level in the
bathtub will rise, just as greenhouse gas emissions
have led to an increase in atmospheric carbon. This
rise in carbon levels ⓒhas already resulted in
negative environmental consequences, such as
climate change. ⓓTo make matters worse, if the
water is not effectively drained, the bathtub will
overflow. In other words, if we ⓔwon't reduce
carbon emissions sufficiently, atmospheric carbon
will continue to accumulate.

body:
Blue Carbon and Getbol
One of the most promising ways to reduce carbon
in the atmosphere is to (A)____________________________
________________________. The Earth’s carbon can be
divided into three types: black carbon, green
carbon, and blue carbon. Black carbon is released
while burning fossil fuels, such as coal, oil, and gas.
It causes the greenhouse effect, leading to global
warming and climate change. Green carbon, on the
other hand, is carbon absorbed by and stored in
land ecosystems, such as rainforests like the
Amazon in South America. It plays a vital role in
maintaining the ecosystem because it absorbs
carbon dioxide through photosynthesis. Finally, blue
carbon is the carbon stored in the ocean, including
coastal and marine ecosystems such as mangrove
wetlands, seagrass beds, and tidal marshes. The
carbon absorption rate of marine ecosystems is
about 50 times faster than that of land ecosystems.
Blue carbon can store up to 10 times more carbon
per unit area than forests on land, making it highly
cost-effective.
(B)청색 탄소의 눈에 띄는 예는 대양 주변에 위치한
갯벌에서 발견될 수 있다. Research conducted in
2021 has revealed that getbol in Korea stores
approximately 13 million tons of carbon and
absorbs over 260,000 tons of carbon dioxide each
year. This means that getbol alone can offset the
carbon dioxide emissions produced by 110,000 cars
in a year. Considering that getbol contains
numerous organisms and marine animals that store
carbon, the treasure house of blue carbon has
become a promising and sustainable solution to the
current environmental problem. Scientists worldwide
are continuing to explore the capabilities of tidal
flats with the goal of having them officially
recognized as blue carbon.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: use the “good” carbon on Earth
ban the use of fossil fuels completely
exploit useless rainforests for commercial use
relocate urban industrial facilities to the coastline
accelerate the development of green energytechnologies
solution: 정답은 ① 이다. (해설 없음)

Thanks to its rich biodiversity, getbol is visited by about 118 species of migratory birds every year. For millions of migratory birds that travel between Australia and the Russian Far East or Alaska, Korea’s tidal flats are a vital stopover location. Without getbol, they would not have a place to rest and feed themselves during their long journeys, and they would become extinct. Since getbol is not only a unique ecosystem crowded with diverse species but also a resting place for endangered birds, it was added to the UNESCO World Natural Heritage List in 2021. It includes the four tidal flats on the western and southern coasts of Korea: Seocheon Getbol, Gochang Getbol, Shinan Getbol, and Boseong-Suncheon Getbol.

Getbol serves as an essential staging site for millions of migratory birds flying between Australia and the Russian Far East or Alaska.
If it were not for getbol, offering rest and food during their long journeys, millions of migratory birds would be in danger of extinction.
As a distinctive habitat for diverse wildlife and threatened bird species, getbol earned a place on the UNESCO World Natural Heritage List in 2021.
All four mudflats designated as UNESCO World Natural Heritage sites are located only along Korea’s western coastline.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓑ conducting → conducted (동사구 has revealed에 대한 주 어 Research를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사가 쓰일 수 있 으나, 수식받는 명사 Research가 ‘행해진’ 대상이며 뒤에 이어 진 목적어가 없으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 conducting 을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 conducted로 고친다.) ⓕ caused → causing (완전한 절(This ~ flats) 뒤에 접속사 없이 동 사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로 흐름상 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구 문을 이끄는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 원인에 해당하는 앞 절의 내용 이 ‘초래한’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 a loss of biodiversity가 있으므로, caused를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 causing으로 고친다.) ⓖ Had it not been for → Were it not for[If it were not for] 또는 Without[But for] (주절에 ‘조동사 과거형+동사원형’인 would fail이 쓰였으며 흐름상 과거 사실이 아닌 현재 사실과 반 대되는 일을 가정하고 있으므로, ‘~이 없다면, …할 것이다’를 뜻 하는 가정법 과거 표현인 ‘Were it not for[If it were not for/But for/Without] ~, 주어+조동사 과거형+동사원형 …’을 써야 한다. 따라서 과거 사실의 반대를 가정하는 가정법 과거완료 표현인 ‘Had it not been for[If it had not been for/Without/But for] ~, 주어+조동사 과거형+have+p.p. …(~가 없었다면, …했을 것이다)’ 의 Had it not been for를 Were it not for, If it were not for, But for, Without 중 하나로 고친다.)

다음 글의 시사점으로 알맞은 것은?

One of the most promising ways to reduce carbon
in the atmosphere is to use the “good” carbon on
Earth. The Earth’s carbon can be divided into three
types: black carbon, green carbon, and blue carbon.
Black carbon is released while burning fossil fuels,
such as coal, oil, and gas. It causes the greenhouse
effect, leading to global warming and climate
change. Green carbon, on the other hand, is carbon
absorbed by and stored in land ecosystems, such as
rainforests like the Amazon in South America. It
plays a vital role in maintaining the ecosystem
because it absorbs carbon dioxide through
photosynthesis. Finally, blue carbon is the carbon
stored in the ocean, including coastal and marine
ecosystems such as mangrove wetlands, seagrass
beds, and tidal marshes. The carbon absorption rate
of marine ecosystems is about 50 times faster than
that of land ecosystems. Blue carbon can store up
to 10 times more carbon per unit area than forests
on land, making it highly cost-effective.
choices: Replacing fossil fuels with green carbon sourceswill eliminate the risk of global warming.
Black carbon must be converted into blue carbonto increase the overall rate of photosynthesis.
Preserving marine ecosystems can be a highlyefficient strategy for mitigating climate change.
Land ecosystems are more cost-effective thanmarine ecosystems in absorbing carbon dioxide.
Mangrove wetlands and tidal marshes absorbcarbon at a slower rate than rainforests like theAmazon.

body:
Hobbies Are Serious
For many people, hobbies are serious. Serious
leisure may sound like a contradiction, but that’s
what it takes for an activity (A)[to qualify /
qualifying] as a hobby. To take a hobby seriously,
you have to make a meaningful effort to improve
your skills, take risks, overcome hardships, or (B)[to
become / become] a better version of yourself. If
you meet someone who has woken up at the crack
of dawn to take a picture at the “magic hour,” you
can assume that they think of themselves as a
“photographer.” A runner, a gamer, or a
photographer are titles (C)[what / that] people are
proud to call themselves. On the other hand, you
wouldn’t call yourself a “TV watcher” or “online
surfer.” Watching TV and surfing online aren’t
considered serious hobbies because there’s no
challenge or way to improve yourself.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: to qualify  becomethat
to qualify  to becomethat
qualifying  to becomewhat
to qualify  becomewhat
qualifying  becomethat
solution: (A) 주어 자리의 it, 동사 takes, 의미상 주어 for+명사(구)/대명사와 함께 ‘it takes …(+for A)+to부정사 (A가) ~하는 데 …가 들다[필요 하다]’의 구문을 이루어야 하므로 to부정사 to qualify가 적절하다. (B) 등위접속사 or에 의해, ‘A, B, C, or D’의 형태로 to에 이어 지는 동사원형들(improve, take, overcome)이 병렬 연결되어 ‘기술을 향상하고, ~ 자신이 되기 위해’라는 뜻의 부사적 용법 의 to부정사구를 이루어야 하므로 동사원형 become이 적절하 다. 또는 ‘기술을 향상하고, ~ 자신이 되기 위한 (의미 있는 노 력)’이라는 뜻으로 명사구 a meaningful effort를 수식하는 형 용사적 용법의 to부정사로 볼 수도 있다. (C) to call의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(people ~ call themselves)을 이끌어 선행사 titles를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루 어야 하므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.

J. R. R. Tolkien, the author of The Hobbit and The
Lord of the Rings, was passionate about language.
He invented languages with grammar rules and
histories: Sindarin and Quenya, the former
ⓐinspired by Welsh, and the latter inspired by
Finnish and Latin. But ⓑinventing languages was a
frustrating hobby because he had to isolate himself
while creating them. He wrote of the isolation that
he and other people who loved languages
ⓒwere experienced: “But they become shy, ashamed
of spending the valuable commodity of time for
their private pleasure, and higher developments are
locked in secret places.”
Things are very different now. The Internet allows
people ⓓto learn about languages and meet other
language enthusiasts from all over the world.
Instead of working on their projects in private, they
can easily find other like-minded people to share
their passion, ⓔcelebrate their achievements, and
encourage each other along the way. They could
even work together on language projects that
Tolkien may have never been able to imagine.

the frustrating and lonely process of inventing anew language
the negative effects of isolating oneself
the historical background and origins of Tolkien’sinvented languages
the shift of language creation from a solitaryhobby into a shared experience

body:
Hobbies Are Gratifying
While some people pursue a hobby to improve
their skills, some do for the sheer pleasure of doing
it. Albert Einstein started learning to sail when he
was 18 years old, venturing out on the lakes in
Switzerland and simply enjoying the time on his
boat. He continued to enjoy sailing as a life-long
sailor. (A)그는 물리학의 천재로 여겨짐에도 불구하고,
뛰어난 선원이 아니었으며, 자신의 항해술에도 신경
쓰지 않았다. His technique remained at a basic
level, which was simply to “Set sail, make it fast, no
thoughts of energy or speed, lean back, let the
boat drift.”
On a boat, he forgot everything else in the world,
which may explain why he enjoyed sailing so much.
For him, it was being out on the water that
mattered the most. Einstein used the hobby of
sailing to go to a place where he could be
completely relaxed. Maybe that’s why he named his
boat Tinef, meaning “worthless” in Yiddish, after the
apparent meaninglessness of his sailing adventures.
Watching the waves while on his boat, Einstein
forgot all his worries. Like Einstein, for many people,
hobbies just provide the conditions for a sense of
pure satisfaction.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Einstein continued sailing for many years becausehe found joy in the activity itself.
Einstein’s sailing method stayed simple rather thanbecoming highly advanced.
Einstein may have named his boat Tinef becausehe wanted to show his great achievements insailing.
Sailing helped Einstein forget his concerns andrelax while he was on the water.
Many people pursue hobbies because they canexperience a feeling of pure satisfaction.
solution: 무의미한 것처럼 보이는 자신의 항해 모험을 따서 자신의 배 이름을 이디시어로 ‘가치 없는’이라는 뜻의 ‘티네프(Tinef)’로 지 었을지도 모른다는 내용이 두 번째 문단에 언급되었으므로 ❸ ‘아인슈타인(Einstein)은 자신의 뛰어난 항해 성과를 보여 주고 싶었기 때문에 자신의 배를 ‘티네프(Tinef)’라고 이름을 붙였을 지도 모른다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

Nowadays, everybody has a hobby they like to do in their free time. In the past, though, this probably wasn’t true because most people had to work long hours in agriculture or manufacturing, so free time must have been hard to come by. However, the Industrial Revolution and the labor movement that followed it led to a gradual decrease in working hours to eight-hour work days and five-day work weeks. For the first time in history, a majority of people had free time to enjoy activities that they found meaningful outside of work: hobbies.

[요약문] People in the past (A)____________ time for hobbies, but (B)____________ working hours after the Industrial Revolution and the labor movement allowed them to enjoy meaningful activities beyond work.
choices: (A) wanted — (B) extended
(A) lacked — (B) extended
(A) possessed — (B) shortened
(A) lacked — (B) reduced
(A) lacked — (B) increased
solution:
1. 과거에는 대부분 농업·제조업에서 오래 일해야 해서 여가 시간을 얻기 어려웠다(free time must have been hard to come by) → (A) lacked(부족했다).
2. 산업혁명과 노동 운동 뒤 근로 시간이 하루 8시간, 주 5일로 점차 줄었다(a gradual decrease in working hours) → (B) reduced(줄어든).
3. ②·⑤는 (B)가 글과 반대이고, ①의 wanted·③의 possessed는 (A)가 글과 맞지 않는다.
4. 따라서 답은 ④이다.

body:
Long-distance hiking trails are becoming popular
with more and more people. Let’s explore the
appeal of long-distance hiking through a famous
trail, the PCT.
The PCT, or Pacific Crest Trail, is a 4,265-kilometer
long hiking trail that stretches vertically across the
U.S. Being so long, it crosses three states and seven
national parks. Hikers can experience a varied range
of landscapes, from hot desert regions to great
mountain ranges. It takes about five months for the
average person to walk through the trail, which is
known as thru-hiking. “Thru-hikers” usually start in
early spring and head north, arriving at their
destination in early winter. It’s a hard journey with a
low completion rate; just 14% of all hikers attempting
a thru-hiking succeed in finishing the PCT.
In addition to the physical difficulties and mental
isolation, surviving in nature for months itself can
be a tremendous challenge. (A) Hikers cook their
own meals, and sometimes they have to endure
days without eating. (B) Hikers are advised to carry
the latest PCT Water Report, a list of all water
sources. (C) When it comes to sleeping, most hikers
sleep in tents, and in some areas, they can use
shelters to stay safe from the harsh weather. (D) If
you are lucky, you may find “trail angels,” who
provide transportation to close towns, meals, or
other forms of assistance. (E)
Why Do They Bother? Hear from Finishers.
• While the PCT was demanding, it was also a gift.
It allowed me to see what I am truly capable of.
• Traveling the PCT can be about the people you
meet along the way. The trail has led to lasting
friendships.
• The PCT is a journey of a lifetime. It is a chance
to see the magnificent landscapes of the
American West.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the characteristics and challenges of thru-hikingthe PCT
the necessary equipment and supplies for survivingon the PCT
how to address the low completion rate of thefive-month hike
the personal benefits of experiencing a longjourney in nature
the diverse geographical features and climaticvariations across the U.S.
solution: PCT는 미국을 가로지르는 대표적인 장거리 하이킹 코스로, 다양한 자 연경관을 경험할 수 있다는 매력이 있지만 약 5개월에 걸친 종주 동안 신체적 어려움과 정신적 고립을 견뎌야 할 뿐만 아니라 식량, 물, 숙소 등 생존과 관련된 여러 어려움도 극복해야 하는 힘든 여정이라는 내용 의 글이므로, ❶ ‘PCT 스루 하이킹의 특징과 어려움’이 적절하다.

solution: (A) 다음 문장에서 톨킨이 자신과 언어를 사랑하는 다른 사람 들이 겪었던 고립감(isolation)에 대해 글을 썼다고 했으므로 ‘isolate(고립시키다)’가 적절하다. (B) 앞에서, 사람들이 부끄러워하며 자신들의 사적인 즐거움을 위해 시간이라는 귀중한 재화를 쓰는 것을 부끄러워한다고 했 으므로 더 높은 수준의 언어적 발전은 결국 비밀스러운 장소 에 갇히게 된다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘secret(비밀스러 운)’이 적절하다. (C) 과거에는 혼자 작업했던 것과 달리 현재는 인터넷의 발달 로 다른 이들과 소통할 수 있고, 열정을 공유할 마음이 맞는 사람들을 쉽게 찾을 수 있다고 했으므로 ‘개인적으로 자신의 프로젝트를 진행하는 대신에’라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘(in) private(개인적으로)’이 적절하다.

body:
Long-distance hiking trails are becoming popular
with more and more people. Let’s explore the
appeal of long-distance hiking through a famous
trail, the PCT.
The PCT, or Pacific Crest Trail, is a 4,265-kilometer
long hiking trail that stretches vertically across the
U.S. Being so long, it crosses three states and seven
national parks. Hikers can experience a varied range
of landscapes, from hot desert regions to great
mountain ranges. It takes about five months for the
average person to walk through the trail, which is
known as thru-hiking. “Thru-hikers” usually start in
early spring and head north, arriving at their
destination in early winter. It’s a hard journey with a
low completion rate; just 14% of all hikers attempting
a thru-hiking succeed in finishing the PCT.
In addition to the physical difficulties and mental
isolation, surviving in nature for months itself can
be a tremendous challenge. (A) Hikers cook their
own meals, and sometimes they have to endure
days without eating. (B) Hikers are advised to carry
the latest PCT Water Report, a list of all water
sources. (C) When it comes to sleeping, most hikers
sleep in tents, and in some areas, they can use
shelters to stay safe from the harsh weather. (D) If
you are lucky, you may find “trail angels,” who
provide transportation to close towns, meals, or
other forms of assistance. (E)
Why Do They Bother? Hear from Finishers.
• While the PCT was demanding, it was also a gift.
It allowed me to see what I am truly capable of.
• Traveling the PCT can be about the people you
meet along the way. The trail has led to lasting
friendships.
• The PCT is a journey of a lifetime. It is a chance
to see the magnificent landscapes of the
American West.

Hobbies Are Gratifying
While some people pursue a hobby to improve
their skills, some do for the sheer pleasure of doing
it. Albert Einstein started learning to sail when he
was 18 years old, venturing out on the lakes in
Switzerland and simply enjoying the time on his
boat. He continued to enjoy sailing as a life-long
sailor. Although he is considered a genius in
physics, he wasn’t a good sailor, nor did he care
about his sailing technique. His technique remained
at a(n) (A)____________ level, which was simply to
“Set sail, make it fast, no thoughts of energy or
speed, lean back, let the boat drift.”
On a boat, he forgot everything else in the world,
which may explain why he enjoyed sailing so much.
For him, it was being out on the water that
mattered the most. Einstein used the hobby of
sailing to go to a place where he could be
completely relaxed. Maybe that’s why he named his
boat Tinef, meaning “worthless” in Yiddish, after the
apparent (B)____________ of his sailing adventures.
Watching the waves while on his boat, Einstein
forgot all his worries. Like Einstein, for many people,
hobbies just provide the conditions for a sense of
pure satisfaction.
(A)
(B)

advancedpointlessness
advancedmeaninglessness
elementarymeaningfulness
basicmeaninglessness비상(홍민표) 1과

You may be surprised to find that pursuing a
hobby can accomplish more than self-satisfaction.
That is, it sometimes __________________________________
______________________. For example, Thomas Bopp, a
manager at a construction materials factory and an
amateur astronomer, discovered the comet
Hale-Bopp while observing the sky with his friends
in the Arizona desert. To make the story even more
shocking, he was using a borrowed telescope that
his friend had assembled himself. And Bopp is not
alone. Numerous amateur astronomers have
discovered comets, stars, and supernovas, which
helps us to better understand the solar system and
the universe. Amateurs in many other fields have
made important contributions through their hobbies,
such as amateur programmers developing new
technologies, amateur writers publishing their work
in local magazines, amateur history researchers
preserving historical sites … The list goes on and
on!
choices: leads to an unexpected contribution to society
requires professional skills and advanced equipment
hinders people from focusing on their primarycareers
results in a predictable financial reward for amateurs
forces individuals to isolate themselves fromtheir community

body:
다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

For many people, hobbies are serious. Serious leisure may sound like a contradiction, but that’s what it takes for an activity to qualify as a hobby. To take a hobby seriously, you have to make a meaningful effort to improve your skills, take risks, overcome hardships, or become a better version of yourself. If you meet someone who has woken up at the crack of dawn to take a picture at the “magic hour,” you can assume that they think of themselves as a “photographer.” A runner, a gamer, or a photographer are titles that people are proud to call themselves. On the other hand, you wouldn’t call yourself a “TV watcher” or “online surfer.” Watching TV and surfing online aren’t considered serious hobbies because there’s no challenge or way to improve yourself.

What effort is required for an activity to qualify as a serious hobby?
What makes people who get up at dawn to take photographs feel proud?
Why are watching TV and surfing online not considered serious hobbies?
What motivates people to choose a particular hobby over other activities?

practice, you’ll be taking nice photos.

body:
Hobbies Are Serious
For many people, hobbies are serious. Serious
leisure may sound like a contradiction, but that’s
what it takes for an activity ⓐ[qualifies / to qualify]
as a hobby. To take a hobby seriously, you have to
make a meaningful effort to improve your skills,
take risks, overcome hardships, or become a better
version of yourself. If you meet someone who has
woken up at the crack of dawn to take a picture at
the “magic hour,” you can assume ⓑ[that / what]
they think of themselves as a “photographer.” A
runner, a gamer, or a photographer are titles that
people are (A)____________ to call themselves. On the
other hand, you wouldn’t call yourself a “TV
watcher” or “online surfer.” Watching TV and surfing
online aren’t considered serious hobbies because
there’s no challenge or way to improve yourself.
Hobbies Create Community
J. R. R. Tolkien, the author of The Hobbit and The
Lord of the Rings, was passionate about language.
He invented languages with grammar rules and
histories: Sindarin and Quenya, the former inspired
by Welsh, and the latter inspired by Finnish and
Latin. But inventing languages was a frustrating
hobby because he had to isolate himself while
creating them. He wrote of the (B)____________ that
he and other people who loved languages
experienced: “But they become shy, ashamed of
spending the valuable commodity of time for their
private pleasure, and higher developments are
locked in secret places.”
Things are very different now. The Internet allows
people to learn about languages and meet other
language enthusiasts from all over the world.
Instead of working on their projects in private, they
can easily find other like-minded people to share
their passion, celebrate their achievements, and
encourage each other along the way. They could
even work together on language projects ⓒ[what /
that] Tolkien may have never been able to imagine.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

ⓐ
ⓑ
ⓒ
choices: to qualify   that      that
to qualify   what       that
qualifies   what       what
to qualify   that      what
qualifies   that      that
solution: ⓐ 주어 자리의 it, 동사 takes, to부정사의 의미상 주어를 나타 내는 for와 함께 ‘it takes …(+for A)+to부정사 (A가) ~하는 데 …가 들다[필요하다]’의 구문을 이루어야 하므로 to부정사 to qualify가 적절하다. ⓑ 완전한 절(they ~ “photographer.”)을 이끌어 동사 assume 의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접 속사 that이 적절하다. ⓒ to imagine의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(Tolkien ~ imagine)을 이끌어 선행사 language projects를 수식하는 관계 사절을 이루어야 하므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.

body:
Hobbies Can Contribute
㉠여러분은 취미를 추구하는 것이 자기만족 이상의
것을 성취할 수 있다는 사실을 알게 되어 놀랄지도 모
른다. That is, it sometimes leads to an unexpected
(A)contribution to society. For example, Thomas
Bopp, a manager at a construction materials factory
and an (B)amateur astronomer, discovered the
comet Hale-Bopp while observing the sky with his
friends in the Arizona desert. To make the story
ⓐeven more shocking, he was using a borrowed
(C)telescope that his friend had assembled himself.
And Bopp is not alone. Numerous amateur
astronomers have discovered comets, stars, and
supernovas, which helps us ⓑto better understand
the solar system and the universe. Amateurs in
many other fields have made important contributions
through their hobbies, such as amateur programmers
developing new technologies, amateur writers
publishing their work in local magazines, amateur
history researchers preserving historical sites ... The
list goes on and on!
There are many reasons why people pursue
hobbies. For many people, the challenge of learning
a new skill or achieving a difficult goal is their
primary (D)motivation. Other people enjoy hobbies
for the communities ⓒwhere they can become a
part of or the friendships they can make there. Still
others enjoy hobbies because they can lose track of
time and be in the moment, similar to being in a
(E)meditative state. Some people even end up making
contributions to society through their hobbies,
oftentimes unexpectedly. It is the physical, mental,
or emotional experience, or even a combination of
them, that makes a hobby ⓓrewarding and fun.
Perhaps it ⓔshould call “pleisure.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E)의 영영풀이로 알맞은 것을모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

<보기>
(A): something that you give or do in order to
help something be successful
(B): doing a job, sport, or activity for money, rather
than just for fun
(C): an optical instrument used for viewing very
small objects, such as mineral samples or
animal or plant cells
(D): the reason why you want to do something
(E): relating to the practice of emptying your
mind of thoughts and feelings, in order to
relax completely or for religious reasons
solution: (A) 공헌: 어떤 것이 성공하도록 돕기 위해 당신이 주거나 하는 것 (D) 동기: 당신이 무언가를 하고 싶어 하는 이유 (E) 명상의: 완전히 긴장을 풀기 위해 또는 종교적인 이유로 당 신의 마음에서 생각과 감정을 비워내는 수행과 관련된 비상(홍민표) 1과

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

The PCT, or Pacific Crest Trail, is a 4,265-kilometer
long hiking trail that stretches vertically across the U.S.
Being so long, it crosses three states and seven
national parks. Hikers can experience a (A)[monotonous
/ varied] range of landscapes, from hot desert regions
to great mountain ranges. It takes about five months
for the average person to walk through the trail,
which is known as thru-hiking. “Thru-hikers” usually
start in early spring and head north, arriving at their
destination in early winter. It’s a hard journey with a
low completion rate; just 14% of all hikers attempting
a thru-hiking succeed in finishing the PCT.
In addition to the physical difficulties and mental
isolation, surviving in nature for months itself can
be a tremendous challenge. Hikers cook their own
meals, and sometimes they have to endure days
without eating. Securing water is another (B)[minor
/ crucial] requirement because not all the water
sources are safe to drink. Hikers are advised to
carry the latest PCT Water Report, a list of all water
sources. When it comes to sleeping, most hikers sleep
in tents, and in some areas, they can use shelters to
stay safe from the harsh weather. If you are lucky,
you may find “trail angels,” who provide transportation
to close towns, meals, or other forms of assistance.
Why Do They Bother? Hear from Finishers.
• While the PCT was (C)[demanding / effortless], it
was also a gift. It allowed me to see what I am
truly capable of.
• Traveling the PCT can be about the people you meet
along the way. The trail has led to lasting friendships.
• The PCT is a journey of a lifetime. It is a chance to
see the magnificent landscapes of the American West.
(A)
(B)             (C)
choices: monotonous     crucialdemanding
varied     crucialeffortless
monotonous     minoreffortless
varied     crucialdemanding
varied     minordemanding
solution: (A) 앞에서 PCT는 세 개의 주와 일곱 개의 국립 공원을 통과한다 고 했고, 뒤에서 뜨거운 사막 지대부터 웅장한 산맥까지 경험할 수 있다고 했으므로 다양한 풍경이라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라 서 varied(다양한)가 적절하다. (B) 자연에서 수개월 동안 생활해야 하며 모든 수원이 마실 수 있는 것은 아니라고 했으므로, 물을 확보하는 것은 매우 중요하 다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 crucial(필수적인)이 적절하다. (C) 앞에서 낮은 완주율, 식수 확보의 어려움, 가혹한 날씨 등을 언 급했으며, ‘~이지만’을 뜻하는 접속사 While이 쓰였으므로 주절에서 언급한 ‘선물(gift)’과 대조되는 의미의 demanding(힘든)이 적절하다.

For many people, hobbies are serious.
(A) On the other hand, you wouldn’t call yourself a
“TV watcher” or “online surfer.” Watching TV
and surfing online aren’t considered serious
hobbies because there’s no challenge or way to
improve yourself.
(B) Serious leisure may sound like a contradiction,
but that’s what it takes for an activity to qualify
as a hobby. To take a hobby seriously, you
have to make a meaningful effort to improve
your skills, take risks, overcome hardships, or
become a better version of yourself.
(C) If you meet someone who has woken up at the
crack of dawn to take a picture at the “magic
hour,” you can assume that they think of
themselves as a “photographer.” A runner, a
gamer, or a photographer are titles that people
are proud to call themselves.

body:
While some people pursue a hobby to improve
their skills, some do for the sheer pleasure of doing
it. Albert Einstein started learning to sail when he
was 18 years old, venturing out on the lakes in
Switzerland and simply enjoying the time on his
boat. He continued to enjoy sailing as a life-long
sailor. Although he is considered a genius in
physics, he wasn’t a good sailor, nor did he care
about his sailing technique. His technique remained
at a basic level, which was simply to “Set sail, make
it fast, no thoughts of energy or speed, lean back,
let the boat drift.”
On a boat, he forgot everything else in the world,
which may explain why he enjoyed sailing so much.
For him, it was being out on the water (A)[what /
that] mattered the most. Einstein used the hobby of
sailing to go to a place (B)[which / where] he could
be completely relaxed. Maybe that’s why he named
his boat Tinef, meaning “worthless” in Yiddish, after
the apparent meaninglessness of his sailing
adventures. (C)[Watching / Watch] the waves while
on his boat, Einstein forgot all his worries. Like
Einstein, for many people, hobbies just provide the
conditions for a sense of pure satisfaction.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: whatwhere      Watching
thatwhich      Watching
thatwhere      Watch
whatwhich      Watch
thatwhere      Watching
solution: (A) 주어 자리의 it, 동사 was와 함께 동명사구 ‘being out on the water(물 위에 나가 있는 것)’를 강조하는 ‘it is[was] ~ that …(…한 것은 바로 ~이다[이었다])’ 형태의 ‘it - that’ 강조구 문을 이루어야 하므로 that이 적절하다. (B) 완전한 절(he ~ relaxed)을 이끌어 선행사 a place를 수식하 는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 관계부사 where가 적절하다. (C) 콤마(,) 뒤의 완전한 절(Einstein ~ worries)과 접속사 없이 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며 주어 Einstein이 ‘보는’ 주체이므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 Watching이 적절 하다.

Hobbies Are Gratifying
While some people pursue a hobby to improve
their skills, some do for the sheer pleasure of doing
it. Albert Einstein started learning to sail when he
was 18 years old, venturing out on the lakes in
Switzerland and simply enjoying the time on his
boat. He continued to enjoy sailing as a life-long
sailor. Although he is considered a genius in
physics, he wasn’t a good sailor, nor did he care
about his sailing technique. His technique remained
at a basic level, which was simply to “Set sail, make
it fast, no thoughts of energy or speed, lean back,
let the boat drift.”
On a boat, he forgot everything else in the world,
which may explain why he enjoyed sailing so much.
For him, it was being out on the water that
mattered the most. Einstein used the hobby of
sailing to go to a place where he could be
completely relaxed. Maybe that’s why he named his
boat Tinef, meaning “worthless” in Yiddish, after the
apparent meaninglessness of his sailing adventures.
Watching the waves while on his boat, Einstein
forgot all his worries. Like Einstein, for many people,
hobbies just provide __________________________________
_________________________.

the visible results of their continuous hard workand effort
the practical means to solve realistic problems intheir lives
the conditions for a sense of pure satisfaction
the recognition of their abilities from others비상(홍민표) 1과

Hobbies Are Modern Activities
Nowadays, everybody has a hobby they like to do
in their free time. In the past, though, this probably
wasn’t true because most people had to work long
hours in agriculture or manufacturing, so free time
must have been hard to come by. However, the
Industrial Revolution and the labor movement that
followed it led to a gradual decrease in working
hours to eight-hour work days and five-day work
weeks. For the first time in history, a majority of
people had free time to enjoy activities that they
found meaningful outside of work: hobbies.
Hobbies Are Serious
For many people, hobbies are serious. Serious leisure
may sound like a contradiction, but that’s what it
takes for an activity to qualify as a hobby. To take a
hobby seriously, you have to make a meaningful
effort to improve your skills, take risks, overcome
hardships, or become a better version of yourself. If
you meet someone who has woken up at the crack
of dawn to take a picture at the “magic hour,” you
can assume that they think of themselves as a
“photographer.” A runner, a gamer, or a photographer
are titles that people are proud to call themselves. On
the other hand, you wouldn’t call yourself a “TV
watcher” or “online surfer.” Watching TV and surfing
online aren’t considered serious hobbies because
there’s no challenge or way to improve yourself.
choices: These days, everyone has their own activity thatthey enjoy doing when they are not working.
The Industrial Revolution and the labor movementcontributed to shorter working hours.
The reduction in working hours gradually gavemore people the chance to enjoy meaningfulactivities outside their jobs.
A serious hobby involves trying to develop one'sabilities rather than simply enjoying an activity.
An activity can still be regarded as a serioushobby even if it offers neither challenge norpersonal development.

with more and more people. Let’s explore the
appeal of long-distance hiking through a famous
trail, the PCT.
What Is the PCT?
The PCT, or Pacific Crest Trail, is a 4,265-kilometer
long hiking trail that stretches vertically across the
U.S. Being so long, it crosses three states and seven
national parks. Hikers can experience a varied range
of landscapes, from hot desert regions to great
mountain ranges. It takes about five months for the
average person (A)[walks / to walk] through the
trail, which is known as thru-hiking. “Thru-hikers”
usually start in early spring and head north,
(B)[arrive / arriving] at their destination in early
winter. It’s a hard journey with a low completion
rate; just 14% of all hikers attempting a thru-hiking
(C)[succeed / to succeed] in finishing the PCT.

body:
Long-distance hiking trails are becoming popular
with more and more people. Let’s explore the
appeal of long-distance hiking through a famous
trail, the PCT.
What Is the PCT?
The PCT, or Pacific Crest Trail, is a 4,265-kilometer
long hiking trail that stretches vertically across the
U.S. Being so long, it crosses three states and seven
national parks. Hikers can experience a varied range
of landscapes, from hot desert regions to great
mountain ranges. It takes about five months for the
average person (A)[walks / to walk] through the
trail, which is known as thru-hiking. “Thru-hikers”
usually start in early spring and head north,
(B)[arrive / arriving] at their destination in early
winter. It’s a hard journey with a low completion
rate; just 14% of all hikers attempting a thru-hiking
(C)[succeed / to succeed] in finishing the PCT.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

In addition to the physical difficulties and mental
isolation, surviving in nature for months itself can
be a tremendous challenge. Hikers cook their own
meals, and sometimes they have to endure days
without eating. Securing water is another crucial
requirement because not all the water sources are
safe to drink. Hikers are advised to carry the latest
PCT Water Report, a list of all water sources. When
it comes to sleeping, most hikers sleep in tents,
and in some areas, they can use shelters to stay
safe from the harsh weather. If you are lucky, you
may find “trail angels,” who provide transportation
to close towns, meals, or other forms of assistance.
Why Do They Bother? Hear from Finishers.
• While the PCT was demanding, it was also a gift.
It allowed me to see what I am truly capable of.
• Traveling the PCT can be about the people you
meet along the way. The trail has led to lasting
friendships.
• The PCT is a journey of a lifetime. It is a chance
to see the magnificent landscapes of the American
West.

Hobbies Are Modern Activities
Nowadays, everybody has a hobby they like to do
in their free time. In the past, though, this probably
wasn’t true because most people had to work long
hours in agriculture or manufacturing, so free time
must have been hard to come by. (A)____________,
the Industrial Revolution and the labor ⓐmovement
that followed it led to a gradual decrease in
working hours to eight-hour work days and five-day
work weeks. For the first time in history, a majority
of people had free time to enjoy activities that they
found meaningful outside of work: hobbies.
Hobbies Are Serious
For many people, hobbies are ⓑserious. Serious
leisure may sound like a ⓒcontradiction, but that’s
what it takes for an activity to ⓓqualify as a
hobby. To take a hobby seriously, you have to
make a meaningful effort to improve your skills,
take risks, overcome hardships, or become a better
version of yourself. If you meet someone who has
woken up at the crack of dawn to take a picture at
the “magic hour,” you can assume that they think
of themselves as a “photographer.” A runner, a
gamer, or a photographer are ⓔtitles that people
are proud to call themselves. (B)____________, you
wouldn’t call yourself a “TV watcher” or “online
surfer.” Watching TV and surfing online aren’t
considered serious hobbies because there’s no
challenge or way to improve yourself.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Hobbies Create Community
J. R. R. Tolkien, the author of The Hobbit and The
Lord of the Rings, was passionate about language.
He invented languages with grammar rules and
histories: Sindarin and Quenya, the former inspired
by Welsh, and the latter inspired by Finnish and
Latin. But inventing languages was a frustrating
hobby because he had to isolate himself while
creating them. He wrote of the isolation that he
and other people who loved languages experienced:
“But they become shy, ashamed of spending the
valuable commodity of time for their private
pleasure, and higher developments are locked in
secret places.”
Things are very different now. The Internet allows
people to learn about languages and meet other
language enthusiasts from all over the world.
Instead of working on their projects in private, they
can easily find other like-minded people to share
their passion, celebrate their achievements, and
encourage each other along the way. They could
even work together on language projects that
Tolkien may have never been able to imagine.
choices: Tolkien invented languages based on the featuresof several real languages.
Creating new languages required Tolkien tospend much of his time alone.
The Internet enables language enthusiasts tomeet people with similar interests.
Modern language lovers usually continue towork on their projects in private.
The Internet lets people share their passion andcooperate on language projects.

Hobbies Are Gratifying
While some people pursue a hobby to improve
their skills, some do __________________________________.
Albert Einstein started learning to sail when he was
18 years old, venturing out on the lakes in
Switzerland and simply enjoying the time on his
boat. He continued to enjoy sailing as a life-long
sailor. Although he is considered a genius in
physics, he wasn’t a good sailor, nor did he care
about his sailing technique. His technique remained
at a basic level, which was simply to “Set sail, make
it fast, no thoughts of energy or speed, lean back,
let the boat drift.”
On a boat, he forgot everything else in the world,
which may explain why he enjoyed sailing so much.
For him, it was being out on the water that
mattered the most. Einstein used the hobby of
sailing to go to a place where he could be
completely relaxed. Maybe that’s why he named his
boat Tinef, meaning “worthless” in Yiddish, after the
apparent meaninglessness of his sailing adventures.
Watching the waves while on his boat, Einstein
forgot all his worries. Like Einstein, for many people,
hobbies just provide the conditions for a sense of
pure satisfaction.

because they want to become professional experts

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Hobbies Can Contribute
You may be surprised to find that pursuing a
hobby can accomplish more than self-satisfaction.
That is, it sometimes leads to a(n) (A)[predictable /
unexpected] contribution to society. For example,
Thomas Bopp, a manager at a construction materials factory and an amateur astronomer,
discovered the comet Hale-Bopp while observing
the sky with his friends in the Arizona desert. To
make the story even more shocking, he was using
a borrowed telescope that his friend had assembled
himself. And Bopp is not alone. Numerous amateur
astronomers have discovered comets, stars, and
supernovas, which helps us to better understand the
solar system and the universe. Amateurs in many
other fields have made important contributions
through their hobbies, such as amateur
programmers developing new technologies, amateur
writers publishing their work in local magazines,
amateur history researchers preserving historical
sites ... The list goes on and on!
There are many reasons why people pursue
hobbies. For many people, the challenge of learning
a new skill or achieving a difficult goal is their
primary (B)[motivation / discouragement]. Other
people enjoy hobbies for the communities they can
become a part of or the friendships they can make
there. Still others enjoy hobbies because they can
lose track of time and be in the moment, similar to
being in a (C)[distracted / meditative] state. Some
people even end up making contributions to society
through their hobbies, oftentimes unexpectedly. It is
the physical, mental, or emotional experience, or
even a combination of them, that makes a hobby
rewarding and fun. Perhaps it should be called
“pleisure.”
(A)
(B)               (C)

unexpected    motivation  meditative

predictable  motivation       meditative

There is light at the end of the tunnel, however.
The sports community is optimistic that it can reduce
its environmental impact by taking two main steps:
ⓐtransitioning to more sustainable operations before,
during, and after events and ⓑraising awareness
among the public about their impact. Efforts to adopt
more responsible approaches have been made by
various organizations, and the International Olympic
Committee (IOC) is leading the way by setting a
good example. The IOC set up the Sport and
Environment Commission decades ago and ⓒdeclared
the environment as essential to the Olympic
Movement, in addition to sports and culture. It has
since encouraged host nations to adopt more
environmental approaches to putting on the Olympics.
As a result, the Olympic Village built for the 2000
Sydney Summer Olympics became the world’s
largest solar-powered suburb and the 2002 Salt
Lake City Winter Olympics ⓓadopted a new energy
recycling system which used the curling hall’s air
conditioning unit to heat the showers and bathrooms
in the ⓔvenue. Also, for the 2010 Vancouver Winter
Olympics, the Olympic speed-skating venue was built
with salvaged timber. (A)한때 오염되었던 산업 대지
위에 지어진 2012년 런던 하계 올림픽의 ‘올림픽 파크‘는
유럽에서 가장 큰 도시 공원으로 탈바꿈되었다. Then
at the 2020 Tokyo Summer Olympics, electricity was
generated with hydrogen instead of fossil fuel,
which supplied power for many residential buildings
in the Olympic Village and Paralympic Village.

On April 20, 2010, an enormous explosion shook
the Deepwater Horizon drilling platform in the Gulf
of Mexico, causing a significant oil leak into the
sea. Over a three-month period, approximately 134
million gallons of oil, comparable to more than 200
Olympic swimming pools, flowed into the sea before
it was eventually halted. Despite continuing restoration
efforts, the sea has not yet fully recovered.
(A) When an oil spill occurs, these bacteria are
attracted to the oil and begin to multiply. As
they grow, they release enzymes that break
down oil into carbon dioxide and water.
(B) One approach to addressing the issue of oil
contamination is bioremediation, a restoration
method that utilizes bacteria. Some types of
bacteria naturally exist in marine environments
and possess the capability to break down
various components of oil.
(C) Although this process may take several weeks or
months, it represents a more sustainable method
of cleaning up oil spills compared to conventional
approaches involving harmful chemicals.
Bacteria can also play a role in the process of
plastic decomposition. When plastic enters the ocean,
some bacteria are attracted to it, leading to their
growth and reproduction. Similar to the process of
breaking down oil, the bacteria release enzymes
that break down plastic into smaller molecules,
ultimately resulting in carbon dioxide and water.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

It’s not all good news, however. There are challenges
associated with bioremediation. The breakdown of
oil or plastic by bacteria, as mentioned earlier, can
be a time-consuming process requiring weeks or
months. These bacteria can also be sensitive to

body:
Many sporting events have a negative impact on
the environment because they require massive
structures to host them. To draw more spectators,
sports stadiums and sporting facilities are getting
bigger, consuming larger areas of land and requiring
greater amounts of building materials for construction.
Whenever a hectare of grassland is cleared for a
construction site, there is a loss of nature. Every ton
of concrete and steel used in the building
foundation and structure is produced, transported,
poured, and put together by equipment and facilities
that emit waste into the ground and atmosphere.
Then, after the stadium is completed, large amounts
of water, electricity, and other forms of resources
are consumed to operate and maintain the facility.
Every sporting event affects the environment
before, during, and even after it. (A) For example, a
long-track speed skating competition can only take
place, provided that the ice of a 400-meter oval
track is frozen until it is 3 to 5 cm thick. (B) As
long as the competition is on, the track needs to
be kept frozen by specialized refrigeration systems
while the temperature, humidity, and air quality
inside the stadium also have to be maintained for
optimal ice conditions. (C) Additionally, all of the
stadium employees, athletes, and spectators need to
travel to and from the stadium, often from other
cities or even from abroad. (D) During the event,
spectators and athletes eat and drink, and the
plastic bottles and wrappers of whatever they
consumed leave trash cans overflowing. (E) After the
event has ended, in addition to the significant
amount of trash that needs to be disposed of, the
effects those people caused and the emissions
generated from their travel continue to have a
lasting negative impact on air quality.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: challenges in maintaining optimal conditions forwinter sports facilities
the need to build eco-friendly stadiums to protectthe environment
the environmental consequences of hosting majorsporting events
how sporting facilities are constructed andmaintained
the economic and social costs of running sportingevents
solution: 스포츠 행사는 경기장 건설부터 많은 땅이 개간되어 자연이 사라지고, 완공 이후에도 대규모 스포츠 시설과 운영에는 많은 자원과 에너지가 필요하며, 대회 개최 시에는 선수와 관중의 이동, 쓰레기 발생 등 여러 과정에서 환경에 부정적인 영향을 미칠 뿐만 아니라, 이로 인한 배출과 폐기물이 대회 종료 후에도 환경에 지속적인 영향을 준다고 했으므로 이 글의 주제로 ❸ ‘주요 스포츠 행사를 개최하는 것의 환경적 결과’가 적절하다.

다음 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

M: Can you hand me a grocery bag?
W: Do you mean one of these cotton bags?
M: Yes. They are reusable and environmentally friendly,
unlike disposable plastic bags.
W: Are you sure? I read an article recently about
those bags. It contended that reusable bags are
only effective if they are used more than 7,100
times.
M: Is that a lot?
W: Of course. That means you’d have to utilize the
same bag every day for 20 years.
M: Wow! Then, should I give up and go back to
disposable plastic bags?
W: Not necessarily. Just remember to use reusable
bags as often as you can.
M: Okay. I’ll use the ones I have until they fall
apart.
W: Good idea. It’s important to put sustainability
into practice in our daily lives.

The woman explained that reusable bags mightnot provide environmental benefits unless peopleuse them thousands of times.
The woman suggested that the man shouldstop using reusable bags because they requiretoo much effort to be environmentally effective.
Themandecidedtocontinueusinghisreusable bags until they were no longer usable.
Thewomanemphasizedthatpracticingsustainabilitythrougheverydayactionsisimportant.

body:
Every sporting event affects the environment
before, during, and even after it. For example, a
long-track speed skating competition can only take
place, provided that the ice of a 400-meter oval
track is frozen until it is 3 to 5 cm thick. As long
as the competition is on, the track needs to be
kept frozen by specialized refrigeration systems
while the temperature, humidity, and air quality
inside the stadium also have to be maintained for
optimal ice conditions. Additionally, all of the
stadium employees, athletes, and spectators need to
travel to and from the stadium, often from other
cities or even from abroad. In fact, more than 25%
of the emissions generated by the 2018
PyeongChang Winter Olympics are estimated to be
caused by fan travel and accommodations. During
the event, spectators and athletes eat and drink,
and the plastic bottles and wrappers of whatever
they consumed leave trash cans (A)[vacant /
overflowing]. After the event has ended, in addition
to the significant amount of trash that needs to be
disposed of, ⓐ그 사람들이 초래한 영향과 그들의 이
동으로부터 발생된 배기가스는 대기 질에 계속해서 지
속적인 부정적 영향을 미친다.
Alarm bells sounded when research (B)[disputed /
suggested] the possibility that nearly one in every
four English soccer stadiums could be partially or
completely flooded in the near future due to
climate change and extreme weather events. Some
research even predicted that by 2050 almost half of
the cities that once hosted the Winter Olympics
would not be able to do so again for lack of snow
and ice. Also, the US Open Tennis Championships
organizers implemented an “extreme heat policy,”
having (C)[optional / mandatory] short breaks for
players to cool down during matches, after a few
quit their matches due to extreme heat. As more
sports are affected by climate change, concerns are
growing.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)              (C)
choices: overflowing   suggested      mandatory
overflowing   disputed optional
vacant   disputed mandatory
overflowing   suggested optional
vacant   suggested mandatory
solution: (A) 대회 기간 동안 관중과 선수들이 먹고 마시기 때문에 플라 스틱병과 포장지 같은 쓰레기가 대량으로 발생한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 쓰레기통이 overflowing (넘치는)이 적절하다. (B) 앞에서 위기감이 고조되었다고 했으므로 잉글랜드 축구 경 기장의 약 4곳 중 1곳이 기후 변화로 침수될 가능성이 있다는 연구가 제시되었다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 suggested(제 시했다)가 적절하다. (C) 뒤에서 선수들이 극심한 더위를 이기지 못해 경기를 포기 하는 심각한 상황이 발생했다고 했으므로 선수의 건강과 안전 을 보호하기 위한 폭염 대책으로서, 경기 중 선수들이 몸을 식 히는 것이 의무적이라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 mandatory (의무적인)가 적절하다.

There is light at the end of the tunnel, however.
The sports community is optimistic that it can
reduce its environmental impact by taking two main
steps: transitioning to more sustainable operations
before, during, and after events and raising
awareness among the public about their impact.
Efforts to adopt more responsible approaches have
been made by various organizations, and the
International Olympic Committee (IOC) is leading
the way by setting a good example. The IOC set
up the Sport and Environment Commission decades
ago and declared the environment as essential to
the Olympic Movement, in addition to sports and
culture. It has since encouraged host nations to
adopt more environmental approaches to putting
on the Olympics.
As a result, the Olympic Village built for the 2000
Sydney Summer Olympics ⓐbecoming the world’s
largest solar-powered suburb and the 2002 Salt
Lake City Winter Olympics adopted a new energy
recycling system ⓑwhich used the curling hall’s air
conditioning unit to heat the showers and bathrooms in the venue.
Also, for the 2010
Vancouver Winter Olympics, the Olympic speed-skating
venue was built with ⓒsalvaged timber. The Olympic
Park for the 2012 London Summer Olympics,
ⓓwhat was built on industrial land that was once
contaminated, was converted to the biggest urban
park in Europe. Then at the 2020 Tokyo Summer
Olympics, electricity was ⓔgenerated with hydrogen
instead of fossil fuel, which supplied power for
many residential buildings in the Olympic Village
and Paralympic Village.

choices: the environmental problems caused by internationalsporting events
the role of the IOC in organizing successfulOlympic Games
the development of renewable energy technologiesfor sports facilities
the economic benefits of adopting eco-friendlyapproaches in sports
green efforts to reduce environmental impactsthrough sustainable practices
solution: 첫 번째 단락에서 스포츠 공동체가 ‘지속 가능한 운영으로의 전환’과 ‘대중의 환경 인식 높이기’를 중요하게 보며, 이를 통 해 환경에 가는 영향을 줄여가려 하고 있음을 언급하며, 두 번 째 단락에서는 국제올림픽위원회(IOC)의 선도적 역할과 함께 역대 올림픽에서 환경 영향을 줄이기 위해 실천해 온 지속 가 능한 운영 방식과 다양한 친환경 사례를 설명하고 있으므로, 이 글의 주제로 ❺ ‘지속 가능한 실천을 통해 환경 영향을 줄 이기 위한 친환경적인 노력’이 가장 적절하다. 비상(홍민표) 2과

Thanks to its popularity, sports is a powerful tool
for universally raising awareness about
environmental responsibility. Simply put, the sports
industry influences billions of individuals that are
(A)involved in sports either as spectators, athletes,
or organizers. Through sports, strategies to increase
awareness and educate the public about the
importance of sustaining the environment (B)have
shown good results. Research has found (C)that fans
are ⓐreceptive to ecological or environmental
ⓑinitiatives organized at sporting events, and many
are willing to change their lifestyle habits accordingly.
The social status of athletes can have a strong
effect, too. For example, high-profile athletes and
coaches can be sports ⓒambassadors to foster
environmental consciousness among fans, especially
young people who look up to them. The broad
appeal of sports becomes a vehicle to reach many
people at once.
While sports provide us with such immense
benefits, we ─along with sporting event organizers
─need to be aware of the ⓓadverse environmental
effects (D)that sports have at times. As long as we
are all aware of the effects, we can take steps
toward finding ways to minimize or even completely
(E)eliminating them. While Green Sports Day, on
October 6th, is a global event that ⓔpromotes
environmentally friendly sports, maybe it’s time we
declare every day a day to encourage greater
sustainability in sports.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞은 것을모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

<보기>
ⓐ receptive: willing to consider new ideas or listen
to someone else’s opinions
ⓑ initiative: a new plan or process to achieve
something or solve a problem
ⓒ ambassador: an important official who works in a
foreign country representing his or
her own country there
ⓓ adverse: not good or favourable
ⓔ promote: to raise someone to a higher or more
important position or rank

On April 20, 2010, an enormous explosion shook
the Deepwater Horizon drilling platform in the Gulf
of Mexico, causing a significant oil leak into the
sea. Over a three-month period, approximately 134
million gallons of oil, comparable to more than 200
Olympic swimming pools, flowed into the sea
before it was eventually halted. Despite continuing
restoration efforts, the sea has not yet fully
recovered.
One approach to addressing the issue of oil
contamination is bioremediation, a restoration method that utilizes bacteria. Some types of
bacteria naturally exist in marine environments and
__________________________________________________________.
When an oil spill occurs, these bacteria are
attracted to the oil and begin to multiply. As they
grow, they release enzymes that break down oil
into carbon dioxide and water. Although this
process may take several weeks or months, it
represents a more sustainable method of cleaning
up oil spills compared to conventional approaches
involving harmful chemicals.
Bacteria can also play a role in the process of
plastic decomposition. When plastic enters the
ocean, some bacteria are attracted to it, leading to
their growth and reproduction. Similar to the
process of breaking down oil, the bacteria release
enzymes that break down plastic into smaller
molecules, ultimately resulting in carbon dioxide and
water.

are able to degrade diverse components of oil
prevent marine animals from growing in the sea
survive only by consuming plastics instead of oil
produce harmful substances while breaking downoil

body:
Many sporting events have a negative impact on
the environment because (A)_________________________
____________________________. To draw more spectators,
sports stadiums and sporting facilities are getting
bigger, consuming larger areas of land and
requiring greater amounts of building materials for
construction. Whenever a hectare of grassland is
cleared for a construction site, there is a loss of
nature. Every ton of concrete and steel used in the
building foundation and structure is produced,
transported, poured, and put together by equipment
and facilities that emit waste into the ground and
atmosphere. Then, after the stadium is completed,
large amounts of water, electricity, and other forms
of resources are consumed to operate and
ⓐ[maintain / maintained] the facility.
Every sporting event affects the environment
before, during, and even after it. For example, a
long-track speed skating competition can only take
place, provided that the ice of a 400-meter oval
track is frozen until it is 3 to 5 cm thick. As long
as the competition is on, the track needs to be
kept frozen by specialized refrigeration systems
while the temperature, humidity, and air quality
inside the stadium also have to be maintained for
optimal ice conditions. Additionally, all of the
stadium employees, athletes, and spectators need to
travel to and from the stadium, often from other
cities or even from abroad. In fact, more than 25%
of the emissions generated by the 2018
PyeongChang Winter Olympics are estimated to be
caused by fan travel and accommodations. During
the event, spectators and athletes eat and drink,
and the plastic bottles and wrappers of ⓑ[whatever
/ no matter what] they consumed leave trash cans
overflowing. After the event has ended, in addition
to the significant amount of trash that needs to be
disposed of, the effects ⓒ[that / what] those
people caused and the emissions generated from
their travel continue to have a lasting negative
impact on air quality.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

ⓐ
ⓑ
ⓒ
choices: maintainwhateverwhat
maintainedno matter whatthat
maintainedwhateverthat
maintainwhateverthat
maintainno matter whatwhat
solution: ⓐ ‘~하기 위해’의 의미를 갖는 ‘목적’의 부사적 용법으로 쓰인 to부정사 to operate와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어 목적 어 the facility를 공유해야 하므로 to를 생략한 동사원형 maintain이 적절하다. ⓑ 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(they consumed)을 이끌어 전치 사 of의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 을 이루는 복합관계대명사 whatever가 적절하다. 참고로 no matter what은 불완전한 절을 이끌어 양보 부사절 을 이루기 때문에 of의 목적어 자리에 올 수 없다. ⓒ 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(those people caused)을 이끌어 선행사 the effects를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 목 적격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.

It’s not all good news, however. There are challenges associated with bioremediation. The breakdown of oil or plastic by bacteria, as mentioned earlier, can be a time-consuming process that (A)[requires / requiring] weeks or months. These bacteria can also be sensitive to specific environmental conditions such as temperature and sea water constituents. Despite these challenges, there (B)[is / are] no doubt that bioremediation holds promise as a technology for oil spill or plastic cleanup in the ocean. Because the bacteria used in this process occur naturally, they do not need to be transported to the polluted site. Bioremediation may be a more effective way to confront contamination problems and (C)[reduce / reducing] environmental harm.
choices: requires – are – reduce
requiring – is – reducing
requires – is – reducing
requires – is – reduce
requiring – are – reduce
solution:
1. (A) 선행사 a time-consuming process를 수식하는 관계사절(that ~)의 동사 자리이고 선행사가 단수이므로 requires가 알맞다.
2. (B) 유도부사 there 구문에서 주어 doubt가 단수이므로 is가 알맞다.
3. (C) to confront와 and로 병렬 연결된 to부정사의 동사원형 자리이므로 reduce가 알맞다.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

Thanks to its popularity, sports is a powerful tool for universally raising awareness about environmental responsibility. Simply put, the sports industry influences billions of individuals that are involved in sports either as spectators, athletes, or organizers. Through sports, strategies to increase awareness and educate the public about the importance of sustaining the environment have shown good results. Research has found that fans are receptive to ecological or environmental initiatives organized at sporting events, and many are willing to change their lifestyle habits accordingly. The social status of athletes can have a strong effect, too. For example, high-profile athletes and coaches can be sports ambassadors to foster environmental consciousness among fans, especially young people who look up to them. The broad appeal of sports becomes a vehicle to reach many people at once.

[요약문] The (A)____________________ popularity and influential figures of the sports industry serve as a way to spread environmental awareness and (B)____________________ eco-friendly lifestyle changes among the public.
choices: extensive – discourage
limited – foster
extensive – promote
limited – promote
widespread – discourage
solution:
1. 스포츠는 인기가 높아 수십억 명에게 영향을 미치고(광범위한 인기), 유명 선수·코치가 팬의 환경 의식을 높인다고 했다.
2. 팬들은 환경 캠페인을 잘 받아들이고 생활 습관을 바꿀 의향이 있다고 했으므로 스포츠는 친환경적 생활 변화를 ‘촉진’한다.
3. (A)에는 extensive(광범위한), (B)에는 promote(촉진하다)가 알맞다. limited는 인기가 ‘제한적’이라는 뜻이라 틀리고, discourage는 반대 방향이다.
따라서 답은 ③이다.

W: Hi, today I’m excited to introduce a place I
recently visited during my summer vacation: the
Aral Sea.
(A) The Aral Sea serves as an example of how human
actions can have destructive environmental impacts.
I’m worried that other parts of the world may
also suffer from this kind of ecological collapse.
(B) Sadly, however, as of 2007, it had substantially
declined to 10% of its original size due to the
construction of dams and canals for cotton
farming. The decline not only damaged local
water resources but also induced changes in the
local climate, resulting in extended summers and
dry days.
(C) It is located in Central Asia, between Uzbekistan
and Kazakhstan. The Aral Sea, meaning “sea of
islands” in Kazakh, is not a sea but a saltwater
lake that was once the world’s fourth-largest lake.
We should be mindful of the impact of our choices.

위 주어진 담화에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 여자가 최근 여름방학 동안 방문한 아랄해를 소개하게 되어 기쁘다고 말하는 주어진 담화 뒤에, 아랄해의 위치와 명칭의 의미, 그리고 과거 세계에서 네 번째로 큰 염수호였다는 기본 적인 배경 정보를 설명하는 (C), Sadly, however(그러나 안타깝 게도)를 통해 과거와 현재를 대비하며, 댐과 운하 건설로 인해 호수의 면적이 원래의 10% 수준으로 줄어들었고 그 결과 지 역의 기후까지 변화했다는 내용을 설명하는 (B), 아랄해의 사 례가 인간의 행동이 환경에 파괴적인 영향을 미칠 수 있음을 보여 주는 대표적인 예임을 언급하고, 이러한 생태계 붕괴가 다른 지역에서도 발생할 수 있다는 화자의 우려를 나타내는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

On April 20, 2010, an enormous explosion shook
the Deepwater Horizon drilling platform in the Gulf
of Mexico, causing a significant oil leak into the
sea. Over a three-month period, approximately 134
million gallons of oil, comparable to more than 200
Olympic swimming pools, (A)[flowed / flowing] into
the sea before it was eventually halted. Despite
continuing restoration efforts, the sea has not yet
fully recovered.
One approach to addressing the issue of oil
contamination is bioremediation, a restoration method that utilizes bacteria. Some types of
bacteria naturally exist in marine environments and
possess the capability to break down various
components of oil. When an oil spill occurs, these
bacteria are attracted to the oil and begin to
multiply. As they grow, they release enzymes
(B)[what / that] break down oil into carbon dioxide
and water. Although this process may take several
weeks or months, it represents a more sustainable
method of cleaning up oil spills compared to
conventional approaches involving harmful chemicals.
Bacteria can also play a role in the process of
plastic decomposition. When plastic enters the
ocean, some bacteria are attracted to it, leading to
their growth and reproduction. Similar to the
process of breaking down oil, the bacteria release
enzymes that break down plastic into smaller
molecules, ultimately (C)[result / resulting] in carbon
dioxide and water.

used in buildings today.

Stewardship of the environment has become an
issue that affects almost all aspects of our lives.
Consequently, individuals and organizations constantly
strive to make small changes to their daily habits to
build a greener environment. Individuals practice a
more ⓐmindful approach to their way of living to
reduce their environmental impact while organizations
strive to modify their way of doing business to
minimize their effect on the environment. The world
of sports is no ⓑexception and it has a lot of
potential (A)[to be / being] part of the solution.
Many sporting events have a ⓒnegative impact on
the environment because they require massive
structures to host them. To draw more spectators,
sports stadiums and sporting facilities are getting
bigger, ⓓconserving larger areas of land and
requiring greater amounts of building materials for
construction. (B)[Whatever / Whenever] a hectare of
grassland is cleared for a construction site, there is
a loss of nature. Every ton of concrete and steel
used in the building foundation and structure (C)[is
/ to be] produced, transported, poured, and put
together by equipment and facilities that ⓔemit
waste into the ground and atmosphere. Then, after
the stadium is completed, large amounts of water,
electricity, and other forms of resources are
consumed to operate and maintain the facility.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(B)
(C)
choices: to beWheneveris
to beWheneverto be
beingWhateveris
to beWhateverto be
beingWheneveris
solution: (A) 명사구 a lot of potential을 수식하는 자리로, potential은 to부정사의 수식을 받는 명사이며, '~할 …이 있다‘의 의미로 ’have+명사(구)+to부정사‘의 구조가 쓰이므로, 형용사적 용법의 to부정사 to be가 적절하다. (B) 뒤에 완전한 절(a hectare ~ site)을 이끌어, 뒤에 또 다른 절(there ~ nature)을 이끄는 접속사 역할을 하므로, ‘~할 때 마다’의 의미를 갖는 복합 관계부사 Whenever이 알맞다. (C) 과거분사구(used ~ structure)의 수식을 받는 명사구 Every ton of concrete and steel이 주어이며, 문장의 동사가 없으므 로, 동사 자리이다. 주어의 핵심어는 Every ton이므로 단수로 수일치한 is가 알맞다. 비상(홍민표) 2과

On April 20, 2010, an enormous explosion shook
the Deepwater Horizon drilling platform in the Gulf
of Mexico, ⓐcausing a significant oil leak into the
sea. Over a three-month period, approximately 134
million gallons of oil, comparable to more than 200
Olympic swimming pools, ⓑflowed into the sea
before it was eventually halted. Despite continuing
restoration efforts, the sea has not yet fully recovered.
One approach to ⓒaddressing the issue of oil
contamination is bioremediation, a restoration
method ⓓwhat utilizes bacteria. Some types of
bacteria naturally exist in marine environments and
possess the capability to break down various
components of oil. When an oil spill occurs, these
bacteria are attracted to the oil and begin to
multiply. As they grow, they release enzymes that
ⓔbreak down oil into carbon dioxide and water.
Although this process may take several weeks or
months, it represents a more sustainable method of
cleaning up oil spills ⓕcompared to conventional
approaches involving harmful chemicals.
Bacteria can also play a role in the process of
plastic decomposition. When plastic enters the ocean,
some bacteria are attracted to it, ⓖlead to their
growth and reproduction. Similar to the process of
breaking down oil, the bacteria release enzymes
that break down plastic into smaller molecules,
ultimately ⓗresulting in carbon dioxide and water.

nations to adopt more environmental approaches to
putting on the Olympics.

from cells we keep alive in a controlled
environment. It is different from conventional
beef or chicken, which is produced by raising
and slaughtering farm animals. It’s also different from plant-based meat, which
derives its protein solely from plants. It is
often called cultured or cultivated meat, too.

the world’s farming land and produces 60%
of agricultural greenhouse gas emissions.
Since lab-grown meat doesn’t require killing
animals, it reduces carbon emissions, and it
retains the same nutrition and flavor as regular
meat. This makes it an attractive substitute.

research team. Our team is working to ⓑtrace
the process of cell division and growth in

cultivation environment that enables the creation
of a better texture (C)while burning less energy.

from plant-based meat, (D)which derives its

cultured or cultivated meat, too.

uses 83% of the world’s farming land and ⓓ

emissions, and it retains the same nutrition

attractive ⓔsubstitute.

As our planet faces increasing environmental
challenges and climate change, there is growing
interest in eco-friendly foods that have less impact
on the environment. The following foods eaten in
various regions of the world are gaining attention
as sustainable foods for the future.
False Bananas
ⓐ에티오피아는 그것의 커피 재배로 유명한데, 유망한
미래 작물인 엔셋(enset)이 번성하는 지역이기도 하다.
Enset, also known as “false banana,” is a close
relative of the banana. The fruit of the plant isn’t
safe to eat, but the stems and roots can be
processed and used to make bread. Approximately
20 million people (A)[rely on / do without] this
plant for food in Ethiopia, but it is almost unknown
outside of the country. Scientists anticipate that this
crop has the potential to feed more than 100
million people in a warming world, establishing
itself as a new fundamental food for the future.
Cacti
Native to the deserts of both North and South
America, cacti are a fundamental food in Latin
American communities, where the flat pads are
often stirred and served with eggs or in salads and
tacos. There are over 1,500 species of cacti, and
many of them are safe to eat. Cacti are rich in
fiber, vitamins, and other nutrients. Cacti’s ability to
thrive in dry and harsh environments makes them a
(B)[crucial / dispensable] crop in the face of climate
change.
Seaweed
Seaweed is a type of plant that typically flourishes
along rocky coasts around the world. This plant
offers a range of flavors that are used in a variety
of dishes, including soups, salads, and snacks.
Seaweed is mostly eaten in Korea, Japan, and
China, but it is becoming more common in other
parts of the world. Seaweed, gaining attention for
(C)[aggravating / addressing] soil degradation, is
packed with fiber, essential vitamins, and minerals,
offering numerous health benefits.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: rely oncrucialaggravating
rely oncrucialaddressing
rely ondispensableaddressing
do withoutcrucialaddressing
do withoutdispensableaggravating
solution: (A) 미래의 주요 식량으로 자리 잡아 1억 명 이상을 먹여 살릴 잠재력이 있는 엔셋은 빵을 만드는 데 사용되므로, 에티오피아 에서는 약 2천만 명의 사람들이 식량을 이 작물에 ‘의존한다 (rely on)’는 흐름이 적절하다. (B) 북미와 남미 사막 지역이 원산지인 선인장은 라틴아메리카의 주요 식량이며, 건조하고 혹독한 환경에서 잘 자라 기후 변화에 ‘중 요한’ 작물이라는 흐름이 알맞으므로, crucial(중요한)이 적절하다. (C) 전 세계의 바위 암석 해안을 따라 주로 번성하는 식물로, 식이 섬유, 필수 비타민 및 미네랄이 풍부해 많은 건강상 이점을 제공하 는 해조류가 주목받는 또 다른 이유로 토양 황폐화 문제를 ‘해결하 는 것(addressing)’을 위해 주목받는다는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

Seaweed
Seaweed is a type of plant that typically flourishes
along rocky coasts around the world. This plant
offers a range of flavors that are used in a variety of
dishes, including soups, salads, and snacks. Seaweed
is mostly eaten in Korea, Japan, and China, but it is
becoming more common in other parts of the world.
Seaweed, gaining attention for addressing soil
degradation, is packed with fiber, essential vitamins,
and minerals, offering numerous health benefits.
Insects
Insects have been a traditional source of protein in
many cultures for centuries. (A) People have been
enjoying seasoned, roasted insects for a long time
in Mexico, and many African countries incorporate
insects into soups. (B) Insects are high in protein,
vitamins, and minerals. (C) In contrast to other
protein sources, they also require significantly less
land, water, and food to produce, which diminishes
the environmental footprint of our diets. (D) These
merits make insects a magnificent alternative,
sustainable source of protein. (E)

challenges and climate change, there is growing
interest in eco-friendly foods that have less impact

various regions of the world are gaining attention
as sustainable foods for the future.
False Bananas
Ethiopia, noted for its coffee cultivation, is also a
region where the promising future crop enset
prevails. Enset, also known as “false banana,” is a
close relative of the banana. The fruit of the plant
isn’t safe to eat, but the stems and roots can be
processed and used to make bread. Approximately
20 million people rely on this plant for food in
Ethiopia, but it is almost unknown outside of the
country. Scientists anticipate that this crop has the
potential to feed more than 100 million people in a
warming world, establishing itself as a new
fundamental food for the future.

Host: Welcome to News Tonight. What was once
the stuff of science fiction is finally arriving
on our dinner plates. We’re talking about
lab-grown meat. You may be reluctant to try
it. However strange it may seem, many
people say it tastes just like regular meat,
and it has big advantages for preventing
animal suffering and reducing pollution.
Today, we have tissue engineering expert Dr.
Mike Perry with us to learn more about
lab-grown meat. It’s an honor to meet you,
Dr. Perry. Can you tell our viewers what kind
of research you are currently conducting?
Dr. Perry: Thank you for having me, Kelly. I am
currently leading a lab-grown meat project
research team. Our team is working to trace
the process of cell division and growth in
lab-grown meat, with the goal of discovering
a cultivation environment that enables the
creation of a better texture while burning
less energy.
Host: I see. Now let’s dive into our main topic,
lab-grown meat. First, tell us what lab-grown
meat is.
Dr. Perry: Lab-grown meat refers to meat grown
from cells we keep alive in a controlled
environment. It is different from conventional
beef or chicken, which is produced by raising
and slaughtering farm animals. It’s also different from plant-based meat, which
derives its protein solely from plants. It is
often called cultured or cultivated meat, too.
Host: I’m sure many people are wondering about
the reasons for developing lab-grown meat.
Dr. Perry: Every year, 80 billion animals are
slaughtered for meat. The livestock industry
uses 83% of the world’s farming land and
produces 60% of agricultural greenhouse gas
emissions. Since lab-grown meat doesn’t
require killing animals, it reduces carbon
emissions, and it retains the same nutrition
and flavor as regular meat. This makes it an
attractive substitute.

Many people claim that lab-grown meat closelyresembles conventional meat while helping curbanimal suffering and pollution.
Dr. Mike Perry’s team is investigating how cellsdivide and grow in lab-grown meat.
Lab-grown meat is distinct from plant-basedmeat made solely from plants.
Lab-grown meat serves as an appealing substitutefor conventional meat that differs in terms ofnutrition and taste.

products, we will need to collect more data over
a long period of time to ensure its safety.

Host: I think it really could be an attractive
alternative to the current options. How is
lab-grown meat made?
Dr. Perry: The process of making lab-grown meat
begins with the extraction of cells from a
living animal’s muscle or skin tissue. We then
determine which cells can be multiplied to
form delicious meat products. From there, we
place the cells in a culture medium. This is a
clean and controlled environment that offers
the necessary nutrients for cells to replicate
and mature by themselves. When the meat is
ready, it is harvested and processed like a
regular meat product.

Dr. Perry: Yes, indeed. Most of the original taste
tests ____________________________________________.

difference between lab-grown and regular
meat. Some of them even guessed incorrectly
which sample was lab-grown.

when we already have plant-based meat?

Cacti
Native to the deserts of both North and South
America, cacti are a fundamental food in Latin
American communities, where the flat pads are
often stirred and served with eggs or in salads and
tacos. There are over 1,500 species of cacti, and
many of them are (A)[safe / harmful] to eat. Cacti
are rich in fiber, vitamins, and other nutrients.
Cacti’s ability to thrive in dry and harsh
environments makes them a crucial crop in the face
of climate change.
Seaweed
Seaweed is a type of plant that typically flourishes
along rocky coasts around the world. This plant
offers a range of flavors that are used in a variety
of dishes, including soups, salads, and snacks.
Seaweed is mostly eaten in Korea, Japan, and
China, but it is becoming more common in other
parts of the world. Seaweed, (B)[lacking / gaining]
attention for addressing soil degradation, is packed
with fiber, essential vitamins, and minerals, offering
numerous health benefits.
Insects
Insects have been a traditional source of protein in
many cultures for centuries. People have been
enjoying seasoned, roasted insects for a long time
in Mexico, and many African countries incorporate
insects into soups. Also, insects are a popular street
food in some Asian countries. Insects are high in
protein, vitamins, and minerals. In contrast to other
protein sources, they also require significantly
(C)[more / less] land, water, and food to produce,
which diminishes the environmental footprint of our
diets. These merits make insects a magnificent
alternative, sustainable source of protein.

(B)
(C)

safegainingless
safegainingmore
