Another characteristic of universal design is
ⓐrequiring low physical effort. Universal design seeks
to create products ⓑwhat can be used efficiently and
comfortably without causing unnecessary fatigue.
Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble trying to
open a lid of a jar that was stuck. ⓒOpening a lid can
be a great challenge to people with a weak grip, the
elderly, or people with hand or finger impairments.
Fortunately, various clever opening devices have been
designed. A lever-type door handle, ⓓthat requires no
firm grip or twisting, is also an example that reflects this
characteristic of universal design. A door with a
lever-type door handle can be opened using an elbow or
a closed hand, which ⓔbenefits people carrying baskets
as well as those with limited strength in their hands.

윗글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?

(A) Universal design completely eliminates the need
for any physical effort when opening products
like jars or doors. (T/F)
(B) People with weak grip strength or hand-related
difficulties may struggle to open a tightly
closed jar. (T/F)
(C) Products with universal design are unnecessary
for general users. (T/F)
(D) A lever-type door handle can be operated without
requiring users to firmly hold or twist it. (T/F)
(E) People carrying baskets may find a lever-type
door handle useful because they can open the
door with an elbow or a closed hand. (T/F)

body:
Universal design is not limited to the design of physical products or facilities. Universal design pushes for designs in which critical information is conveyed well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the user’s sensory abilities. Information should be conveyed not just through written language but also through universal symbols and audio cues. For instance, when it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier when they can simply look for the universally recognized restroom symbol rather than trying to interpret the local language. For those with visual or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival times are not only presented on electronic boards but also called out through voice announcements. In elevators, braille, which indicates the floor number, allows individuals with visual impairments to select their desired floor. As such, providing information in these diverse forms ensures that everyone can access and understand important information, regardless of language barriers, sensory impairments, etc.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Necessity of a Common Language for Efficient Information Delivery
Why Foreign Travelers Need Visual Symbols and Braille in Modern Elevators
Universal Design for Accessible Information Across Languages and Sensory Abilities
How the Advancement of Technology Makes Information Access More Convenient
The Role of Electronic Boards and Voice Announcements in Public Transportation

body:
Play is a fundamental aspect of human
development that continues all through our lives.
Playgrounds serve as a central place for play, but
many individuals struggle to fully engage in these
spaces due to their restrictive arrangements. Often,
playgrounds are designed to satisfy specific types of
play or particular age groups, which can leave
children who cannot participate in the intended
manner ⓐfeeling excluded.
For children with disabilities, play is even more
crucial as it offers an opportunity to practice social
skills. However, the conventional design of
playgrounds does not typically accommodate their
needs, either ⓑoverwhelm or boring them. A visit
to a standard playground with children with
disabilities can highlight the weaknesses in design
ⓒthat fail to satisfy everyone.
Playgrounds should be designed to foster social
connections for all ages, provide sensory stimulation,
encourage physical exercise, and ⓓconnect with
nature. Achieving this integration is a challenging
design task. By involving children with disabilities
and their families in the design process and
creating friendlier playgrounds, we can acknowledge
ⓔthat play is more than just
a source
of
enjoyment. This approach results in spaces where
people of all abilities, ages, and languages can take
part in the joy of play.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

For example, Martin’s Park, designed by Michael
Van Valkenburgh Associates, is a universally designed
playground. Unusual play structures and a large
ship provide (A)[endless / finite] experiences of play
that can engage every child. The various methods
of play have different means of access, allowing
kids who are able to scramble up hills, while
children who can’t walk can use the sloping paths
to reach the top. Interpretive signs point out the
(B)[exclusive / inclusive] routes and elements of the
playground. The inclusion of more than 1,000 trees
grants children and adults the chance to experience
the sensory aspects of plants.
Play isn’t just for kids anymore. (C)[Kid / Senior]
play spaces and public exercise equipment are
being installed around the world. Play spaces for
older adults provide health benefits and encourage
engagement with their families and community.
Hence, playgrounds need to be redesigned as
spaces where everyone can enjoy themselves.
(A)
(B)
(C)

endlessinclusive        Senior

Universal design also ensures that an environment
or product is accessible to everyone. Anyone should
be able to use a design regardless of who they are
and what they’re capable of, and no one should be
excluded. Curb cuts are a good example. Without
curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard
time navigating the city. Curb cuts eliminate barriers
not only for wheelchair users but also for people
moving heavy loads or riding bikes. Like curb cuts,
automatic doors in public buildings also allow all
people to enter without any major problems.
Another characteristic of universal design is
requiring low physical effort. Universal design seeks
to create products that can be used efficiently and
comfortably without (A)[cause / causing] unnecessary
fatigue. Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble
trying to open a lid of a jar that was stuck.

Universal design suggests that design be as
flexible as possible so that it can accommodate
diverse needs and a wide range of individual
preferences. This could involve providing a variety
of options for customization or adding adjustable
features to a product.
Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse,
and the desk pictured below. Do you notice how
they differ from the more common types of
scissors, mice, and desks? They are all designed for
left-handed people. Without them, about 10% of
the world’s population, who are left-handed, would
find these simple products difficult to use.
The height-adjustable desk is also a good example
of a universal design that accommodates a wide
range of individual preferences and abilities. If the
desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it
to the heights they want. If desired, the user can
work while standing. A wheelchair user is also able
to use the desk at a comfortable height.

Play is a fundamental aspect of human
development that continues all through our lives.
Playgrounds serve as a central place for play, but
many individuals struggle to fully engage in these
spaces due to their restrictive arrangements. Often,
playgrounds are designed to satisfy specific types of
play or particular age groups, which can leave
children who cannot participate in the intended
manner feeling excluded.
For children with disabilities, play is even more
crucial as it offers an opportunity to practice social
skills. However, the conventional design of
playgrounds does not typically accommodate their
needs, either overwhelming or boring them. A visit
to a standard playground with children with
disabilities can highlight the weaknesses in design
that fail to satisfy everyone.
Playgrounds should be designed to foster social
connections for all ages, provide sensory stimulation,
encourage physical exercise, and connect with
nature. Achieving this integration is a challenging
design task. By involving children with disabilities
and their families in the design process and
creating friendlier playgrounds, we can acknowledge
that play is more than just a source of enjoyment.
This approach results in spaces where people of all
abilities, ages, and languages can take part in the
joy of play.
choices: Playgrounds should be built not only for childrenbut also for adults.
Children with disabilities should be encouragedto play more to develop social skills.
Playgrounds need to be divided into separateareas tailored to specific age groups.
Families need to play an active role in helpingtheir children engage in playground activities.
Playgrounds must be redesigned to embracepeople with all physical capacities, generationsand languages.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

For example, Martin’s Park, designed by Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates, is a universally designed playground. Unusual play structures and a large ship provide endless experiences of play that can engage every child. The various methods of play have different means of access, allowing kids who are able to scramble up hills, while children who can’t walk can use the sloping paths to reach the top. Interpretive signs point out the inclusive routes and elements of the playground. The inclusion of more than 1,000 trees grants children and adults the chance to experience the sensory aspects of plants.
Play isn’t just for kids anymore. Senior play spaces and public exercise equipment are being installed around the world. Play spaces for older adults provide health benefits and encourage engagement with their families and community. Hence, playgrounds need to be redesigned as spaces where everyone can enjoy themselves.

[요약문] As a universally designed playground, Martin's Park offers (A)____________________ in its facilities, ensuring the successful (B)____________________ of diverse individuals across generations.

Universal design suggests that design (A)be as
ⓐflexible as possible so that it can ⓑaccommodate
diverse needs and a wide range of individual
preferences. This could involve providing a variety
of options for ⓒcustomization or adding adjustable
features to a product.
Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse,
and the desk (B)picturing below. Do you notice how
they differ from the more common types of scissors,
mice, and desks? They are all designed for
left-handed people. Without them, about 10% of the
world’s population, who are left-handed, (C)would
have found these simple products difficult to use.
The height-adjustable desk is also a good example
of a universal design that accommodates a wide
range of individual preferences and abilities. If the
desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it
to the heights they want. If desired, the user can
work while (D)standing. A wheelchair user is also
able to use the desk at a comfortable height.
Universal design also ensures (E)that an
environment or product is accessible to everyone.
Anyone should be able to use a design regardless
of who they are and what they’re capable of, and
no one should be ⓓexcluded. Curb cuts are a
good example. Without curb cuts, people in
wheelchairs would have a hard time ⓔnavigating
the city. Curb cuts eliminate barriers not only for
wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy
loads or (F)ride bikes. Like curb cuts, automatic
doors in public buildings also (G)allow all people to
enter without any major problems.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

Another characteristic of universal design is
requiring low physical effort. Universal design seeks
to create products that can be used efficiently and
comfortably without causing unnecessary fatigue.
Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble trying
to open a lid of a jar that was stuck. Opening a lid
can be a great challenge to people with a weak
grip, the elderly, or people with hand or finger
impairments. Fortunately, various clever opening
devices have been designed. A lever-type door
handle, which requires no firm grip or twisting, is
also an example that reflects this characteristic of
universal design. A door with a lever-type door
handle can be opened using an elbow or a closed
hand, which benefits people carrying baskets as well
as those with limited strength in their hands.

What do you think good design is? Some might
assert good design makes products easy to use,
while others might say ⓐwhat good design is
stylish or innovative. There are even some who
believe that good design should be as
environmentally friendly as possible. All of these are
important elements of design. However, there is a
new idea called “universal design.” This idea
suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty
looks and functions. Universal design takes into
account the diverse needs of different people and
includes features that make it possible for them
ⓑaccess and use products without any barriers.
Now let’s take a look at how universal design is
tackling the problem of limited access and
reshaping the design of products and services.
Universal design is not limited to the design of
physical products or facilities. Universal design
pushes for designs ⓒwhich critical information is
conveyed well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the user’s sensory abilities.
Information should be conveyed not just through
written language but also through universal symbols
and audio cues. For instance, when it comes to
foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier
when they can simply look for the universally
recognized restroom symbol rather than trying to
interpret the local language. For those with visual
or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival times
are not only presented on electronic boards but
also called out through voice announcements. In
elevators, braille, ⓓthat indicates the floor number,
allows individuals with visual impairments to select
their desired floor. Additionally, audio announcements
confirm the selected floor and tell passengers when
the elevator has reached their desired floor.
As such, providing information in these diverse
forms ⓔensure that everyone can access and
understand important information, regardless of
language barriers, sensory impairments, etc.
Universal design is beneficial to everyone. With
universal design, no one needs to put up with
unnecessary discomfort. The supporters of universal
design suggest that it should be part of every
design. Take a look around you. Is there anything
that needs improvement so that it can be
accessible to more people? If so, why not create a
design and bring joy to more people?

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 알맞게 고쳐 쓰지못한 것은?
choices: ⓐ: what → that
ⓑ: access and use → accessing and using
ⓒ: which → in which
ⓓ: that → which
ⓔ: ensure → ensures
solution: ⓑ access and use → to access and (to) use (동사 make, 가목 적어 it, 목적격보어 possible, 의미상 주어 for them과 함께 ‘-가 ~하는 것을 …하게 만들다’의 의미를 갖는 ‘make+it(가목적어)+목 적격보어(형용사)+for+의미상 주어+to부정사(진목적어)’의 구조로, ‘가목적어-진목적어’ 구문을 이루어야 한다. 따라서 진목적어 자리 이자 ‘for+목적어(them)‘의 형태로 의미상주어를 취하고 있으므로, access and use를 accessing and using이 아니라 to부정사구 to access and (to) use로 고친다. 참고로 to부정사가 병렬 연결될 때 to는 생략 가능하므로 to use 또는 use 모두 가능하다.)

body:
Play is a fundamental aspect of human
development that continues all through our lives.
Playgrounds serve as a central place for play, but
many individuals struggle to fully engage in these
spaces due to their restrictive arrangements. Often,
playgrounds are designed to satisfy specific types of
play or particular age groups, which can leave
children who (A)________________________________________
feeling excluded.
For children with disabilities, play is ⓐ[very / even]
more crucial as it offers an opportunity to practice
social skills. However, the conventional design of
playgrounds does not typically accommodate their
needs, either overwhelming or boring them. A visit
to a standard playground with children with
disabilities can highlight the weaknesses in design
that fail to satisfy everyone.
Playgrounds should be designed to foster social
connections for all ages, provide sensory stimulation,
encourage physical exercise, and connect with
nature. ⓑ[Achieve / Achieving] this integration is a
challenging design task. By involving children with
disabilities and their families in the design process
and creating friendlier playgrounds, we can
acknowledge that play is more than just a source
of enjoyment. This approach results in spaces
ⓒ[which / where] people of all abilities, ages, and
languages can take part in the joy of play.

choices: can easily satisfy their needs in conventional spaces
prefer quieter places to traditional playgrounds
are able to move around without restriction
have different interests from other children
cannot participate in the intended manner

Universal design suggests that design be as
flexible as possible so that it can accommodate
diverse needs and a wide range of individual
preferences. This could involve providing a variety
of options for customization or adding adjustable
features to a product.
Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse,
and the desk pictured below. Do you notice how
they differ from the more common types of
scissors, mice, and desks? They are all designed for
left-handed people. Without them, about 10% of
the world’s population, who are left-handed, would
find these simple products difficult to use.
The height-adjustable desk is also a good example
of a universal design that accommodates a wide
range of individual preferences and abilities. If the
desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it
to the heights they want. If desired, the user can
work while standing. A wheelchair user is also able
to use the desk at a comfortable height.

pushes for designs in which ⓑcritical information is

ⓓsymbols and audio cues. For instance, when it
comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is
much easier when they can simply look for the
universally recognized restroom symbol rather than
trying to interpret the local language. For those
with visual or audio ⓔimpairments, bus and subway

or product is accessible to everyone. Anyone should

Play is a fundamental aspect of human
development that continues all through our lives.
Playgrounds serve as a central place for play, but
many individuals struggle to fully engage in these
spaces due to their restrictive arrangements. Often,
playgrounds are designed to satisfy specific types of
play or particular age groups, which can leave
children who cannot participate in the intended
manner feeling (A)[included / excluded].
For children with disabilities, play is even more
crucial as it offers an opportunity to practice social
skills. However, the (B)[conventional / unconventional]
design of playgrounds does not typically accommodate
their needs, either overwhelming or boring them. A
visit to a standard playground with children with
disabilities can highlight the weaknesses in design
that fail to satisfy everyone.
Playgrounds should be designed to foster social
connections for all ages, provide sensory stimulation,
encourage physical exercise, and connect with
nature. Achieving this (C)[integration / division] is a
challenging design task. By involving children with
disabilities and their families in the design process
and creating friendlier playgrounds, we can
acknowledge that play is more than just a source
of enjoyment. This approach results in spaces where
people of all abilities, ages, and languages can take
part in the joy of play.
(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: included conventional  integration

design is stylish or innovative. There are even
some ⓔwho believe that good design should
be as environmentally friendly as possible.
Now let’s take a look at how universal design is
tackling the problem of limited access and
reshaping the design of products and services.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

Universal design is not limited to the design of
physical products or facilities. Universal design pushes
for designs in which critical information is conveyed
well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the
user’s sensory abilities. Information should be conveyed
not just through written language but also through
universal symbols and audio cues. For instance, when
it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is
much easier when they can simply look for the
universally recognized restroom symbol rather than
trying to interpret the local language. For those with
visual or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival
times are not only presented on electronic boards but
also called out through voice announcements. In
elevators, braille, which indicates the floor number,
allows individuals with visual impairments to select
their desired floor. Additionally, audio announcements
confirm the selected floor and tell passengers when
the elevator has reached their desired floor.
As such, providing information in these diverse forms
ensures that ______________________________________________.
Universal design is beneficial to everyone. With
universal design, no one needs to put up with
unnecessary discomfort. The supporters of universal
design suggest that it should be part of every
design. Take a look around you. Is there anything
that needs improvement so that it can be
accessible to more people? If so, why not create a
design and bring joy to more people?

people need different information depending ontheir language and abilities
all visual messages are automatically translatedinto audio cues
individuals with sensory impairments can safelyuse elevators
tourists can overcome language barriers in foreigncountries

Addario’s career took a significant turn when she
went to Afghanistan in 2000. Her photographs
captured the grief, resilience, and courage of
Afghan women.
(A) Time and again, however, she has risked her life
to capture images that speak volumes about the
suffering of those ⓐ[catching / caught] in the
conflicts between nations.
“The idea of me going to a war zone was out
of the question. ㉠그때 9.11 테러가 왔고, 이건
내가 취재해야 할 것만 같은 생각이 들었던 결정
적인 역사적 순간이었어요.
(B) This body of work gained international recognition,
ⓑ[served / serving] as a stepping stone for
Addario’s future achievements. Over the years,
Addario’s work has taken her to many regions
torn by war, including Iraq, Sudan, Libya, and
Syria. She knows very well what could happen in
the wars: she was captured twice and was even
threatened with her life.
(C) From there I ended up covering the war in Iraq
in 2003 because again, I felt like I needed to
be there. Young soldiers of my generation were
going in to fight, and I thought it was
important to document the war. I’m lucky
because I’ve survived. I’m now at the point in
my life and my career ⓒ[which / where] many
of my friends are not. And so I think it’s
important to realize there is a reason I’m still
here, and I have to keep pushing forward.”

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 주어진 글에서 Addario가 2000년 아프가니스탄에 가서 아프간 여성들의 사진을 찍었다고 했으므로, 그 작업(This body of work)이 국제적 인정을 받아 이후 여러 전쟁 지역으로 이어졌 고 두 번 붙잡히는 등 위험을 겪었다는 내용의 (B)가 먼저 이 어진다. (B)에서 전쟁에서 벌어질 수 있는 위험을 언급한 뒤, however로 그럼에도 목숨을 걸고 사진을 담아 왔다는 (A)가 이어지며, (A) 끝에서 9.11 테러가 결정적 순간이었다고 언급한 다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 From there(그곳에서부터)로 이어받아 2003년 이라크 전쟁을 취재하게 된 이야기와 계속 나아가야 한다는 다짐으로 마무리된다. 따라서 순서는 (B)-(A)-(C)이다.

I have found that nothing in life is of value (A)[if /
unless] you take risks. Nothing. Now I’m sure in
your experiences in school, in applying to college,
in picking your major, in deciding what you want to
do with life, people have told you to make sure
you have something to “fall back on.” But I never
understood that concept, having something to fall
back on. If I’m going to fall, I don’t want to fall
back on anything. I want to fall forward. This is
what I mean. Reggie Jackson struck out 2,600 times
in his career, the most in the history of baseball.
But you don’t hear about it. People remember the
home runs. Fall forward. Thomas Edison conducted
1,000 (B)[failed / successful] experiments because
the 1,001st was the light bulb. Fall forward. Every
failed experiment is one step closer to success.

about why that’s so important. You will fail at some

in picking your major, in deciding what you want to
do with life, people have told you to make sure
you have something to “fall back on.” But I never
understood that concept, having something to fall
back on. If I’m going to fall, I don’t want to fall
back on anything. I want to fall forward. This is
what I mean. Reggie Jackson struck out 2,600 times
in his career, the most in the history of baseball.
But you don’t hear about it. People remember the
home runs. Fall forward. Thomas Edison conducted
1,000 (B)[failed / successful] experiments because
the 1,001st was the light bulb. Fall forward. Every
failed experiment is one step closer to success.
You’ve got to take risks. I want to talk to you
about why that’s so important. You will fail at some
point in your lives. You will lose. You will embarrass
yourselves. There is no doubt about it. I know
that’s probably not a traditional message for a
graduation ceremony but I’m telling you. Embrace it
because it’s (C)[avoidable / inevitable].

choices: You should always prepare something to fall backon before taking risks.
Great achievements are the result of overcomingcountless trials.
Diverse experiences in one's youth are a preciousasset in life.
Wisdom is required to minimize the possibilityof failure in life.
You should use failure as a stepping stone tomove toward success.

body:
In the acting business, you fail all the time. Early
on in my career, I auditioned for a part in a
Broadway musical. A perfect role for me, I thought,
except for the fact that I can’t sing. So I’m in the
wings. I’m about to go on stage but the guy in
front of me, he’s singing like Pavarotti, and I’m just
getting smaller and smaller. I didn’t get the job. But
here’s the thing. I didn’t quit. I didn’t fall back. I
walked out of there to prepare for the next
audition and the one after that. I continued to fail
and fail, but it didn’t matter. There is an old saying:
if you hang around the barbershop long enough,
sooner or later you’re going to get a haircut. So
you will catch a break, which is exactly what I did.
Last year I did a play called Fences on Broadway. It
was at the Court Theater. It was at the same
theater that I failed that first audition 30 years
prior. The point is every graduate here today has
the training and the talent to succeed. But do you
have _____________________________?

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: an eye for talent
the courage to fail
a drive to compete
the ability to avoid failure
the confidence to succeed
solution: 화자는 브로드웨이 뮤지컬 오디션에서 떨어진 뒤에도 포기하 지 않고 계속 도전했고, 거듭된 실패 끝에 결국 기회를 잡았 다. 즉, 실패를 피하는 것이 아니라 실패하더라도 계속 나아가 는 태도가 중요하다는 내용이므로, 빈칸에는 ❷ ‘실패할 용기’ 가 가장 적절하다.

What can I help you with?

and I was wondering what kinds of questions I
might be asked in the interview.
W: Usually interviewers start by asking you to tell
them a little bit about yourself. Then they might
ask you what kinds of activities you did in high
school.

enjoyed reading books about biology.

interested in studying at the college.

you want to attend that college. You can search
the college’s website and see what courses are
offered.
B: Oh, that’s a good idea. I should probably do
that soon.

act confidently and always be polite.

how to prepare for the interview.

Lynsey Addario
“Where in the world would I rather be than on
the front line of history?”
Born in Connecticut, United States, in 1973, Lynsey
Addario developed an early passion for photography.
Her father gave her an old 35mm camera when she
was about 12 years old. She started reading books
on how to take photographs. (A)너무 수줍어서 사람
들에게 다가가지 못했기 때문에, 그녀는 꽃과 달의 사
진을 찍었다. Despite her love for taking pictures,
she never learned photography formally.
Her parents taught her to appreciate diverse cultures
and inquire about the world beyond her immediate
surroundings. She studied international relations and
Italian at college. After graduation, she moved to
Argentina to study Spanish, and it was there that
she started working as a news photographer.

captured the grief, resilience, and courage of
Afghan women. This body of work gained
international recognition, ⓐserved as a stepping
stone for Addario’s future achievements. Over the
years, Addario’s work has taken her to many
regions which ⓑwere torn by war, including Iraq,
Sudan, Libya, and Syria. She knows very well what
could happen in the wars: she was captured twice
and was even ⓒthreatened with her life. Time and

body:
Researcher and professor Carol Dweck uses the
term mindset to describe the way people think
about ability and talent. Dweck describes two
different mindsets. One is a fixed mindset, which
suggests that your abilities are inherent and
unchangeable. The other is a growth mindset, which
views them as something you can improve through
practice. There are several differences between these
two mindsets. First, in a fixed mindset, you view
failure as permanent, but with a growth mindset,
you see failure as a chance to learn. Second, those
with a fixed mindset are more likely to view
negative feedback as a personal attack, while those
with a growth mindset will see it as a chance to
improve. Lastly, those with a fixed mindset are likely
to give up when they face an obstacle. Meanwhile,
those with a growth mindset will view obstacles as
a chance to experiment and solve problems.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: how to overcome failure using a growth mindset

how fixed and growth mindsets shape responsesto challenges
the process of measuring a person's inborn abilityand talent
ways to teach children to develop a growth mindset

Addario’s career took a significant turn when she
went to Afghanistan in 2000. Her photographs
captured the grief, resilience, and courage of
Afghan women. (A)This body of work gained
international recognition, ㉠____________________________
________________. Over the years, Addario’s work has
taken her to many regions torn by war, including
Iraq, Sudan, Libya, and Syria. She knows very well
what could happen in the wars: she was captured
twice and was even threatened with her life. Time
and again, however, she has risked her life to
capture images that speak volumes about the
suffering of those caught in the conflicts between
nations.
“The idea of me (B)going to a war zone was
(C)out of the question. Then came 9/11, and it was
such a defining moment in history that I felt like I
needed to cover it. From there I ended up covering
the war in Iraq in 2003 because again, I felt like I
needed to be there. Young soldiers of my
generation (D)were going in to fight, and I thought
it was important to document the war. I’m lucky
because I’ve survived. I’m now at the point in my
life and my career (E)where many of my friends are
not. And so I think it’s important to realize there is
a reason I’m still here, and I have to keep pushing
forward.”

We often see individuals who manage to
accomplish seemingly impossible tasks. It almost
appears as if they (A)[lacked / possessed] the ability
to ignite their own spirits. They could be innovators
who achieve success after countless trials and
errors, athletes who push themselves tirelessly until
they go beyond their limits, or activists who are
willing to take risks to (B)[resist / pursue] what they
believe is right. They make us wonder: “What could
be the (C)[driving / restraining] force behind them?
What makes their lives meaningful to them and
even to us?” Let us meet two prominent individuals
and try to answer these questions.
(A)　　　  (B)　　　    (C)
choices: lacked resist   driving
lacked pursue   restraining
possessed resist   restraining
possessed pursue   driving
possessed resist   driving
solution: (A) 앞에서 이들이 ‘겉보기에 불가능해 보이는 일을 성취해 내 는 사람들’이라고 했으므로, 자기 영혼에 불을 붙이는 능력이 ‘부족했다’기보다 그러한 능력을 ‘지니고 있었다’는 흐름이 자 연스러워 possessed(지니고 있었다)가 알맞다. (B) 활동가들이 기꺼이 위험을 감수하는 것은 자신이 옳다고 믿는 바를 이루기 위해 계속 행동하는 모습이므로, resist(저항 하다)보다 pursue(추구하다)가 알맞다. (C) 혁신가는 수많은 시행착오 끝에 성공하고, 운동선수는 자 신의 한계를 넘어설 때까지 쉬지 않고 자신을 밀어붙이며, 활 동가는 위험을 감수하면서도 신념을 실천한다. 이처럼 세 사례 모두 행동을 멈추게 하는 것이 아니라 계속 앞으로 나아가게 하는 힘과 관련되므로, restraining(억제하는)보다 driving(추진 하는, 원동력이 되는)이 알맞다.

G: I’m planning to volunteer to make soap for
children in need. I heard that many children
suffer from diseases by not washing their hands
with soap.
B: That’s so sad. Proper hand washing should be
practiced by everyone. I want to volunteer to
make soap, too. Can I join you?
G: Why not? Let’s start this weekend. Why don’t we
meet at my house this Saturday?
B: Sure. What kind of soap do you want to make?
G: I want to make see-through soap. It’s a good
example of a nudge strategy, leading children to
regularly wash their hands.
B: See-through soap? Why was it made see-through?
G: There’s a toy inside it and you can see it.
B: Oh, that’s a clever idea. To get the toy inside,
children have to frequently wash their hands
with it.
G: Yes. That’s the point. According to a report, not
only did the soap help reduce diseases, but it
also helped children develop hand washing
habits.
B: See-through soap is more useful than I thought.
I hope more people use it.
G: I hope so, too.
choices: The girl plans to take part in a volunteeractivity that supports children in need.
The boy becomes interested in joining theactivity after hearing about the children’s healthproblems.
The soap contains a visible toy that motivateschildren to use it frequently.
A report showed that the soap improvedhygiene habits but had no effect on illness.
Both speakers hope that the special soap willbecome more widely used.

body:
You have probably received a notification from
your smartphone telling you that it is time to
exercise or move. These devices lead people to
move by sending notifications when they have been
inactive for a set amount of time. You may not
have realized it, but this is an example of a nudge.
A nudge is an intervention that gently guides
individuals toward a desired action, without
forbidding any options. For example, if a school
wants to reduce the amount of sugary drinks that
students consume, then making them less visible
than bottled water counts as a nudge, while
banning them altogether does not.
Having been studied in the domain of behavioral
economics and marketing, nudging can be applied
to inducing people to make better or ideal
decisions. Here are some ways nudges have
succeeded in bringing about positive changes by
tweaking people’s choices.

윗글의 내용과 (A)~(D)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?

(A) Smartphones send notifications to encourage
people to move after a period of inactivity.
(B) Banning sugary drinks altogether is given as
an example of a nudge.
(C) Nudging has mainly been examined in fields
unrelated to human decision-making.
(D) Nudges can produce beneficial changes by
slightly adjusting the way choices are presented.
choices: F-F-T-F
T-F-F-T
F-T-F-T
T-T-F-T
T-F-F-F
solution: 차례대로 T-F-F-T이다 (A) 스마트폰은 일정 시간 동안 활동이 없으면 사람들이 움직 이도록 유도하는 알림을 보낸다. (일치) (B) 설탕이 든 음료를 전면적으로 금지하는 것이(→생수보다 덜 눈에 띄게 배치하는 것이) 너지의 예로 제시된다. (불일치) (C) 너지는 주로 인간의 의사 결정과 관련이 없는 분야에서(→ 행동경제학과 마케팅 분야에서) 연구되어 왔다. (불일치) (D) 너지는 선택이 제시되는 방식을 조금 조정함으로써 긍정적 인 변화를 만들어 낼 수 있다. (일치)

body:
If you are told what other people do, ㉠여러분도
그들이 하는 것이 아마 좋은 생각일 것이라 여기기 때
문에 똑같이 하게 될 수 있다. And even if you aren’t
sure, you might not want to disobey social norms,
so you will go along. Highlighting the right
decisions of others can lead one ⓐto do the right
thing. While the sign saying “Take your trash home
or get a ＄100 fine.” pushes people, the one saying
“Take your trash home. Other people do.” ⓑnudges
them. Many people feel compelled to match their
behavior with that of the majority. The decision is
theirs, but they have been nudged.
(A) However, nudging people into making good
choices ⓒdo not always go as planned. (B) For
instance, in a study of household energy
conservation, the researchers provided the residents
with information about their neighbors’ average
energy use. (C) As expected, those who ⓓhad
consumed more energy than the average reduced
their use later; however, households with low levels
of energy consumption increased their use after
learning that their consumption had been lower
than their neighbors’. (D) Later, they added a smiley
face to the information ⓔsending to those who
used less energy than the average, and found that
it neutralized the opposite effect. (E)

Why People Always Follow the Behavior of theMajority

body:
A default is defined as an option that applies if
the chooser does ⓐnothing. Of course, the chooser
has the freedom to opt out of the default. Defaults
are effective at nudging people toward more
desirable behaviors. (A)인간은 그들이 이미 갖고 있는
것을 고수하려는 강력한 욕구의 영향을 받는데, 변화
하는 것은 의식적인 노력이 필요하기 때문이다.
Furthermore, because a default also gives the
impression that someone is ⓑrecommending this
choice, if people choose to opt out, they might feel
they are not being good citizens, particularly in the
case of green defaults.
(B)_____________________________________________________ can automatically nudge people into more
sustainable behaviors. In 2008, Rutgers University
instituted a new student printing policy to ⓒsave
on paper waste: it established printing on both
sides of paper as the default setting for all its
printers. As a result of that simple change, the
university saved about 62 million sheets of paper in
about three years.
Nudging through defaults can also apply to a
food delivery app. A company recently announced
an update for its app where it would change the
default settings for the optional items, such as
forks, spoons, and straws. Users would have to
ⓓopt out of the default to get them. The company
mentioned in an online post that having surveyed
many of its customers, they found that more than
90% of them didn’t really need disposable plastic
items with their orders.
Are you interested in changing certain people’s
behavior? Then why not nudge them in the right
direction? There are many ways to ⓔovertly
influence people to make better decisions. As we
are all choice architects every now and then, it pays
to know how to set people on the right path.

윗글의 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Providing information about environmental effects
Imposing fines for excessive resource use
Requiring conscious effort to opt out
Allowing consumers to freely choose
Setting greener choices as defaults
solution: 앞 문단에서 디폴트의 개념과 그것이 왜 효과적인지를 설명한 뒤, 빈칸 문장에서 이를 지속가능한 행동과 연결하고 뒤에 Rutgers 대학에서 양면 인쇄를 기본 설정하여 종이를 크게 절 약했고, 배달 앱에서 일회용품을 받지 않도록 기본 설정하여 일회용품의 사용을 감소한 사례가 이어지고 있으므로, 빈칸에 는 환경과 관련된 디폴트를 설정하는 것에 대한 내용이 들어 가야 한다. 따라서 ❺ ‘환경친화적 선택을 디폴트로 두는 것’이 알맞다. 천재(강상구) 2과

body:
Dark patterns are design elements or processes
that companies use to manipulate consumer
behavior. They come in a wide variety of forms.
Sometimes they are harmless, but sometimes they
are misleading. The following examples of dark
patterns will help you recognize and deal with them
properly in the future.
Forced Continuity
If you have signed up for a streaming service
recently, you have probably run into this dark
pattern where your credit card is automatically
charged as soon as a free trial comes to an end.
While the companies that do this would argue that
it enables users to continue to access their service
uninterrupted, users receive no warning that their
cards are about to be charged, often causing them
to be billed unexpectedly. This method is used by
many streaming platforms, but it is also common
with other services that offer free trials.
Artificial Scarcity
“Only two pieces available!” “Only four hours left
until the offer ends!” “Only ten slots left for this
program!” Artificial scarcity is used to (A)[stimulate /
prohibit] purchases. This typically comes in three
major forms: insufficient quantities, time, or
availability. We make decisions more quickly under
pressure. The decision is then often made quite
automatically only on the basis of scarcity. After all,
no one wants to miss out on a great offer.
Hidden Information
In this pattern, important information and options
are hidden or displayed in such a way that they are
hardly noticeable. To see the information, you have
to click somewhere, look very closely, or actively
search for it.
Every newsletter must allow you to unsubscribe.
But just because companies have to provide the
option, it doesn’t mean they have to make it easy
for you to see! So the “unsubscribe” link is made
almost (B)[visible / invisible] in the email. Gray print
on a dark background is rather hard to read, as is
very small print.
Dark patterns are everywhere. It is always
important to be aware that a company’s goals don’t
always (C)[different from / correspond with] your
own. To detect and resist dark patterns, you need
to read carefully and think before you click on a
button.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: stimulate – visible – different from
stimulate – invisible – correspond with
prohibit – invisible – correspond with
prohibit – visible – different from
stimulate – invisible – different from
solution:
1. (A) 수량·시간·이용 가능성을 제한해 압박 속에 빨리 결정하게 만든다는 내용이므로 인위적 희소성은 구매를 ‘자극하기(stimulate)’ 위해 쓰인다.
2. (B) 회색 글씨·아주 작은 글씨처럼 읽기 어렵게 만든다고 했으므로 구독 해지 링크는 거의 ‘보이지 않게(invisible)’ 만들어진다.
3. (C) 앞의 don’t always와 이어져 ‘기업의 목표가 항상 당신의 목표와 일치하지는 않는다’가 되어야 하므로 correspond with가 알맞다(different from은 동사가 아니어서 don’t 뒤에 올 수 없다).
따라서 답은 ②이다.

body:
Changes in visual designs can markedly affect
behaviors of people, especially on streets. Two artists,
mother and daughter, painted a 3D crosswalk on
several roads in Ahmedabad, India. To motorists,
the painted lines look like roadblocks, ⓐcausing
them to slow down without braking too suddenly.
The scheme was also adopted in Delhi, India. This,
in turn, inspired Ralf Trylla, an environmental
commissioner in Iceland, to head a similar project.
As a result, drivers ⓑwere being more careful at
intersections, which reduced accidents and elevated
the safety of pedestrians. The idea has been well
received and ⓒmirrored in cities of China, the U.S.,
Canada, and the UK as well.
Likewise, traffic engineers design pavement markings
on the roads that drive people ⓓto change their
behavior without realizing it. Chicago was one of
the first U.S. cities to experiment with this idea. In
2006, it painted a series of lines across the road
ahead of a dangerous curve on North Lake Shore
Drive. The lines are spaced in such a way that as
the road nears the curve, the gaps between the
lines get smaller and smaller. This gives drivers
approaching the curve an illusion ⓔwhich they are
speeding up, which prompts them to step on the
brakes. Chicago traffic engineers reported a 36%
reduction in crashes at the North Lake Shore Drive
curve in the first six months after painting the lines.
Since then, the Chicago Department of Transportation
has painted the gapped lines at similar curves.

윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: Who painted the 3D crosswalk in Ahmedabad, India?
What effect does the painted 3D crosswalk haveon motorists?
In which cities of China, the U.S., Canada, andthe UK has the idea been adopted?
When and where did Chicago start using thepavement markings designed by traffic engineers?
How do the pavement markings in Chicagoencourage drivers to change their behavior?

body:
Dark patterns are design elements or processes
that companies use to manipulate consumer
behavior. They come in a wide variety of forms.
Sometimes they are harmless, but sometimes they
are misleading. The following examples of dark
patterns will help you recognize and deal with them
properly in the future.
Forced Continuity
If you have signed up for a streaming service
recently, you have probably run into this dark pattern
where your credit card is automatically charged as
soon as a free trial comes to an end. While the
companies that do this would argue that it enables
users (A)[continuing / to continue] to access their
service uninterrupted, users receive no warning that
their cards are about to be charged, often causing
them to be billed unexpectedly. This method is
used by many streaming platforms, but it is also
common with other services that offer free trials.
Artificial Scarcity
“Only two pieces available!” “Only four hours left
until the offer ends!” “Only ten slots left for this
program!” Artificial scarcity is used to stimulate
purchases. This typically comes in three major
forms: insufficient quantities, time, or availability. We
make decisions more quickly under pressure. The
decision is then often made quite automatically only
on the basis of scarcity. After all, no one wants to
miss out on a great offer.
Hidden Information
In this pattern, important information and options
are hidden or displayed in such a way that they are
hardly noticeable. To see the information, you have
to click somewhere, look very closely, or actively
search for it.
Every newsletter must allow you to unsubscribe.
But just because companies have to provide the
option, it doesn’t mean they have to make it
(B)[easy / easily] for you to see! So the
“unsubscribe” link is made almost invisible in the
email. Gray print on a dark background is rather
hard to read, as (C)[is / are] very small print.
Dark patterns are everywhere. It is always
important to be aware that a company’s goals don’t
always correspond with your own. To detect and
resist dark patterns, you need to read carefully and
think before you click on a button.

(A)
(B)
(C)

to continueeasyis

body:
A default is defined as an option that applies if
the chooser does nothing. Of course, the chooser
has the freedom to opt out of the default. Defaults
are effective at nudging people toward more
desirable behaviors. Human beings are subject to a
powerful desire ㉠_____________________________________
because making a change requires a conscious
effort. Furthermore, because a default also gives the
impression that someone is recommending this
choice, if people choose to opt out, they might feel
they are not being good citizens, particularly in the
case of green defaults.
Setting greener choices as defaults can
automatically nudge people into more sustainable
behaviors. In 2008, Rutgers University instituted a
new student printing policy to save on paper waste:
it established printing on both sides of paper as
the default setting for all its printers. As a result of
that simple change, the university saved about 62
million sheets of paper in about three years.
Nudging through defaults can also apply to a
food delivery app. A company recently announced
an update for its app where it would change the
default settings for the optional items, such as
forks, spoons, and straws. Users would have to opt
out of the default to get them. The company
mentioned in an online post that ⓐhas surveyed
many of its customers, they found that more than
90% of them didn’t really need disposable plastic
items with their orders.
Are you interested in changing certain people’s
behavior? Then why not nudge them in the right
direction? There are many ways to subtly influence
people to make better decisions. As we are all
choice architects every now and then, ⓑit pays
knowing how to set people on the right path.

윗글의 빈칸 ㉠에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: to value one’s own opinion
to earn a reward for their choice
to stick with what they already have
to be reluctant to follow social norms
to distrust choices recommended by others

body:
Changes in visual designs can markedly affect
behaviors of people, especially on streets. Two
artists, mother and daughter, painted a 3D crosswalk
on several roads in Ahmedabad, India. To motorists,
the painted lines look like roadblocks, causing them
to slow down without braking too suddenly.
The scheme was also adopted in Delhi, India. This,
㉠______________, inspired Ralf Trylla, an environmental
commissioner in Iceland, to head a similar project.
As a result, drivers were being more careful at
intersections, which reduced accidents and elevated
the (A)[risk / safety] of pedestrians. The idea has
been well received and mirrored in cities of China,
the U.S., Canada, and the UK as well.
㉡______________, traffic engineers design pavement
markings on the roads that drive people to change
their behavior without realizing it. Chicago was one
of the first U.S. cities to experiment with this idea.
In 2006, it painted a series of lines across the road
ahead of a dangerous curve on North Lake Shore
Drive. The lines are spaced in such a way that as
the road nears the curve, the gaps between the
lines get smaller and smaller. This gives drivers
approaching the curve an illusion that they are
(B)[speeding up / slowing down], which prompts
them to step on the brakes. Chicago traffic
engineers reported a 36% (C)[surge / reduction] in
crashes at the North Lake Shore Drive curve in the
first six months after painting the lines. Since then,
the Chicago Department of Transportation has
painted the gapped lines at similar curves.

윗글의 빈칸 ㉠, ㉡에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

㉠
㉡
choices: in turnLikewise
thoughFortunately
howeverSimilarly
moreoverAccordingly
consequentlyAdditionally
solution: ㉠ 모녀 사이인 두 예술가가 인도 아메다바드의 여러 도로에 3차원 횡단보도를 그려 속도를 줄이게 만든 것은 인도의 델리에서도 채택되었으며, 이는 아이슬란드의 환경 위원 Ralf Trylla에게 영감을 주어 비슷한 사업을 이끌게 했다는 내용으로 이어지므로 결과 를 의미하는 in turn(결국), consequently(결과적으로)가 알맞다. ㉡ 앞에 도로에 그림을 그려 운전 속도를 줄이게 한 내용에 이어, 교통 공학 전문가들은 사람들의 행동을 변화시키도록 하 는 도로상의 노면 표시를 설계한다는 유사한 내용이 이어지므 로, Likewise(마찬가지로), Similarly(유사하게)가 알맞다.

body:
Dark patterns are design elements or processes
that companies use to manipulate consumer
behavior. They come in a wide variety of forms.
Sometimes they are harmless, but sometimes they
are misleading. The following examples of dark
patterns will help you recognize and deal with them
properly in the future.
Forced Continuity
If you have signed up for a streaming service
recently, (A)당신은 무료 체험이 끝나자마자 당신의 신
용 카드에서 자동으로 요금이 청구되는 이 다크 패턴
을 아마 경험했을 것이다. While the companies that
do this would argue that it enables users to
continue to access their service uninterrupted, users
receive no warning that their cards are about to
ⓐ[charge / be charged], often causing them to be
billed unexpectedly. This method is used by many
streaming platforms, but it is also common with
other services that offer free trials.
Artificial Scarcity
“Only two pieces available!” “Only four hours left
until the offer ends!” “Only ten slots left for this
program!” Artificial scarcity is used to stimulate
purchases. This typically comes in three major
forms: insufficient quantities, time, or availability. We
make decisions more quickly under pressure. The
decision is then often made quite automatically only
on the basis of scarcity. After all, no one wants to
miss out on a great offer.
Hidden Information
In this pattern, important information and options
are hidden or displayed in such a way that they are
hardly noticeable. To see the information, you have
to click somewhere, look very closely, or actively
search for it.
Every newsletter must allow you to unsubscribe.
But just because companies have to provide the
option, it doesn’t mean they have to make it easy
for you to see! So the “unsubscribe” link is made
almost ⓑ[invisible / invisibly] in the email. Gray
print on a dark background is rather hard to read,
as is very small print.
Dark patterns are everywhere. It is always
important to be aware ⓒ[that / what] a company’s
goals don’t always correspond with your own. To
detect and resist dark patterns, you need to read
carefully and think before you click on a button.

body:
다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

Changes in visual designs can markedly affect behaviors of people, especially on streets. Two artists, mother and daughter, painted a 3D crosswalk on several roads in Ahmedabad, India. To motorists, the painted lines look like roadblocks, causing them to slow down without braking too suddenly. The scheme was also adopted in Delhi, India. This, in turn, inspired Ralf Trylla, an environmental commissioner in Iceland, to head a similar project. As a result, drivers were being more careful at intersections, which reduced accidents and elevated the safety of pedestrians. The idea has been well received and mirrored in cities of China, the U.S., Canada, and the UK as well.

someone gently to do something.

strategy. The footprints will catch people’s
attention and let people know where the trash
can is.

make people behave differently.

body:
You have probably received a notification from
your smartphone telling you that it is time to
exercise or move. These devices lead people to
move by sending notifications when they have been
(A)[active / inactive] for a set amount of time. You
may not have realized it, but this is an example of
a nudge.
A nudge is an intervention that gently guides
individuals toward a desired action, without
forbidding any options. For example, if a school
wants to reduce the amount of sugary drinks that
students consume, then making them less (B)[visible
/ invisible] than bottled water counts as a nudge,
while banning them altogether does not.
Having been studied in the domain of behavioral
economics and marketing, nudging can be applied
to inducing people to make better or ideal
decisions. Here are some ways nudges have
succeeded in bringing about positive changes by
(C)[tweaking / maintaining] people’s choices.

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: activeinvisibletweaking
inactivevisibletweaking

inactiveinvisibletweaking
inactivevisiblemaintaining
solution: (A) 스마트폰에서 이제 운동하거나 움직일 시간이라는 알림은 사람이 일정 시간 동안 ‘활동하지 않을 때’ 보내지는 것이므로, ‘inactive(활동하지 않는)‘가 흐름상 자연스럽다. (B) 너지는 어떤 선택지도 금지하지 않으면서 원하는 행동으로 개인을 부드럽게 안내하는 개입이므로, 그 예시로 학교에서 단 음료의 양을 줄이기 위해서는 생수보다 덜 ’눈에 띄게(visible)‘ 배치하는 것이 흐름상 자연스럽다. (C) 행동경제학과 마케팅 분야에서 너지는 사람들이 더 나은 또는 이상적인 결정을 내리도록 유도하는 데 적용될 수 있으 며, 너지가 긍정적인 변화를 유발하는 데 성공한 방법들이 있 다는 흐름으로, 사람들의 선택을 ’조정한다(tweaking)'가 흐름상 자연스럽다.

Forced Continuity
If you have signed up for a streaming service
recently, you have probably run into this dark
pattern where your credit card is automatically
charged as soon as a free trial comes to an end.
While the companies that do this would argue that
it enables users to continue to access their service
uninterrupted, users receive no warning that their
cards are about to be charged, often causing them
to be billed unexpectedly. This method is used by
many streaming platforms, but it is also common
with other services that offer free trials.
Artificial Scarcity
“Only two pieces available!” “Only four hours left
until the offer ends!” “Only ten slots left for this
program!” Artificial scarcity is used to stimulate
purchases. This typically comes in three major
forms: insufficient quantities, time, or availability. We
make decisions more quickly under pressure. The
decision is then often made quite automatically only
on the basis of scarcity. After all, no one wants to
miss out on a great offer.
Hidden Information
In this pattern, important information and options
are hidden or displayed in such a way that they are
hardly noticeable. To see the information, you have
to click somewhere, look very closely, or actively
search for it.
Every newsletter must allow you to unsubscribe.
But ㉠단지 기업들이 그 선택을 제공해야만 한다고 해
서, 그들이 당신이 보기에 쉽도록 그것을 만들어야 한
다는 뜻은 아니다! So the “unsubscribe” link is made
almost invisible in the email. Gray print on a dark
background is rather hard to read, as is very small
print. Dark patterns are everywhere. It is always
important to be aware that a company’s goals don’t
always correspond with your own. To detect and
resist dark patterns, you need to read carefully and
think before you click on a button.

solution: ⓑ feeling → feel (made와 목적어 Picasso에 이어져 ‘make+ 목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하게 하다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리이며, Picasso가 ‘느끼는’ 주체이고, 사역동사 make의 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동 관계일 경우 목적격보어 로 동사원형을 사용하므로, feeling을 동사원형 feel로 고친다.) ⓓ more strongly → stronger (‘~되다’라는 뜻의 2형식 동사 grow의 과 거형 grew에 이어진 보어 자리이며, 보어로 부사(구)는 쓸 수 없으므로, 부사의 비교급 more strongly를 형용사의 비교급 stronger로 고친다.) ⓕ preparing → prepared (관계부사 where가 이끄는 절의 동사로 enjoyed가 있으므로, 목적어로 이어진 명사구 Spanish dishes 뒤에 이를 수식하는 분사구를 이끄는 분사가 쓰이는 것은 적절하나, 수 식받는 명사구가 ‘준비된’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 행위 주체가 ‘by+명사구’ 형태로 이어져 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 preparing을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 prepared로 고친다.)

In Vallauris, a small town in the South of France, a
black limousine was parked outside a barbershop.
From inside the car, Pablo Picasso impatiently yelled
out. “Please, Arias, hurry up. We’ll be late for
dinner.” A curious crowd gathered around the car,
ⓐwondering who had the nerve to make the
legendary artist wait. A few moments later, Eugenio
Arias, a man with a cheerful smile, emerged from
his modest shop. “Let’s go,” he said as he climbed
into the limousine. Despite the fact that Picasso was
twenty-eight years older than Arias, the two had
been close friends for twenty years. Let’s go back
to that summer afternoon when (A)__________________
_______________________________________________________.
In 1947, Picasso left the crowded city of Paris and
ⓑmoved to the quiet rural town of Vallauris. As a
foreigner, he often desperately longed for familiar
faces from his home country, Spain. One day, a
friend told him about a local barber from Spain
named Arias. But for Picasso, it was not easy to
visit the barbershop because he had a belief ⓒthat
anyone who possessed his hair or nails would have
control over him. ⓓToo superstitious to let other
people cut his hair, he normally chose to cut his
own hair. Eventually, Picasso gathered his courage
and entered Arias’s barbershop because he was so
eager to meet his fellow countryman. Arias
recognized the famous artist right away, but he
treated Picasso ⓔlike an ordinary customer. Leading
him to a chair, Arias warmly welcomed Picasso in
Spanish. Despite the fact that their conversation was
brief that day, Picasso was deeply impressed by
Arias’s direct and simple manner of speech. He
sensed that Arias was a trustworthy individual with
a great sense of humor who put people at ease.

As time passed, Picasso’s health (A)[recovered
declined] with age. One day, Picasso asked Arias,
“What are you going to do with all the paintings
and sketches I gave you?” Arias responded that he
would build a museum in Spain to display the
works. Picasso was moved to hear that and swore
to help Arias. But unfortunately, he did not live to
see the museum completed, passing away in 1973.
Arias was in grief and despair but found comfort in
knowing that his best friend would live on through
his art. A few years later, Arias returned to Spain
and exhibited Picasso’s works. This small exhibit
attracted visitors from all over the world. A foreign
merchant approached Arias one day and attempted
to persuade him to sell all of Picasso’s works. But
he (B)[refused / consented] to bargain, saying, “Even
if you bring all the money in your country, I will
not sell any of his works to you. His works are
symbols of the friendship between Picasso and me.”
The Museo Picasso - Colección Eugenio Arias (The
Picasso Museum - Eugenio Arias Collection) was
finally completed. This was possible because Arias
donated approximately sixty pieces of Picasso’s
works to Arias’s hometown of Buitrago del Lozoya.
They comprised a collection of paintings, posters,
ceramics, and other works. Each of them is
(C)[indistinguishable / distinct] from Picasso’s other
works because Picasso carved each one with the
inscription Para mi amigo, Arias (For my friend,
Arias). When visitors enter this museum, they
quickly discover that it is more than just a tribute
to honor Picasso’s artistic legacy; it is also a
monument to the artist and barber’s lifelong
friendship.

Picasso’s visits to Arias’s barbershop became
somewhat routine after that. Whenever he visited,
the other customers let him be served first. This
situation made Picasso feel uncomfortable because
it caused other people to wait longer. Sensing his
discomfort, Arias asked if Picasso would prefer to
get haircuts and shaves at home. Picasso happily
accepted the offer. Arias went to Picasso’s house to
cut his hair from then on, but he never charged
Picasso for his services. In return, Picasso gave him
sketches, paintings, and ceramics as a gesture of
friendship. As their friendship grew stronger, Arias
started to drop by Picasso’s house, not to shave or
cut his hair, but to hang out. Picasso once said to
Arias, “You are always welcome to come to my
house. When you’re here, I feel like I’m back in
Spain.” Picasso also paid frequent visits to Arias’s
home, where he enjoyed Spanish dishes prepared
by Arias’s mother. When they dined together, they
would sit and talk for hours.

body:
Can monkeys be friends with horses? How about giraffes and goats? It seems that animals of different species are not compatible with one another, but there is one special friendship that bloomed between a dog and a dolphin. The close friendship between Gunner, a seven-year-old dog, and Delta, a ten-year-old dolphin, is an extraordinary bond that goes beyond the boundaries of their species. Despite their differences in habitat, Gunner and Delta have formed a deep and genuine connection that shows the beauty of friendship between different species. Their first encounter occurred when Gunner’s owner took him to the Dolphin Research Center where Delta lives. As Gunner observed Delta swimming elegantly in the water, he could not help but be fascinated by the dolphin’s grace and friendliness. Gunner, with his playful and loyal nature, seemed to be initially intrigued by Delta’s graceful movements and intelligent behavior. Gunner approached the edge of the enclosure and walked alongside the water while wagging his tail, his tongue hanging out in excitement. Delta, being an exceptionally clever creature, sensed Gunner’s friendly intentions and politely swam over to meet him. The two animals inspected each other with cautious sniffs and gentle touches, quickly establishing a sense of trust. Gunner and Delta would have fun together, engaging in playful games. For example, Gunner would bounce around and chase Delta’s splashes, and Delta would perform leaps for Gunner’s amusement. Their interactions were a harmonious dance of joy and companionship, breaking the barriers of their different physical abilities.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: How Different Habitats Shape Animal Behavior
How We Interpret Friendships Between Different Species
Touching: The Language of Trust Among Animals
Building Friendship and Trust: An Instinct for Survival
The Beauty of Friendship Beyond Biological Boundaries
solution:
1. 개 Gunner와 돌고래 Delta가 서식지와 신체 능력의 차이를 넘어 깊은 우정을 쌓은 이야기이다.
2. 글에서 두 동물의 유대가 ‘종의 경계를 넘어서며 서로 다른 종 사이 우정의 아름다움을 보여 준다’고 했다.

따라서 답은 ⑤이다.

body:
How much time do you spend sitting per day?
Studies have found that one-third of the global
population aged fifteen years and older engage in
insufficient physical activity. (A)특히, 청소년들은 앉아
있는 데 너무 많은 시간을 보내고 정기적으로 활동적
인 신체 활동에 거의 참여하지 않습니다.
The scientific community has even coined the term
“sitting disease” for this phenomenon in order to
represent the harmful health effects that result from long
periods of sitting. The longer you sit, the more exposed
you are to the dangers of obesity, heart disease,
diabetes, and even depression. Walking, according to
health experts, is one of the safest, easiest, and cheapest
forms of exercise to combat sitting disease.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Physical Activity Guidelines for Teenagers
Why Teenagers Prefer Sitting Over Exercising

The Limitations of Modern Medicine in AddressingSitting Disease
solution: 전 세계 15세 이상 인구의 3분의 1이 신체 활동이 부족하며 특히, 청소년들은 너무 오래 앉아 있어 신체 활동을 거의 하지 않는데, 이렇게 오래 앉아 있는 것으로 인한 현상을 일컫는 ‘sitting disease(의자병)’라는 용어를 소개하고, 이로 인해 노출 되는 건강상의 위험(비만, 심장병, 당뇨병, 우울증)과 방지책인 걷기 운동을 제안하는 글이므로, 글의 제목으로 ❹ ‘장시간 앉 아 있는 것의 문제점들과 그 해결책들’이 알맞다.

body:
Walking is not only a simple way to avoid the harmful effects of sitting disease, but it also has other health benefits. You may already be aware of the health benefits of walking, such as bone strengthening, blood pressure reduction, and improved heart health. But did you know that walking (A)______________________________? According to research by the University of Exeter, taking daily walks for fifteen minutes can cut chocolate consumption in half. This is because frequent physical activity can enhance brain function, making it easier to limit our consumption of sweet foods such as chocolate. Moreover, walking can keep you from getting sick during the cold and flu season. A study found that people who walked for at least twenty minutes a day, five days a week, had 43% fewer sick days than those who exercised once a week or less. And even if they did get sick, it was for a shorter period of time with milder symptoms. This is primarily due to the improved immune system that results from walking regularly.

choices: can help lower your cravings for sugary foods
can increase your appetite for sweet snacks like chocolate
can lower your blood pressure almost as much as running
can strengthen your bones just as effectively as dairy products
can help support your immune system and reduce the need for medicine

2. 따라서 빈칸에는 걷기가 ‘단 음식에 대한 갈망을 낮추는 데 도움이 된다’는 말이 와야 한다.

4. 따라서 답은 ①이다.

Walking is not only a simple way to avoid the
harmful effects of sitting disease, but it also has
other health benefits. You may already be aware of
the health benefits of walking, such as bone
strengthening, blood pressure reduction, and
improved heart health. But did you know that
walking can help lower your cravings for sugary

cut chocolate consumption in half. This is because

walking regularly.

body:
Walking is not only a simple way to avoid the harmful effects of sitting disease, but it also has other health benefits. You may already be aware of the health benefits of walking, such as bone strengthening, blood pressure reduction, and improved heart health. But did you know that walking can help lower your cravings for sugary foods? According to research by the University of Exeter, taking daily walks for fifteen minutes can cut chocolate consumption in half. This is because frequent physical activity can enhance brain function, making it easier to limit our consumption of sweet foods such as chocolate. Moreover, walking can keep you from getting sick during the cold and flu season. A study found that people who walked for at least twenty minutes a day, five days a week, had 43% fewer sick days than those who exercised once a week or less. And even if they did get sick, it was for a shorter period of time with milder symptoms. This is primarily due to the improved immune system that results from walking regularly.

The Link Between Exercise Frequency and the Immune System

ⓐ Reading slowly and carefully is one of the most valuable skills a student can develop in an age of endless information. ⓑ Online, we are trained to skim: our eyes jump from headline to headline, and we rarely stay with one text for more than a few minutes. ⓒ This habit may help us gather facts quickly, but it leaves little room for the kind of thinking that turns information into understanding. ⓓ When we read slowly, we have time to question the author's claims, connect new ideas to what we already know, and notice what has been left unsaid. ⓔ Deep reading also strengthens our ability to concentrate, an ability that is increasingly rare and therefore increasingly precious. Of course, skimming has its place; no one needs to study a bus schedule line by line. But when a text deserves our attention, giving it that attention is not a waste of time. It is the very process through which knowledge becomes our own.
solution:
1. ⓐ 「끝없는 정보의 시대에 천천히 주의 깊게 읽는 것은 학생이 기를 수 있는 가장 가치 있는 기술 중 하나이다.」 — 글 전체의 중심 내용을 첫 문장에서 먼저 제시한다.
2. ⓑ·ⓒ는 훑어 읽기 습관의 한계(정보를 이해로 바꾸는 사고의 여지가 없음), ⓓ·ⓔ는 천천히 읽을 때의 이점(주장 검토·지식 연결, 집중력 강화)으로 ⓐ를 뒷받침한다. 마지막 문장 「그것이 바로 지식이 우리 자신의 것이 되는 과정이다」도 ⓐ를 다시 확인한다.
3. 대표 오답 ⓔ는 깊이 읽기의 여러 이점 가운데 «집중력» 하나만 말한 세부 근거이므로 주제문이 될 수 없다.
4. 따라서 답은 ①이다.

body:
다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 글 전체의 중심 내용을 담은 주제문으로 가장 적절한 것은?

In school, a wrong answer is usually marked with a red X and quickly forgotten. ⓐ In a laboratory, however, a failed experiment is rarely thrown away so easily. ⓑ When a result does not match the prediction, a careful scientist asks why, because the gap between what was expected and what actually happened often points to something no one has noticed before. ⓒ Many important discoveries began in exactly this way, as an annoying result that refused to go away. ⓓ Even when a failure reveals nothing new, it tells researchers which paths are not worth following, saving others from repeating the same mistake. ⓔ In science, then, failure is not the opposite of progress but one of its most important sources of information. Students might benefit from adopting a similar attitude. Instead of hiding their mistakes, they could study them, asking what each error reveals about their understanding. A wrong answer examined honestly can teach more than a right answer reached by luck.
solution:
1. ⓔ 「그렇다면 과학에서 실패는 진보의 반대가 아니라 진보의 가장 중요한 정보원 중 하나이다.」 — then(그렇다면)으로 앞의 내용을 일반화해 글의 중심 내용을 정리한다.
2. ⓐ 실험실에서는 실패를 쉽게 버리지 않음 → ⓑ 예측과 결과의 차이가 새로운 것을 가리킴 → ⓒ 중요한 발견이 그렇게 시작됨 → ⓓ 아무것도 드러나지 않아도 가지 말아야 할 길을 알려 줌 — 모두 ⓔ의 근거이다. 마지막 세 문장은 이를 학생의 태도에 적용한 것이다.
3. 대표 오답 ⓑ는 실패가 정보가 되는 한 가지 방식(예측과 결과의 차이)을 설명한 세부 내용이다.
4. 따라서 답은 ⑤이다.

body:
다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 글 전체의 중심 내용을 담은 주제문으로 가장 적절한 것은?

ⓐ We often picture creativity as a sudden flash of inspiration that arrives from nowhere, granted only to a few gifted individuals. ⓑ In reality, however, most creative work consists of combining existing ideas in new ways rather than producing something entirely from scratch. ⓒ The printing press, for example, brought together technologies that already existed, such as movable type, ink, and the screw press used for making wine. ⓓ Similarly, many musicians develop their own style by blending the traditions they grew up listening to. ⓔ Even scientific theories are usually built on the careful work of earlier researchers, as Isaac Newton suggested when he wrote that he had seen further by standing on the shoulders of giants. Understanding creativity in this way has a practical benefit. If new ideas come from connecting old ones, then the best way to become more creative is not to wait for inspiration but to fill our minds with a wide range of knowledge and experiences, giving ourselves more pieces to combine.
solution:
1. ⓑ 「그러나 실제로 대부분의 창의적인 작업은 완전히 무에서 무언가를 만들어 내기보다 기존의 생각들을 새로운 방식으로 결합하는 것이다.」 — however로 통념(ⓐ)을 뒤집으며 글의 중심 내용을 밝힌다.
2. ⓒ 인쇄기(가동 활자·잉크·포도주 압착기의 결합), ⓓ 여러 전통을 섞는 음악가, ⓔ 앞선 연구 위에 세워지는 과학 이론(뉴턴의 「거인의 어깨」)은 모두 ⓑ의 예시이다.
3. 대표 오답 ⓐ는 필자가 반박하려는 «통념»(창의성은 소수에게만 주어지는 갑작스러운 영감)이므로 주제문이 아니다. 통념-반박 구조에서는 however 뒤가 주제문이다.
4. 따라서 답은 ②이다.

body:
다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 글 전체의 중심 내용을 담은 주제문으로 가장 적절한 것은?

Imagine a map of a city drawn at a scale of one to one, showing every tree, crack, and lamppost exactly as it is. ⓐ Such a map would be perfectly accurate, yet completely useless, since it would be as large as the city itself. ⓑ A subway map, by contrast, ignores real distances, straightens curved lines, and leaves out nearly every street, and yet millions of people rely on it every day. ⓒ The lesson is that a model becomes useful not by including everything but by deliberately leaving out what does not matter for its purpose. ⓓ Economists who describe markets, climate scientists who simulate the atmosphere, and even teachers who explain complex ideas to children all make similar choices about what to ignore. ⓔ The danger comes only when we forget that these simplifications were chosen, and begin to treat the model as if it were the world itself. Still, this risk does not reduce the value of simplification. A map is helpful precisely because it is not the territory.
solution:
1. ⓒ 「교훈은, 모형은 모든 것을 담아서가 아니라 목적에 중요하지 않은 것을 의도적으로 빼서 유용해진다는 것이다.」 — The lesson is ~ 로 앞의 두 사례에서 일반 원리를 끌어낸다.
2. ⓐ 1:1 축척 지도(정확하지만 쓸모없음)와 ⓑ 지하철 노선도(거리·곡선·거리 이름을 무시하지만 매일 이용됨)의 대조가 ⓒ를 이끌고, ⓓ는 같은 원리를 경제학·기후 과학·교육으로 넓힌다.
3. 대표 오답 ⓔ는 단순화를 «잊을 때»의 위험이라는 단서일 뿐이다. 바로 뒤에서 「이 위험이 단순화의 가치를 줄이지는 않는다」「지도는 실제 땅이 아니기 때문에 유용하다」고 ⓒ를 다시 확인한다.
4. 따라서 답은 ③이다.

body:
다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 글 전체의 중심 내용을 담은 주제문으로 가장 적절한 것은?

ⓐ Many people speak of traditions as if they were fixed objects handed down unchanged from the distant past. ⓑ A holiday meal, a wedding ceremony, or a folk song seems valuable precisely because it appears to connect us with our ancestors. ⓒ Yet if we look closely, we find that each generation quietly adjusts these customs, replacing ingredients that are no longer available, shortening rituals that no longer fit modern schedules, and adding new verses that speak to current concerns. ⓓ Far from being frozen in time, a living tradition survives precisely because people keep reshaping it to fit their changing lives. ⓔ Customs that refuse to change often become museum pieces, admired from a distance but no longer practiced. This does not mean that anything goes; a tradition that changes too quickly may lose the sense of continuity that gives it meaning. The challenge for each generation is to keep what is essential while letting go of what has become empty habit, so that the tradition remains both recognizable and alive.
solution:
1. ⓓ 「시간 속에 얼어붙어 있기는커녕, 살아 있는 전통은 사람들이 변화하는 삶에 맞게 그것을 계속 다시 빚어내기 때문에 살아남는다.」 — 글의 핵심 주장이다.
2. ⓐ·ⓑ는 «전통은 고정된 것»이라는 통념, ⓒ는 세대마다 관습을 조금씩 바꾼다는 관찰(재료 교체·의식 단축·새 가사 추가), ⓔ는 바뀌기를 거부한 관습이 박물관 전시품이 된다는 반대 사례로 ⓓ를 뒷받침한다.
3. 대표 오답 ⓒ는 ⓓ의 근거가 되는 관찰(구체적 사례 나열)이고, ⓐ는 반박 대상인 통념이다. 마지막 두 문장도 «본질은 지키되 변화를 허용하라»는 ⓓ의 연장이다.
4. 따라서 답은 ④이다.

body:
다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 글쓴이가 사례들로부터 이끌어 낸 «일반 원리»를 담아 글의 요지를 가장 잘 드러낸 문장은?

When a hospital is judged mainly by how quickly it treats patients in its emergency room, something curious can happen. ⓐ Staff may begin to move patients out of the emergency room into hallways or waiting areas, not because the patients are better, but because the clock stops once they leave. ⓑ Similarly, a school rated only by test scores may devote more and more class time to test practice, while subjects that are not tested quietly disappear from the schedule. ⓒ In both cases, the numbers improve while the thing they were meant to reflect does not. ⓓ This is because a measurement that works well as an indicator tends to lose its value once people are rewarded for pushing it up directly. ⓔ Numbers are not the problem in themselves; without them, it would be almost impossible to compare performance or to notice when something is going wrong. The solution, then, is not to abandon measurement but to use several indicators at once, to change them from time to time, and to keep asking whether improvements on paper match improvements in reality.
solution:
1. ⓓ 「이는 지표로서 잘 작동하는 측정치가, 사람들이 그 수치를 직접 끌어올리는 데 보상을 받게 되는 순간 가치를 잃는 경향이 있기 때문이다.」 — 병원·학교 사례를 일반 원리로 끌어올린 문장이다.
2. ⓐ(응급실 시간 줄이기 위해 환자를 복도로 옮김)와 ⓑ(시험 점수만으로 평가받는 학교가 시험 연습에 치중함)는 사례, ⓒ는 두 사례의 공통 현상(수치는 좋아지지만 실제는 그대로), ⓓ는 그 원인이 되는 일반 원리이다.
3. 매력적 오답 ⓒ는 «In both cases»라는 말처럼 두 사례에 한정된 요약이고 왜 그런지를 말하지 않는다. ⓔ는 «수치 자체가 문제는 아니다»라는 양보로, 마지막 문장의 해결책(여러 지표 사용)으로 가는 연결 고리일 뿐 요지가 아니다.
4. 따라서 답은 ④이다.

body:
다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

In many classrooms, an assignment is graded once and then returned, and the story ends there. Students glance at the score, perhaps feel pleased or disappointed, and move on to the next task without reading the comments. I believe this system wastes one of the best opportunities for learning. Teachers should give students the chance to revise their work after receiving feedback and to submit it again. When students know that they can improve their grade by acting on comments, they read those comments carefully and think about what went wrong. The second draft becomes a real conversation between teacher and student rather than a final judgment. Some worry that allowing revisions will make grades less meaningful or give students an excuse to be careless the first time. But the purpose of school is not simply to measure what students can do on their first try; it is to help them become better. A grade that reflects what a student has finally learned is, in fact, more meaningful than one that records only an early mistake.
choices: 과제 점수는 첫 제출물만으로 공정하게 매겨야 한다.
교사는 과제에 점수 대신 서술형 논평만 달아야 한다.
교사는 학생들이 피드백을 받은 뒤 과제를 고쳐 다시 제출할 수 있게 해야 한다.
학생들은 과제를 내기 전에 친구와 서로 검토해야 한다.
과제의 양을 줄여 학생들이 한 과제에 집중하게 해야 한다.
solution:
1. 주장은 「Teachers should give students the chance to revise their work after receiving feedback and to submit it again.(교사는 학생들에게 피드백을 받은 뒤 과제를 고쳐 다시 제출할 기회를 주어야 한다.)」에 직접 드러난다.
2. 근거: 고쳐 낼 수 있으면 학생들이 논평을 꼼꼼히 읽고, 두 번째 원고가 «최종 판정»이 아닌 «대화»가 된다. 반론(성적의 의미가 줄어든다)에는 「학교의 목적은 첫 시도를 재는 것이 아니라 더 나아지게 돕는 것」이라고 답한다.
3. 「첫 제출물만으로 채점」은 필자가 비판하는 현재 방식이고, 서술형 논평만 달기·동료 검토·과제 줄이기는 글에 없는 내용이다.
4. 따라서 답은 ③이다.

body:
다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

For most of the last century, city streets were designed with a single goal in mind: moving cars as quickly as possible. Roads were widened, sidewalks were narrowed, and crossings were placed far apart so that traffic would not be slowed. The result, in many cities, is a landscape that feels hostile to anyone who is not sitting behind a wheel. Children cannot walk safely to school, elderly residents hesitate to cross the street, and small shops struggle because few people pass by on foot. It is time for cities to change their priorities. When planning or rebuilding streets, city governments should put pedestrians, not vehicles, at the center of their decisions. Wider sidewalks, more frequent crossings, trees that provide shade, and benches where people can rest may slow traffic slightly, but they bring life back to neighborhoods. Streets are not merely channels for cars to pass through; they are among the most important public spaces a city has, and they should be designed for the people who live beside them.
choices: 교통 체증을 줄이기 위해 도로를 넓혀야 한다.
도심에서는 자동차 통행을 전면 금지해야 한다.
대중교통 요금을 낮춰 자가용 이용을 줄여야 한다.
도시의 거리는 자동차보다 보행자를 중심에 두고 설계해야 한다.
노인과 어린이를 위한 전용 도로를 따로 만들어야 한다.
solution:
1. 주장: 「city governments should put pedestrians, not vehicles, at the center of their decisions(시 정부는 차량이 아니라 보행자를 결정의 중심에 두어야 한다)」.
2. 마지막 문장 「거리는 단지 차가 지나가는 통로가 아니라 도시의 가장 중요한 공공 공간이며, 그 옆에 사는 사람들을 위해 설계되어야 한다」가 이를 다시 강조한다.
3. 매력적 오답 「자동차 통행 전면 금지」: 필자는 보행자 중심 설계가 교통을 «약간 느리게 할 수 있다(may slow traffic slightly)»고 했을 뿐, 차를 금지하자고 하지 않았다. 도로 확장은 필자가 비판하는 과거 방식이다.
4. 따라서 답은 ④이다.

body:
다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

"Great job!" It is perhaps the most common phrase heard in classrooms, offices, and homes. We say it to encourage people, and it certainly feels pleasant to hear. Yet such general praise tells the listener very little. Was it the idea that was good, the effort, the organization, or simply the fact that the task was finished? Without knowing, the person cannot repeat what worked or build on it. Worse, praise that is given for everything eventually loses its value, much like money printed without limit. If we truly want to help others grow, we should replace vague compliments with specific descriptions of what they did well and why it mattered. Saying, "Your opening example made the problem easy to understand," takes only a few more seconds than "Great job," but it gives the listener something to hold on to. Specific praise also shows that we paid attention, and being noticed in this way is often more motivating than any amount of general approval.
choices: 칭찬은 동기를 떨어뜨리므로 되도록 삼가야 한다.
결과보다 노력을 중심으로 칭찬해야 한다.
칭찬과 비판을 균형 있게 섞어 전달해야 한다.
칭찬은 다른 사람들 앞에서 공개적으로 해야 한다.
칭찬할 때는 막연한 말 대신 무엇을 왜 잘했는지 구체적으로 말해 주어야 한다.
solution:
1. 주장: 「we should replace vague compliments with specific descriptions of what they did well and why it mattered(막연한 칭찬을, 상대가 무엇을 잘했고 그것이 왜 중요했는지에 대한 구체적인 묘사로 바꾸어야 한다)」.
2. 근거: 막연한 칭찬은 무엇이 좋았는지 알려 주지 않아 되풀이하거나 발전시킬 수 없고, 무엇에나 주는 칭찬은 한없이 찍어 낸 돈처럼 가치를 잃는다.
3. 필자는 칭찬 자체를 삼가라는 것이 아니라 «구체적으로» 하라는 것이다. 노력 칭찬·비판과의 균형·공개 칭찬은 글에서 다루지 않았다.
4. 따라서 답은 ⑤이다.

body:
다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

When scientists speak to the public, they often feel pressure to sound certain.
