International Book Fair of Bogotá
Where: Bogotá, Colombia
The Bogotá International Book Fair (FILBo) is one of the most important annual events in Colombia. It is held at Corferias, a convention center (A)[locating / located] in the city of Bogotá. It features a wide range of authors and publishers and highlights Colombian and Latin American literature. It promotes books and literacy through various events for 15 days.
Toronto International Festival of Authors
Where: Toronto, Canada
If you’re in Toronto in September, don’t miss Canada’s oldest literary festival! It’s all about books, authors, and readers coming together. You’ll find Canadian and international writers (B)[share / sharing] new stories and talking about writing as an art. Also, if you love mysteries, there’s the Motive Crime & Mystery Festival waiting for you in Toronto as well!
Louisiana Literature Festival
Where: Humlebaek, Denmark
The Louisiana Literature Festival is an annual literary event held in Humlebaek, (C)[which / where] is 30 minutes north of Copenhagen, Denmark. It is held around the third weekend of August at the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art. The festival includes engaging conversations among writers as well as between writers and critics. It also features readings and diverse performances.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: located sharing where
locating sharing which
locating share where
located sharing which
located share which
solution:
(A) 앞에 있는 명사구 a convention center를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사 자리이며, 수식을 받는 a convention center가 ‘위치해 있는’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없어 전치사 in이 바로 이어지고 있으므로, ‘locate A in B(A를 B에 위치시키다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘A be located in B(A가 B에 위치하다)’을 이루는 과거분사 located가 알맞다.
(B) 동사원형 find와 목적어 Canadian and international writers에 이어져 ‘find+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하고 있는 것을 발견하다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리로, 목적어와 목적격보어 사이가 능동적인 관계일 경우 목적격보어로 현재분사를 취할 수 있으며 현재분사인 talking과 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어 있으므로 현재분사 sharing이 알맞다.
(C) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(is ~ Copenhagen, Denmark)을 이끌어 선행사인 Humlebaek를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다.

body:
Santiago saw the shark’s jaws opening and closing in anticipation. He knew this shark no longer cared about the dangers of a boat or of a fisherman. The smell of blood took away the shark’s fear, ⓐmade it brave and reckless. Santiago didn’t have much rope ⓑleft over from tying up the marlin, but he tightened the short remaining piece of rope into a knot on his spear. The shark got closer and closer, mouth open and teeth shining in the sunlight.
Santiago’s mind felt strong and clear, his willpower ⓒrestoring. The spear wasn’t very long, too short to hit the shark before it arrived at the marlin. Still, Santiago refused to give up. The shark’s eyes flashed and he bit the beautiful fish just above the tail. It ripped and bit and took a huge piece of meat — at least 40 pounds — out of the giant marlin.
The old man could hear the marlin’s skin tearing and bones breaking as he drove the spear into the shark’s head. He pushed the weapon in right behind the eyes and above the neck, ⓓwhere the brain was. It turned over, and he could see the shark’s eyes rolling in its head. It hit the water with its tail and turned the ocean water white with its struggling.
Santiago tried to get his spear out, but couldn’t. He ⓔhad cast the spear too deep into the shark’s body, and the rope was too short. Even though its body struggled, the shark was already dead. After a moment, it lay still on the surface before sinking slowly into the water, ⓕtaking the spear with it.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓐ made → making (동사가 있는 완전한 절(The smell ~ fear)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 또 다른 동사(구)가 이어질 수 없으므로, 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 The smell of blood가 ‘만드는’ 주체이고 뒤에 the shark를 가리키는 목적어 it과 목적격보어 brave and reckless가 이어지고 있으므로 made를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 making으로 고쳐야 한다.)
ⓒ restoring → restored (완전한 절(Santiago’s mind ~ clear) 다음에 접속사가 아닌 콤마(,)로만 이어지고 있으므로 주절과 다른 의미상의 주어가 남아있는 독립분사구문으로, 의미상 주어인 his willpower는 ‘회복되는’ 대상이므로 restoring은 수동의 의미인 과거분사 restored로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ 앞의 명사 rope를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사 자리로 수식을 받는 rope가 ‘남겨진’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 left는 알맞다.
ⓓ 콤마(,) 뒤에서 완전한 절(the brain was)을 이끌어 앞의 명사구 right behind the eyes and above the neck을 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 관계부사 where는 알맞다.
ⓔ 흐름상 그가 창을 던졌던 것은 그가 자신의 창을 빼내려고 했던(tried) 것보다 더 먼저 일어난 일이므로 과거완료(had p.p.)인 had cast는 알맞다.

body:
Although group singing has become less common, it’s an activity that can be beneficial. So why does group singing make us feel so good? Decades of research have shown that singing is good for you on many levels by reducing stress and increasing the release of happiness hormones such as endorphins, dopamine, and serotonin. Singing with others has additional benefits. It brings people closer together and helps create bonds that can support self-esteem in a more stable way. The sense of belonging and purpose created in the moment makes us feel connected to others and to something greater. Thus, it’s no surprise that people who sing together have healthier minds and more readily participate in their communities. A few studies have reported that people who sang in choirs were more optimistic, less lonely, had stronger relationships, and were more likely to contribute positively to their communities than those who didn’t. The good news is that people can enjoy these benefits even when they’re singing with others online. Being together is the key.
다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: Why has group singing become less common nowadays?
What effects does singing have on stress and mood?
What additional benefits can people gain from singing with others?
How can singing together contribute to people's self-esteem?
What differences were found between people who sang in choirs and those who did not?

Korean pop music fans are famous for their singing-along during concerts, and their participation in the concert sometimes goes beyond the conventional expectations of musicians. (A)한국에서 공연하는 아티스트들은 떼창이라 불리는 관객들의 노래에 의해 종종 감명을 받는다. What’s so impressive is that they memorize entire songs in English or even in other foreign languages. Before going to a concert, loyal fans look at the set list, memorize the lyrics of all the songs, and plan a tte-chang event to make their concert experience special. In this way, Korean fans show that they really care about the music and the musicians. There are countries where silent appreciation is expected from the concert audience, but at Korean pop music concerts, enthusiastic participation in tte-chang often accompanied by dancing is the norm.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 분사구를 두 번 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것
<보기>
impress, call, perform, tte-chang, artists, the audience singing
______ ______ ______ ______ ______ often ______ ______ ______ ______ ______, ______ ______.
answer: Artists performing in Korea are often impressed by the audience singing, called tte-chang.
solution:
• 주어 Artists를 쓰고, Artists가 ‘공연하는’ 주체이므로 동사 perform을 능동의 의미인 현재분사 performing으로 변형하여 쓰고 수식어 in Korea를 이어 쓴다.
• 주어 Artists가 ‘감명받는‘ 대상이므로 수동태(be+p.p.)를 써야 한다. 주어 Artists에 수일치한 be동사 are를 쓰고 부사 often 뒤에 impress의 과거분사 impressed를 이어 쓴다.
• ’~에 의해‘를 뜻하는 전치사 by를 쓰고 목적어 the audience singing을 이어 쓴다.
• the audience singing이 떼창이라 ’불리는‘ 대상이므로 ’call+목적어+목적격보어(~을 …라고 부르다)’의 수동 표현이 되도록 콤마(,) 뒤에 과거분사구 called tte-chang을 이어 쓴다.

body:
In a highly connected world ⓐwhere technology doesn’t necessarily connect people in a human way, individuals become socially ⓑisolated and feel intense loneliness. The invention of portable music players and earphones has made music more personal, too. However, the communal elements persist, manifesting their power in singing events, large and small. Singing with others can be a way to heal and help us ⓒfeel connected, happy, and healthy. Maybe it is in our genes as a social species. Just open your mouth, start making a sound, and let your voice ⓓgo. You’ll know how good it is almost ⓔinstant.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ instant → instantly (부사 almost의 수식을 받으며, 동시에 동사 know를 수식하므로 형용사 instant를 부사 instantly로 고친다.
참고로 know의 목적어는 how ~ is까지의 간접의문문이므로 is의 보어가 아님에 주의한다.)
오답
ⓐ 완전한 절(technology ~ way)을 이끌어 장소를 뜻하는 명사구 a highly connected world를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 관계부사 where는 적절하다.
ⓑ 2형식 동사 become에 이어지는 보어 자리이며, 주어 individuals가 ‘고립된’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 형태의 형용사 isolated는 적절하다.
ⓒ 동사 help와 목적어인 us 뒤에 이어진 목적격보어 자리이며, 'help+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 것을 돕다)'의 5형식 구문에서 동사 help는 목적격보어로 동사원형 또는 to부정사를 취하므로 동사원형 feel은 적절하다.
ⓓ ‘~가 …하게 하다’라는 뜻의 사역동사 let은 ‘let+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형)’의 구조로, let은 목적격보어로 동사원형을 취하므로 동사원형 go는 적절하다.

body:
The Old Man and the Sea is about an old man called Santiago. Santiago hadn’t caught a fish in 84 days, so people thought he was unlucky, maybe cursed. In order to change his terrible luck, Santiago decided to go out into the deep ocean, far beyond the other fishermen. At first, he only caught a small tuna, but at the end of the 85th day, a powerful, magnificent marlin bit Santiago’s fishing hook. The fish was so strong it dragged Santiago’s boat for three days. Santiago learned to respect the fish, to admire its courage, and to appreciate its beauty. When it finally died, he saw it was too big to put inside the boat. Instead, he tied it to the side of his boat and tried to return home. Unfortunately, a shark smelled the marlin’s blood and threatened to eat Santiago’s prized fish.
윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: a fisherman’s hard-earned success endangered by a shark
the intensified rivalry between Santiago and the other fishermen
Santiago’s ultimately futile struggle to overcome persistent misfortune
the transformation of a dangerous sea creature into a trusted companion
an old man’s admiration for a magnificent marlin that slipped away from him
solution: 84일 동안 물고기를 잡지 못한 노인 Santiago는 자신의 불운을 바꾸기 위해 먼 바다로 나가고, 사흘 동안의 힘겨운 싸움 끝에 거대한 청새치를 잡는 데 성공하여 배 옆에 묶고 귀항하던 중 청새치의 피 냄새를 맡은 상어가 나타나 그의 소중한 물고기를 위협한다는 내용이므로, 글의 주제로 ❶ ‘상어에 의해 위태로워진 한 어부의 힘겹게 얻은 성공’이 알맞다.

body:
Santiago saw the shark’s jaws opening and closing in anticipation. He knew this shark no longer cared about the dangers of a boat or of a fisherman. The smell of blood took away the shark’s fear, making it brave and reckless. Santiago didn’t have much rope left over from tying up the marlin, but he tightened the short remaining piece of rope into a knot on his spear. The shark got closer and closer, mouth open and teeth shining in the sunlight.
Santiago’s mind felt strong and clear, his willpower restored. The spear wasn’t very long, too short to hit the shark before it arrived at the marlin. Still, Santiago refused to give up. The shark’s eyes flashed and he bit the beautiful fish just above the tail. It ripped and bit and took a huge piece of meat — at least 40 pounds — out of the giant marlin.
다음 글을 아래와 같이 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 ㉠, ㉡에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
Despite Santiago's firm resolve and preparation to ㉠______ his catch with a spear, a ㉡______ shark, drawn by blood, succeeded in tearing a significant portion of meat from the marlin.
㉠                    ㉡
choices: protect    timid
retrieve    hesitant
defend    reckless
secure    cautious
cut    bold
solution: [요약문] 잡은 물고기를 창으로 ㉠지키겠다는 Santiago의 굳은 결의와 준비에도 불구하고, 피 냄새에 이끌린 ㉡무모한 상어는 결국 청새치의 살점을 상당량 뜯어내는 데 성공했다.

body:
The old man could hear the marlin’s skin tearing and bones breaking as he drove the spear into the shark’s head. He pushed the weapon in right behind the eyes and above the neck, where the brain was. It turned over, and he could see the shark’s eyes rolling in its head. It hit the water with its tail and turned the ocean water white with its struggling.
Santiago tried to get his spear out, but couldn’t. He had cast the spear too deep into the shark’s body, and the rope was too short. Even though its body struggled, the shark was already dead. After a moment, it lay still on the surface before sinking slowly into the water, taking the spear with it.
다음 글을 읽고 아래 질문에 대한 답을 <조건>에 알맞게 완성하시오.

• 지문의 표현을 찾아 그대로 쓸 것
• (A)는 8단어, (B)는 6단어, (C)는 5단어로 쓸 것
(1) Where did Santiago drive his spear to kill the shark?
→ He drove his spear into the shark’s head, (A) ______.
(2) Why was Santiago unable to recover his spear from the shark?
→ Because the spear had gone (B) ______ and (C) ______.
answer:
(A) right behind the eyes and above the neck
(B) too deep into the shark’s body
(C) the rope was too short
solution:
정답은 (A) right behind the eyes and above the neck
(B) too deep into the shark’s body

bite, flow, so much of, the water, the marlin’s, into

Are you keen on exploring the world of literature? Is reading your hobby? Here’s an exciting type of event — literary festivals! These events are hosted in cities with rich literary histories, connecting authors and readers. Take a glance at these festivals across different regions!
Edinburgh International Book Festival
Where: Edinburgh, Scotland
The Edinburgh International Book Festival happens every year in Edinburgh, which was designated the first UNESCO City of Literature. The festival is one of the largest literary events globally and is typically held in August. It takes place at the University of Edinburgh’s College of Art, creating a village atmosphere. There are outdoor screens for live events, making it an engaging experience for all.
Frankfurter Buchmesse
Where: Frankfurt, Germany
The Frankfurter Buchmesse is the world’s largest book fair, drawing together publishers, authors, and book fans from across the globe. It is held for five days in October, with the initial two days usually reserved for trade visitors and professionals, while the following days are open to the general public. This fair is a must for anybody, speaking any language, who has ambitions in the publishing world or simply loves to read.

choices: Exploring the Historical Backgrounds of Literary Festivals
How Literary Events Cater to Professionals and the General Public
An Introduction to Two Literary Events and Their Key Characteristics
The Challenges of Organizing International Book Fairs in Historic Cities
The Growing Cultural Influence of Literary Festivals on Authors and Readers

body:
“Don’t think, old man,” he said. “Sail on this course and take it when it comes.”
But he couldn’t stop thinking. Alone on the ocean, with the poor marlin’s blood spilling into the water, all he could do was think. He thought of the great baseball player Joe DiMaggio. He wondered if Joe DiMaggio could have killed the shark without losing the spear. Santiago thought of his own injured hands and wondered how Joe DiMaggio could play baseball so well in spite of his own injuries. He wondered if he, like Joe DiMaggio, could ignore the unbearable pain and fatigue in his body long enough to meet his goals.
“ⓐ______, old man,” he said. “Every minute now you are closer to home. You sail lighter for the loss of 40 pounds.”
However, Santiago knew this was false hope. Too much blood in the water. Too many sharks. Too far from land with these strong ocean currents. Still, the fisherman promised he would continue to fight. Neither fear nor the loss of his spear could take away his determination. ⓑ그는 새로운 무기를 생각해 내야 했고, 배를 젓는 노들을 떼어 (그중) 하나에 자신의 칼을 부착했다.
“Now,” he said. “I am still an old man. But I am not unarmed.”
The breeze got stronger and his boat sped up. He felt fresh, and his determination returned. The sharks would almost certainly take his beautiful marlin, but Santiago would never cease fighting them. ⓒA man can be destroyed, but never defeated.
윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Look on the bright side
Trust in your guaranteed success
Recall the pain you have suffered
Concentrate on another shark attack
Stay confident that danger has passed
solution: 이제 매 순간 집에 더 가까워지고 있고, 40파운드를 잃어서 더 가볍게 나아가고 있다는 긍정적인 생각과 이런 생각이 거짓 희망이라는 것을 알고 있었다는 그의 인식이 이어지고 있으므로, 뭔가 기분 좋은 것을 생각해 보라는 흐름으로 빈칸에는 ❶ ‘밝은 면을 바라보자’가 알맞다.

<조건>
• 분사구문을 사용할 것
• 부정대명사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)

<보기>
come up with, attach, remove, have to, a new weapon, the rowing oars, his knife
→ He ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______, ______ ______ ______ ______ and ______ ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: He had to come up with a new weapon, removing the rowing oars and attaching his knife to one.
solution:
• 문맥상 과거의 사건을 묘사하고 있으므로, 제시된 주어 He에 이어지는 동사 자리에 ‘~해야 한다’를 뜻하는 have to의 과거형인 had to를 가장 먼저 쓰고, 동사구를 이루는 come up with와 목적어 a new weapon을 이어서 쓴다.
• 분사구문을 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라 주어진 동사 remove를 변형하되 의미상 주어 He가 ‘떼는’ 주체이므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 removing으로 변형하여 쓰고 이어서 목적어로 the spear를 쓴다. 등위접속사 and 뒤에도 분사구문의 형태로 써야 하며, 의미상 주어 He가 ‘부착하는’ 주체이므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 attaching으로 변형한 뒤, ‘attach A to B(A를 B에 부착하다)’ 구문을 사용해 목적어 his knife와 전치사 to를 이어서 쓴 다음, 부정대명사를 사용하라는 <조건>에 따라 목적어로 ‘(~ 중에) 하나’를 뜻하는 부정대명사 one을 이어서 쓴다. 참고로, one은 one of the rowing oars를 가리킨다.

The Bogotá International Book Fair (FILBo) is one of the most important annual events in Colombia. It is held at Corferias, a convention center located in the city of Bogotá. Toronto International Festival of Authors
Where: Toronto, Canada
If you’re in Toronto in September, don’t miss Canada’s oldest literary festival! It’s all about books, authors, and readers coming together. The Louisiana Literature Festival is an annual literary event held in Humlebaek, which is 30 minutes north of Copenhagen, Denmark. It is held around the third weekend of August at the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art. The festival includes engaging conversations among writers as well as between writers and critics. It also (C)[eliminates / features] readings and diverse performances.

(B) 토론토 국제 작가 축제는 책과 작가, 독자가 함께 모이는 것에 관한 것이라고 했고, 뒤에 캐나다 및 국제 작가들이 예술로서의 글쓰기에 관해 이야기하고 있는 모습을 보게 될 것이라는 축제의 또 다른 특징이 and(그리고)로 연결되므로, 캐나다 및 국제 작가들이 새로운 이야기를 공유하는 모습을 볼 것이라는 축제의 특징을 언급하는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 sharing(~을 공유하는)이 알맞다.
(C) 루이지애나 문학 축제는 작가와 비평가 사이의 대화는 물론 작가들 간의 흥미로운 대화를 포함한다는 축제의 특징을 언급하고 있고 also(또한)로 나열되므로 축제는 또한 낭독회와 다양한 공연을 특색으로 한다는 축제의 또 다른 특징을 언급하는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 features(~을 특색으로 하다)가 알맞다.

The Old Man and the Sea ⓐ[is / are] about an old man called Santiago. Santiago hadn’t caught a fish in 84 days, so people thought he was unlucky, maybe ⓑ[cursing / cursed]. In order to change his terrible luck, Santiago decided to go out into the deep ocean, far beyond the other fishermen. At first, he only caught a small tuna, but at the end of the 85th day, a powerful, magnificent marlin bit Santiago’s fishing hook. The fish was ⓒ[so / too] strong it dragged Santiago’s boat for three days. Santiago learned to respect the fish, to admire its courage, and to appreciate its beauty. When it finally died, he saw (A)______. Instead, he tied it to the side of his boat and tried to return home. Unfortunately, a shark smelled the marlin’s blood and threatened to eat Santiago’s prized fish.
윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ        ⓑ        ⓒ
choices: are    cursed    so
is    cursed    so
are    cursing    too
is    cursed    too
is    cursing    so
solution:
ⓐ 주어 The Old Man and the Sea는 작품 제목으로 그 안에 and로 복수의 명사(구)가 포함되어 있더라도 하나의 작품을 나타내어 단수 취급하므로, 단수동사 is가 알맞다.
ⓑ 콤마(,) 앞의 언급된 he(=Santiago)의 상태를 부연 설명하는 분사구로, 의미상 주어인 he가 ‘저주를 받은’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 형태의 형용사 cursed가 알맞다. maybe와 cursed 사이에 he was가 생략된 것으로도 볼 수 있다.
ⓒ 뒤에 오는 형용사와 결과를 나타내는 완전한 절(it dragged Santiago’s boat for three days)과 함께 ’너무 ~해서 …하다‘라는 뜻의 ’so+형용사/부사(+that)+주어+동사~‘ 구문을 이루어야 하므로 so가 알맞다.

Minority Report
Minority Report, a film set in the year 2050, was released in 2002. It features AI-based advertisements that can identify individuals from a remote distance by scanning people’s eyes. (C) Regarding the technology identifying people through scanning eyes, some devices have already been developed. However, those that do not use AI technology have a critical limitation. They can identify a person only if he or she is standing still. (D) They can scan people’s eyes when they are walking. There has been continuous development of this technology up until now. (E)

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘반면에, AI를 이용하는 기기들은 이러한 한계를 극복했습니다.’라는 뜻으로, On the other hand(반면에)를 사용해 앞서 언급한 한계와 대조되는 내용을 제시하는 흐름이므로, this limitation(이러한 한계)이 가리키는 내용, 즉 AI 기술을 사용하지 않는 기기들은 사람이 가만히 서 있을 때만 그 사람을 식별할 수 있다는 한계를 설명한 내용의 뒤이자, 주어진 문장의 devices employing AI를 They로 가리켜 그것들이 걷고 있는 사람들의 눈도 스캔할 수 있다고 설명하는 내용 앞인 (D)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

body:
2001: A Space Odyssey
This movie, ⓐsetting in 2001, realistically describes a group of scientists on a spaceship heading to another planet. However, it was released in 1968, a year prior to the first moon landing. This means that human imagination goes far beyond reality. In the movie, the ship has a computer system, ⓑcalled “HAL-9000.” It provided the audience with the chance ⓒto understand AI. It could operate and regulate all of the spacecraft’s systems and help the astronauts ⓓconducting experiments by analyzing data. In one scene, the astronauts and HAL-9000 carry out a conversation about a faulty component of the spacecraft. Then, HAL-9000 makes a recommendation for the next step. The system could even draw logical conclusions and evaluate its decisions. The AI helper for a spaceship, which was only seen in the film at the time, ⓔhas become a reality. (A)2008년, 지구의 궤도를 도는 대형 우주선인 국제우주정거장에서 CIMON이라는 이름의 AI 로봇을 사용하기 시작했습니다. It is a floating spherical robot ⓕthat can move around inside the spacecraft. CIMON, ⓖweighing only 5 kg, serves as a competent AI assistant for astronauts. The robot assists astronauts in more effectively accomplishing complex tasks by offering advice during experiments and work. It is also able to record and film the astronauts’ activities when ⓗasked.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓗ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓐ setting → set (주어 This movie에 대한 동사로 describes가 있으므로 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입되어 주어를 부연 설명하는 분사구문을 이루는 분사가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 의미상 주어인 This movie가 ‘설정된’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 ‘be set in ~ ((특정 장소·시대 등)을 배경으로 하다)’의 전치사구 in 2001이 이어져 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 setting을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 set으로 고친다.)
ⓓ conducting → conduct 또는 to conduct (help가 준사역동사로 쓰여 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 것을 돕다)’의 5형식 구문을 이룰 때 목적격보어로 동사원형(원형부정사)이나 to부정사가 쓰이므로, help와 목적어 the astronauts 뒤의 목적격보어 자리에 쓰인 conducting을 동사원형 conduct나 to부정사인 to conduct로 고친다.)
*원래 지문에는 conduct가 쓰였음
오답
ⓑ 완전한 절(the ship has a computer system)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지므로 흐름상 앞 절의 명사구 a computer system을 부연 설명하는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 분사구문의 의미상 주어인 a computer system이 ‘불리는’ 대상이고 뒤에 ‘call+목적어+목적격보어(~을 …라고 부르다)’의 목적격보어에 해당하는 “HAL-9000”가 있으므로, 수동 표현인 ‘be called+보어(…라고 불리다)’의 과거분사 called는 알맞다.
ⓗ 접속사 when 뒤에 주어와 be동사가 생략된 형태인 ‘접속사+분사‘ 구문을 이루는 분사가 올 자리로, 생략된 주어 it(=the robot)이 ’요청받는‘ 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 asked는 알맞다.

solution:
• 주어 the International Space Station 뒤에 두 개의 콤마(,)로 주어와 동격을 이루는 명사구가 삽입된 구조가 되도록 먼저 명사구 a large spacecraft를 쓴 뒤, <조건>에 따라 앞의 명사구를 수식하는 분사구를 사용하되, 수식받는 명사구가 타동사 orbit(~의 주변에 궤도를 그리며 돌다)의 주체이므로 능동을 나타내는 orbiting으로 변형한 후, 목적어로 Earth를 쓴다.

This is a science fiction animation that was released in 2014. There is a scene in the movie where a boy meets Baymax, a personal medical aid AI robot. The robot scans the boy’s body to detect potential health problems ⓐ[using / used] its sensors and cameras. ⓑ[That / What] it discovers within seconds is a wound in his arm. It administers medicine on the wound. In ⓒ[another / other] scene where he has a mood swing, Baymax checks his hormone levels to determine the cause of his mood swing.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: using What another
using What other
using That another
used What other
used That another
solution:
ⓐ 앞의 완전한 절(The robot ~ problems)에 연결되어 동시동작(~하면서)을 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사가 올 자리이며, 주절 주어(The robot)와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어가 ‘사용하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 its sensors and cameras가 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 using이 알맞다.
ⓑ 문장의 주어 자리에서 타동사 discovers의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(it discovers within seconds)을 이끌고 있으므로, 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것’이라는 의미로 명사절을 이끌며, 흐름상 보어인 a wound in his arm을 강조하는 ‘What+주어+동사~+be동사 … (~한 것은 바로 …이다)’ 형태의 강조 구문을 이루는 관계대명사 What이 알맞다.
ⓒ 뒤에 가산명사의 단수형인 scene이 이어져 있으므로, ‘또 하나의 ~’라는 의미로 단수명사(구)를 수식할 수 있는 another가 알맞다. 참고로, other는 ‘다른 ~’이라는 의미로 복수명사(구)나 불가산명사를 수식한다.

These days, AI-based programs or robots are widely used in the medical industry. Some AI programs have been refined to the point that they can not only identify cancer quickly and accurately, but also predict the chance of getting cancer. AI robots are also used in operating rooms. Based on the collected data, AI surgical robots can conduct cognitive activities such as voice recognition, decision-making, problem-solving, and more. Under the guidance and control of doctors, they can conduct elementary operations such as cutting and stitching patients undergoing surgery. Another example is the development of an AI system to forecast when a hospitalized patient’s condition is likely to get worse. It analyzes the patient’s profile and data and assigns scores indicating the need for transfer to an intensive care unit. The medical team intervenes when a patient’s scores reach a certain level.

For example, when provided with the input of a thirty-five-year-old man’s face, the AI program generates different facial images at different ages. ⓒWhile there have been existing techniques that can achieve similar results, they required a (B)simple process. These results are (E)maintained even when the actors make varied facial expressions. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓐ that → what (상관접속사 ‘not only A, but also B(A뿐만 아니라, B도)’에 의해 단수동사 assists와 병렬연결을 이루는 단수동사 enables가 쓰이고 뒤에 복수명사 producers를 가리키는 복수대명사 them과 to부정사 to make가 이어져 ‘enable+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)(~가 …할 수 있게 하다)’의 5형식 구조를 이룬 것과, ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형)(~을 …하게 만들다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리에 ‘come alive(생생하게 살아나다)’의 동사원형 come이 쓰인 것은 모두 알맞으나, 완전한 절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사 that 뒤에 타동사 express의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(they intended to express)이 올 수 없으므로, 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것’을 나타내는 관계대명사 what이 뒤의 불완전한 절을 이끌어 동사 make의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루도록 that을 관계대명사 what으로 고친다.)
ⓑ is → are (콤마(,) 뒤에 전치사 through와 목적격 관계대명사 which가 쓰이고 완전한 절(actors‘ ~ younger)이 이어져 앞 절의 an AI-based program을 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이룬 것과, 관계사절의 주어 ’actors‘ ~ screen‘이 ’늙어 보이거나 더 젊어 보이게 만들어진‘ 대상이므로 수동태(be동사+p.p.)가 쓰여 be동사 뒤에 두 개의 과거분사가 등위접속사 or에 의해 병렬로 연결되고 과거분사 made 뒤에 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(형용사)(~을 …하게 만들다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘~ be made+보어(형용사)(~가 …하게 만들어지다)’를 이루는 비교급 형태의 형용사 younger가 이어진 것은 모두 알맞으나, 관계사절의 핵심주어인 actors‘ faces가 복수명사구이므로 수일치를 위해 단수형 be동사 is를 복수형인 are로 고친다.)
오답
ⓔ ’~라는 것이 예상된다‘라는 뜻으로 ’it is expected that+완전한 절‘ 형태의 ’가주어(it)-진주어(that절)‘ 구문이 쓰인 것과, 진주어절의 주어 this technique이 ’반영되는‘ 대상이므로 조동사 will과 함께 ’incorporate ~ in …(~을 …에 반영[추가]하다)‘의 수동 표현인 ’~ be incorporated in …(~가 …에 반영[추가]되다)‘이 쓰이고 be동사와 과거분사 사이에 부사 widely가 쓰여 뒤의 과거분사를 수식하는 것은 모두 알맞다.

body:
Several artificial intelligence (AI) technologies ⓐare described in films are now a reality. One of them ⓑis self-driving cars. In Total Recall, for example, the taxi driver is the vehicle’s computer system. The taxi is capable of driving ⓒit without any human intervention. ⓓHaving been seen that movie, many people wanted self-driving cars. Luckily, self-driving cars ⓔare being developed and certain versions are already on the road. Additionally, many other AI technologies from movies are either in use or ⓕunder development.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 세 개 찾아 기호를 쓰고, 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오. (단어를 추가하지는 말 것)
<기호> <알맞게 고친 표현>
(1) ______ → ______
(2) ______ → ______
(3) ______ → ______
solution:
ⓐ in films 뒤에 문장의 동사인 are가 있으므로 주어 자리에 쓰인 명사구 Several artificial intelligence (AI) technologies를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 수식을 받는 명사구가 ‘묘사되는’ 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 동사구 are described를 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 described로 고친다.
ⓒ 동명사 driving의 의미상 주어인 The taxi와 동명사의 목적어가 동일한 대상이므로, it을 재귀 용법의 재귀대명사 itself로 고친다.
ⓓ 완전한 절(many people wanted self-driving cars) 앞에 콤마(,)와 함께 분사구문이 올 수 있으며, 흐름상 주절 동사(wanted)가 나타내는 과거 시점 이전에 일어난 일에 해당하므로 완료형 분사구문(Having+p.p. ~)이 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 many people이 ‘본’ 주체이고 목적어로 명사구 that movie가 있으므로, 완료수동형 분사(Having+been+p.p.)가 아닌 완료능동형 분사(Having+p.p.)를 사용해 Having been seen을 Having seen으로 고친다.
오답
ⓕ 상관접속사 ’either A or B(A이거나 B인)‘에 의해 전치사구 in use와 병렬연결을 이루므로 전치사구 under development는 알맞다.

Minority Report, a film set in the year 2050, was released in 2002. It features AI-based advertisements that can identify individuals from a remote distance by scanning people’s eyes. There is a scene where the main character enters a shopping mall. After scanning him and identifying who he is, the advertising system ______. Nowadays, we frequently encounter personalized advertisements provided by AI. For instance, many online shopping malls, platforms for sharing videos, and social media use AI. Their AI systems provide us with advertisements based on our previous searches or other online behavior. Regarding the technology identifying people through scanning eyes, some devices have already been developed. However, those that do not use AI technology have a critical limitation. They can identify a person only if he or she is standing still. On the other hand, devices employing AI have overcome this limitation. They can scan people’s eyes when they are walking. There has been continuous development of this technology up until now.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: asks him to stand still for accurate scanning
offers products that may be appealing to him
deletes his previous online search history for his privacy
blocks unwanted advertisements from appearing on the screen
tracks his physical movements to prevent his entry to the mall
solution:
앞에서 광고 시스템이 그를 스캔해 그가 누구인지 식별한다고 했고, 뒤에는 오늘날 우리가 AI에 의해 제공되는 개인 맞춤형 광고를 자주 접하게 된다는 내용이 이어지므로, 영화의 주인공이 쇼핑몰에 들어가는 장면에서 광고 시스템이 그를 스캔해 그의 성향에 맞는 제품을 추천한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ② ‘그의 마음을 끌지도 모르는 제품들을 제안합니다’가 알맞다.
오답

③ 그의 사생활을 위해 그의 이전 온라인 검색 기록을 삭제합니다

reality incapable out of use
solution:
(A) 글 뒷부분에서 자율주행 자동차가 개발되고 있는 중이며 특정 모델은 이미 도로에서 운행되고 있다고 했으므로, 영화 속에서 묘사된 여러 인공지능(AI) 기술은 이제 현실이라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 reality(현실)가 알맞다.
fantasy 환상, 공상
(B) 영화 <Total Recall>에서 택시 기사는 그 차량의 컴퓨터 시스템이며 인간의 개입이 없다는 내용이 언급되므로, 스스로 운전할 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 capable(~할 수 있는)이 알맞다.
incapable ~할 수 없는
(C) 자율주행 자동차가 개발되고 있으며, 특정 모델은 이미 도로에서 운행되고 있다고 한 뒤에 Additionally(게다가)로 이어지므로, 영화 속의 많은 다른 AI 기술이 사용되거나 개발되고 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 in use(사용되고 있는)가 알맞다.
out of use 사용되지 않는

body:
AI in movies and our future
AI has been progressing rapidly over the years, and its potential is only beginning to be fully recognized. It is certain that AI will continue to play a significant role in more and more aspects of our lives. (A)______, these days, a lot of movies feature various kinds of AI. Some AI robots have personalities and emotionally engage with people in the same way that humans do. (B)______, some AI characters are physically indistinguishable from humans. ⓐ이런 영화들은 보기에 재밌을 뿐만 아니라 영감을 주기도 합니다. They show us what AI might be like in the future and how it could affect us. What AI technology from a movie do you think will be used in our lives in the future?

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말로 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: However Nonetheless
Otherwise For example
Accordingly Furthermore
Nevertheless Additionally
Consequently Still
solution:
(A) AI가 계속해서 우리 삶의 점점 더 많은 측면에서 중요한 역할을 할 것이라는 것이 확실하다는 이유를 앞에서 제시한 뒤, 요즘 많은 영화들이 다양한 종류의 AI를 특징으로 삼는다는 결과를 연결하므로, 인과관계를 나타내는 Accordingly(그에 따라, 그 결과로) 또는 Consequently(그 결과, 따라서)가 알맞다.
(B) 일부 AI 로봇이 성격을 가지고 있고 인간이 하는 방식으로 사람들과 감정적으로 소통한다고 한 뒤에 일부 AI 캐릭터는 신체적으로 인간과 구분이 안 된다는 추가적인 설명을 덧붙이므로, ’더욱이, 게다가‘라는 뜻의 Furthermore 또는 Additionally가 알맞다.
오답
① 하지만 그럼에도 불구하고
② 그렇지 않으면 예를 들어
④ 그럼에도 불구하고 더욱이, 게다가
⑤ 그 결과, 따라서 그래도

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• ‘not only A, but also B’ 형태의 상관접속사를 사용할 것
• 부사적 용법의 to부정사와 분사를 사용할 것

watch, inspire, these movies, fun

answer: These movies are not only fun to watch, but also inspiring.
solution:
⦁주어 자리에 명사구 These movies를 쓴 뒤, 복수명사구인 주어에 수일치한 복수형 be동사 are를 추가한다. 이어서 <조건>에 따라 ‘not only A, but also B(A뿐 아니라, B도)’ 형태의 상관접속사를 사용해 두 개의 보어가 병렬연결을 이루도록 한다.
⦁먼저 not only 뒤에 첫 번째 보어로 형용사 fun을 쓰고, <조건>에 따라 부사적 용법 중 형용사를 수식하는 to부정사를 사용해 watch를 to부정사인 to watch로 변형해 fun 뒤에 쓴다.
⦁콤마(,) 뒤에 but also를 연결하고 두 번째 보어를 쓰되, 주어 These movies가 ‘영감을 주는’ 주체이므로, 동사 inspire를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 inspiring으로 변형한다.

body:
2001: A Space Odyssey
This movie, set in 2001, realistically describes a group of scientists on a spaceship heading to another planet. However, it was released in 1968, a year prior to the first moon landing. This means that human imagination goes far beyond reality.

(A) Then, HAL-9000 makes a recommendation for the next step. The system could even draw logical conclusions and evaluate its decisions. The AI helper for a spaceship, which was only seen in the film at the time, has become a reality. In 2008, the International Space Station, a large spacecraft orbiting Earth, started to use an AI robot named CIMON.

(B) It is a floating spherical robot that can move around inside the spacecraft. CIMON, weighing only 5 kg, serves as a competent AI assistant for astronauts. The robot assists astronauts in more effectively accomplishing complex tasks by offering advice during experiments and work. It is also able to record and film the astronauts’ activities when asked.

(C) In the movie, the ship has a computer system, called “HAL-9000.” It provided the audience with the chance to understand AI. It could operate and regulate all of the spacecraft’s systems and help the astronauts conduct experiments by analyzing data. In one scene, the astronauts and HAL-9000 carry out a conversation about a faulty component of the spacecraft.

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 영화 <2001: A Space Odyssey>는 최초의 달 착륙보다 1년 먼저 개봉되었으며 이는 인간의 상상력이 현실을 훨씬 넘어섬을 의미한다는 내용의 주어진 글에 이어, 이 영화에 등장하는 HAL-9000이라는 컴퓨터 시스템의 역할과 기능을 설명하고 그것이 우주선의 결함이 있는 부품에 관해 우주비행사들과 대화하는 장면을 소개하는 (C), Then(그런 다음)을 사용해 앞선 대화 이후 HAL-9000이 하는 일로 다음 단계에 대한 권고를 전한다는 것과 추가적으로 수행할 수 있는 일들을 소개한 뒤, 당시 영화에서만 볼 수 있었던 우주선의 AI 도우미가 2008년에 국제우주정거장에서 CIMON이라는 AI 로봇으로 현실화했다고 설명하는 (A), CIMON을 It(그것)으로 가리켜 그것이 우주선 내부를 돌아다닐 수 있는 공중에 떠다니는 구 모양의 로봇이라고 설명을 이어가는 (B)로 이어지는 것이 알맞다.

But the young boy’s eyes followed the path to a rocky bay that was a bit farther away. ⓐFeeling that his attention was elsewhere, his mother worried about the ideas that he might be getting. The boy, noticing his mother’s concern, smiled at her and continued following along. He kept ⓑglancing over his shoulder at the wild bay, however, imagining what it might hold.

[2]
The next morning, Jerry’s mother asked him if he was interested in trying another beach. He first answered no, regretting that he had made his mother ⓒto think that he was bored with their usual place. As they were walking, however, he suddenly changed his mind and said, “I’d like to go and have a look at those rocks down there.” She gave the idea some thought. The area he was pointing to looked somewhat dangerous, but she decided ⓓwhat it would be fine to let him go on his own. As his mother walked away, Jerry felt like running after her again and enjoying the beach as they had always done, but he ⓔdid not.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓒ to think → think (과거완료 had made는 사역동사로 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/p.p.)’의 형태로 쓰이며 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동 관계일 때 동사원형을, 수동 관계일 때 과거분사(p.p.)를 쓴다. 여기서 목적어 his mother가 ‘생각하는‘ 주체이므로 목적격보어 자리의 to think를, 능동을 나타내는 동사원형 think로 고친다.)
ⓓ what → that (완전한 절(it ~ own)을 이끌어 동사 decided의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)
*ⓓ는 원래 지문에서 생략되어 있음
오답
ⓐ 완전한 절(his mother ~ getting)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 his mother가 ‘느끼는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 Feeling은 적절하다.
ⓑ ‘계속 ~하다‘의 의미로 'keep -ing'의 형태를 취하므로 동사 kept 뒤에 이어지는 glancing은 적절하다.
ⓔ 그녀를 뒤따라가서 해변을 즐기지 않았다는 의미의 ‘did not run after her again and enjoy the beach’에서 앞 절과 반복되는 어구인 run after her again and enjoy the beach가 생략된 것으로, 대동사의 부정형 did not은 적절하다.

Feeling rejected, Jerry watched the boys from a distance and noticed that they were underwater for a long time. He started counting the seconds. At fifty, he started to worry. At one hundred, he wondered whether he should yell for help. But around one hundred and fifty, he realized that they were in fact swimming through some rocks in the water and coming out the other side. After they left, he tried to do what they had done, but when he tried to open his eyes to see underwater, his eyes stung from the salty water. (A)그러나 자신의 눈을 감은 채로, 그는 소년들이 헤엄쳐 통과한 굴을 볼 수 없었다. His only option was to give up and go home.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.

<조건>
• ‘with 분사구문’으로 시작할 것
• 적절한 관계대명사를 사용할 것
• 과거완료를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것

<보기>
unable, eyes, the tunnel, see, close, swim through

→ ______ ______ ______ ______, however, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: With his eyes closed, he was unable to see the tunnel that[which] the boys had swum through
solution:
*본문에서는 that이 쓰였음
• ‘with 분사구문’으로 시작해야 하므로, ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)’의 형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 전치사 With, 명사구 his eyes를 쓰고 his eyes가 ‘감긴’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 closed를 쓴다.
• 주어 he를 쓰고 ‘be unable+to부정사(~할 수 없다)’를 사용하여 was unable to를 쓴다. ‘굴을 보다’를 뜻하도록 see the tunnel을 이어 쓴다. 명사구 the tunnel을 수식하는 관계사절을 영작하기 위해 관계대명사 that 또는 which를 쓴다.
• 관계사절의 주어 the boys를 쓰고 그가 볼 수 없었던 과거 시점보다 소년들이 헤엄친 것이 먼저 발생한 일이므로 swim의 과거완료형 had swum을 쓴다. ‘~을 통과해’를 뜻하는 전치사 through를 이어 쓴다.

① 한 어린 소년의 숨겨진 수중 굴의 성공적 발견

body:
Jerry soon began to feel restless being back at the beach with his mother, and he worried that all the practice he ⓐhad put in would go to waste. The next day, he decided to go back to the rocky bay. He now spent his days exploring the tunnel at the bay and ⓑpracticing his breathing whenever he was back with his mother. He knew that (A)______ would help him conquer the tunnel that had defeated him.

After a few days, his mother told him ⓒthat they would soon need to return home. This news urged him to go back to the bay. He felt that he absolutely needed to go through the tunnel before they went home. (B)______, however, made him think that just practicing some more and trying again next year might be wiser.

But even after reaching that conclusion, he found himself sitting on the rock with a longing to overcome his fear and ⓓconquered the tunnel. It would be now or never. He decided to try once more. His hands were shaking, but he placed them firmly at his sides. He looked up at the sky, ⓔfilled his lungs with air, and then sank fast into the ocean.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓓ conquered → conquer 또는 to conquer (흐름상 ‘두려움을 극복하고 굴을 정복하려는 갈망’을 뜻하므로 명사구 a longing을 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사 to overcome과 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어야 한다. 따라서 conquered를 to부정사 to conquer 또는 to를 생략한 동사원형 conquer로 고친다.)
*ⓓ는 원래 지문에서 conquer로 쓰였음
오답
ⓐ 주절의 시점인 그가 걱정한 과거 시점(worried)보다 그가 연습을 한 것이 더 먼저 일어난 일이므로, 과거완료 had put은 적절하다.
ⓑ 'spent+목적어+-ing(~하는데 (시간/돈)을 썼다)‘를 이루는 exploring과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬 연결되었으므로 practicing을 적절하다.
ⓒ 완전한 절(they ~ home)을 이끌어 동사 told의 직접목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다.
ⓔ 등위접속사 and에 의해 주어 He에 이어지는 과거동사 looked, sank와 병렬 구조를 이루고 있으므로 과거동사 filled는 적절하다.

blind courage / His inner anxiety
outside support / His fear of failure
blind courage / His confidence

solution:
(A) Jerry는 매일 굴을 탐험하고 호흡을 연습하며 굴을 정복하기 위한 준비를 계속하고 있다고 했으므로 준비하는 것이 굴을 정복하는 데 도움이 된다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 thorough preparation(철저한 준비)이 적절하다.
본문변형 원래 (A)는 being prepared이었음
(B) Jerry가 더 연습하고 다음 해에 다시 시도하는 것이 나을지도 모른다고 생각하지만, 곧이어 두려움을 극복하고 굴을 정복하려는 갈망으로 바위에 앉아 있는 자신의 모습을 발견한다고 했으므로, 그가 앞서 느낀 마음은 자신의 도전을 망설이게 하는 불안 또는 두려움이라고 볼 수 있다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 His inner anxiety(그의 내면의 불안), His fear of failure(실패에 대한 그의 두려움)가 적절하다.

body:
On the first morning of their summer vacation, a young English boy named Jerry and his mother walked together towards their usual beach. But the young boy’s eyes followed the path to a rocky bay that was a bit farther away. Feeling that his attention was elsewhere, his mother worried about the ideas that he might be getting. The boy, noticing his mother’s (A)indifference, smiled at her and continued following along. He kept glancing over his shoulder at the wild bay, however, imagining what it might hold.

The next morning, Jerry’s mother asked him if he was (B)interested in trying another beach. He first answered no, (C)regretting that he had made his mother think that he was bored with their usual place. As they were walking, however, he suddenly (D)changed his mind and said, “I’d like to go and have a look at those rocks down there.” She gave the idea some thought. The area he was pointing to looked somewhat (E)dangerous, but she decided it would be fine to let him go on his own. As his mother walked away, Jerry felt like running after her again and enjoying the beach as they had always done, but he did not.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: (A) indifference(무관심) → concern(걱정)

body:
He soon found the entrance to the tunnel. He took the edges of the hole in his hands and drew (A)[him / himself] into it. It was pitch black, but he kept counting, just as he had practiced. Fifty, fifty-one, fifty-two… Soon he reached a hundred, a hundred and one… He kept moving through the tunnel, and when he thought he couldn’t last any longer, he spotted a crack of light at the end. The feeling of victory filled him as he realized that with a few more strokes, he would be coming out the other side. He felt like he was running out of air, but he kept kicking and thinking just a little bit more!

Finally, his hands found the exit of the tunnel, and he swam out into the open sea. At first, he started to gasp like a fish out of water, but after some time, his heart quieted and his eyes cleared. He had made it. After resting a short while on the warm rock, he got on his feet and walked back home. His mother’s eyes lit up, as she was happy (B)[seeing / to see] him back. “Did you have a nice morning?” she asked. Jerry replied with pride, “Mom, I can stay underwater for two minutes, three minutes, at least!” His mom thought about telling him (C)[to rest / resting] for the remainder of the day, but she didn’t have to. He was now happy to stay home and rest. Going to the bay was no longer important to him.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

(A) (B) (C)
choices: him / seeing / to rest
himself / seeing / resting
him / to see / to rest
himself / to see / to rest
himself / to see / resting
solution:
(A) 주어 He와 drew의 목적어가 동일인을 가리키므로 재귀대명사 himself가 알맞다.
(B) 감정 형용사 happy 뒤에 쓰여 ‘~해서 행복하다’의 의미로 감정의 원인을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to see가 알맞다.
(C) telling의 목적어 him에 이어지는 목적격보어 자리로, ‘tell+목적어+목적격보어(…가 ~하게 시키다[말하다])’의 구조를 취하는 tell은 목적격보어 to부정사를 취하므로, telling의 목적격보어 자리에 to부정사 to rest가 적절하다.

solution:

② 굴을 통과해 나아가는 동안, Jerry는 반대편 끝에서 가느다란 빛의 틈을 발견했다.
③ 굴의 출구에 도달한 후, Jerry는 탁 트인 바다로 나왔고 호흡을 다시 조절하는 데 시간이 좀 걸렸다.
④ 자신의 성취를 자랑스러워하며, Jerry는 어머니에게 자신이 물속에서 2분 또는 심지어 3분 동안 머물 수 있다고 말했다.

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘유일한 선택지는 포기하고 집으로 가는 것이었다.’라는 뜻으로 이 문장 앞에는 Jerry가 무언가를 시도하지만 그 시도가 어떤 난관에 부딪혀 더 이상 진행할 수 없는 상황이 와야 한다. (D) 앞에서 소년들이 한 행동을 따라 하려고 했으나 소금기 있는 물 때문에 눈이 따가웠고, (E) 앞에서 눈을 감은 채로는 소년들이 헤엄쳐 지난 굴을 볼 수 없었다고 했으므로, 더 이상 굴을 통과할 수 없다고 판단한 Jerry가 결국 포기하고 집으로 돌아가기로 했다는 주어진 문장이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다. 따라서 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (E)이다.

body:
Reaching the rocky bay, he started swimming but soon felt somewhat lonely being so far from his mother. After some time, he encountered a group of local boys who were diving from the rocks. They were around his age, and he desperately wanted to become friends with them. He swam closer, and they turned to watch him. One smiled and waved him over. They showed him how to dive from the rocks into the deep water. He tried diving with them, but he was too afraid. Noticing his hesitation, the boys soon lost interest. Jerry tried calling out to them in the local language, “Bonjour! Merci! Monsieur, monsieur!” but they ignored him and swam away.

Feeling rejected, Jerry watched the boys from a distance and noticed that they were underwater for a long time. He started counting the seconds. At fifty, he started to worry. At one hundred, he wondered whether he should yell for help. But around one hundred and fifty, he realized that they were in fact swimming through some rocks in the water and coming out the other side. After they left, he tried to do what they had done, but when he tried to open his eyes to see underwater, his eyes stung from the salty water. With his eyes closed, however, he was unable to see the tunnel that the boys had swum through. His only option was to give up and go home.

Jerry approached the local boys in the hope of making friends, but they became (A)______ to him when he was too frightened to dive with them; afterward, he discovered that they were swimming through an underwater tunnel but gave up trying to (B)______ them because of the pain caused by the salty water.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

(A) (B)
choices: indifferent / help
hospitable / imitate
indifferent / copy
hospitable / follow
friendly / assist
solution:
요약문 Jerry는 현지 소년들과 친구가 되기를 바라며 다가갔지만, 너무 두려워 그들과 함께 다이빙하지 못하자 그들은 그에게 (A)무관심해졌다; 이후 그는 소년들이 수중 터널을 통과해 헤엄치고 있다는 사실을 발견했지만, 소금물로 인한 고통 때문에 소년들을 (B)따라 하려는 시도를 포기했다.
오답
① 무관심한 / 돕다
② 환대하는, 친절한 / 따라하다
④ 환대하는, 친절한 / 따라 가다
⑤ 친절한, 우호적인 / 돕다

He tried to enter it, but the darkness and the feeling of seaweed on his skin frightened him. He gave up and decided to practice holding his breath underwater instead.

From that day forward, every morning, the boy left his mother at the beach and came to the rocks to practice his breathing and diving. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.

<조건>
• 명사절 접속사를 사용할 것
• 사역동사를 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 19단어로 영작할 것

at, have, usual beach, join, worry about, tell, have

→ ______
answer: His mother told him that she was worried about him and had him join her at their usual beach.
solution:
• 주어 His mother, 동사 told를 쓰고, told는 ‘tell+간접목적어(사람)+직접목적어(명사절)’의 4형식 구문으로 쓰일 수 있으므로 told 뒤에 간접목적어 him을 쓰고, 직접목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 영작하기 위해 명사절 접속사 that을 쓴다.
• that절의 주어 she를 쓰고 she가 ‘걱정된’ 대상이므로 수동태 was worried, 전치사 about, 목적어 him을 차례대로 쓴다.
• 등위접속사 and 뒤에 사역동사 had를 쓰고, ‘사역동사have+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/p.p.)’의 구조로 쓰이며 목적어 him이 ‘함께 하는’ 주체이므로 목적격보어로 능동 관계를 나타내는 동사원형 join을 쓴다. join의 목적어 her를 쓰고 ‘그들이 평소에 가던 해변에’를 뜻하도록 수식어 at their usual beach를 이어 쓴다.

body:
The next morning, Jerry’s mother asked him ⓐthat he was interested in trying another beach. He first answered no, regretting that he had made his mother think that he was bored with their usual place. As they were walking, however, he suddenly changed his mind and said, “I’d like to go and have a look at those rocks down there.” She gave the idea some thought. The area ⓑhe was pointing to looked somewhat dangerous, but she decided it would be fine to let him go on his own. As his mother walked away, Jerry felt like running after her again and enjoying the beach as they ⓒhad always done, but he did not.

ⓓReaching the rocky bay, he started swimming but soon felt somewhat lonely ⓔbeing so far from his mother. After some time, he encountered a group of local boys who were diving from the rocks. They were around his age, and he desperately wanted to become friends with them. He swam closer, and they turned to watch him. One smiled and waved him over. They showed him how to dive from the rocks into the deep water. He tried diving with them, but he was too afraid. Noticing his hesitation, the boys soon lost interest. Jerry tried calling out to them in the local language, “Bonjour! Merci! Monsieur, monsieur!” but they ignored him and swam away.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ에 대한 설명으로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: ‘다른 해변에 가 보는 데 관심이 있는지’를 묻는 간접화법이 쓰인 문장이므로 that을 명사절 접속사 if(~인지 아닌지)로 고쳐야 한다.
ⓑ: 장소를 나타내는 명사구 The area를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절로, he 앞에 관계부사 where가 생략되었다.
ⓒ: 그들이 항상 해변을 즐겼던 것은 Jerry가 느낀(felt) 과거 시점보다 먼저 일어났던 일이므로 과거완료 had always done이 쓰였다.
ⓓ: 시간을 나타내는 분사구문으로 부사절 When he reached로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.
ⓔ: ‘~해서’라는 뜻의 이유를 나타내는 분사구문으로 부사절 as he was로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.
solution: ⓑ 전치사 to의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(he was pointing to)이 선행사 The area를 수식하고 있으므로, he 앞에는 목적격 관계대명사 that 또는 which가 생략되었다.

But even after reaching that conclusion, he found himself sitting on the rock with a longing to ______. It would be now or never. He decided to try once more. His hands were shaking, but he placed them firmly at his sides. He looked up at the sky, filled his lungs with air, and then sank fast into the ocean.

body:
Old pictures often depict people ⓐsinging together in church, with their families at home or with companions at community events. Unfortunately, these scenes have become less common nowadays. There could be several reasons ⓑwhy singing in a group has become less common. First, we spend less time in groups these days and are more isolated. Technology has made ⓒit easier to enjoy music individually rather than in a larger setting. Instead of being played in a large setting and under social circumstances, music has become something ⓓenjoying privately on our personal play devices. Second, our society is more diverse, so we don’t always know the same songs. The list of music that is common to different groups of people is becoming shorter. We might also worry more about our social image, and singing in front of others can make us feel awkward. Lastly, we have more entertainment options today than in the past when people gathered around the piano or the guitar just because ⓔit was fun to do so.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓓ enjoying → enjoyed (부정대명사 something을 수식하는 분사 자리이며, something이 ‘즐겨지는’ 대상이므로 enjoying을 수동의 의미인 과거분사 enjoyed로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 동사 depict의 목적어 people을 수식하는 분사 자리이며, people이 ‘노래하는’ 주체이므로, 능동의 의미인 현재분사 singing은 적절하다.
ⓑ 완전한 절(singing ~ common)을 이끌어 이유를 뜻하는 명사구 several reasons를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 관계부사 why는 적절하다.
ⓒ 동사 has made, 목적격보어 easier, to부정사구 to enjoy music individually와 함께 ‘make+가목적어(it)+목적격보어+진목적어(to부정사(구))’의 ‘가목적어-진목적어’ 구문을 이루고 있으므로 목적어 자리의 가목적어 it은 적절하다.
ⓔ 진주어 to do so에 상응하는 가주어 자리이므로 주어 자리의 it은 적절하다.

body:
Although group singing has become less common, it’s an activity that can be beneficial. (A) So why does group singing make us feel so good? (B) Decades of research have shown that singing is good for you on many levels by reducing stress and increasing the release of happiness hormones such as endorphins, dopamine, and serotonin. (C) It brings people closer together and helps create bonds that can support self-esteem in a more stable way. (D) The sense of belonging and purpose created in the moment makes us feel connected to others and to something greater. (E) Thus, it’s no surprise that people who sing together have healthier minds and more readily participate in their communities. A few studies have reported that people who sang in choirs were more optimistic, less lonely, had stronger relationships, and were more likely to contribute positively to their communities than those who didn’t. The good news is that people can enjoy these benefits even when they’re singing with others online. Being together is the key.
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
Singing with others has additional benefits.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘다른 사람들과 함께 노래하는 것에는 추가적인 이점이 있다.’라는 뜻으로, 이 문장 앞에는 다른 사람들과 함께 노래하기와 관련된 이점이 제시되고 이 문장 뒤에는 다른 사람들과 함께 노래하기의 또 다른 이점이 이어져야 한다. (C) 앞에서 노래하기의 이점으로 스트레스 감소와 행복 호르몬의 분비 증가가 처음 언급되었고, (C) 뒤에서 그것(It)이 사람들을 더 가깝게 만들고 자존감을 안정적으로 뒷받침하는 유대감을 형성한다는 내용이 이어지므로, It이 가리키는 것이 Singing with others(다른 사람과 함께 노래하기)임을 알 수 있으며 그것의 또 다른 이점이 제시되고 있으므로, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (C)이다.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: what stay inspiring
that have stayed inspired
what stay inspired
that stay inspiring
what have stayed inspired
solution:
(A) ‘~한 것’이라는 뜻으로 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(you love)을 이끌어 관계사절의 동사 love의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what이 적절하다.
(B) 현재 사실의 반대 상황, 즉 여기서는 앞 문장에서 제시한 공연의 목적을 반대로 가정하기 위해 ‘if+주어+과거동사(wasn't) ~’의 가정법 과거의 부사절로 시작하고 있으므로, 주절에는 ‘주어+조동사 과거형(would)+동사원형 ~’이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 you would의 축약형 you'd에 이어지는 동사원형 stay가 알맞다.
참고로 가정법 과거에서 주어에 상관없이 if절에는 be동사 were을 쓰는 것이 원칙이지만, 실제로 was도 많이 사용되고 있다.
(C) 동사 get에 이어지는 주격보어 자리이며, 주어 singers가 ‘영감을 받는’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 형태의 형용사 inspired가 적절하다.

body:
Korean pop music fans are famous for their singing-along during concerts, and their participation in the concert sometimes goes beyond the conventional expectations of musicians. Artists ⓐperform in Korea are often impressed by the audience singing, ⓑcalled tte-chang. What’s so impressive is ⓒthat they memorize entire songs in English or even in other foreign languages. Before going to a concert, loyal fans look at the set list, memorize the lyrics of all the songs, and ⓓplan a tte-chang event to make their concert experience special. In this way, Korean fans show that they really care about the music and the musicians. There are countries where silent appreciation is expected from the concert audience, but at Korean pop music concerts, enthusiastic participation in tte-chang often ⓔaccompanying by dancing is the norm.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 두 개 골라 기호를 쓰고 알맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.
기호 알맞게 고친 표현
(1) ______ : ______
(2) ______ : ______
solution:
ⓐ 뒤에 동사 are가 있으므로 주어 Artists를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, Artists가 ‘공연하는’ 주체이므로 perform을 능동의 의미인 현재분사 performing으로 고친다.
ⓔ 뒤에 동사 is가 있으므로 주어부 enthusiastic participation in tte-chang을 수식하는 분사 자리이며, enthusiastic participation in tte-chang가 춤이 ‘동반되는’ 대상이므로 accompanying을 수동의 의미인 과거분사 accompanied로 고친다.
오답
ⓑ 콤마(,) 앞의 명사구 the audience singing을 부연 설명하는 분사구를 이루는 자리이며, the audience singing이 떼창이라고 ‘불리는’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미인 과거분사 called는 적절하다.
ⓒ 뒤에 완전한 절(they ~ languages)을 이끌어 is의 보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다.

Before going to a concert, loyal fans look at the set list, memorize the lyrics of all the songs, and ⓓplan a tte-chang event to make their concert experience special. In this way, Korean fans show that they really care about the music and the musicians. There are countries where silent appreciation is expected from the concert audience, but at Korean pop music concerts, enthusiastic participation in tte-chang often ⓔaccompanying by dancing is the norm.

why silence and respect matter during live musical performances

body:
Although group singing has become less common, it’s an activity that can be beneficial. So why does group singing make us feel so good? Decades of research have shown that singing is good for you on many levels by reducing stress and increasing the release of happiness hormones such as endorphins, dopamine, and serotonin. Singing with others has additional benefits. It brings people closer together and helps create bonds that can support self-esteem in a more stable way. (A)그 순간에 형성되는 소속감과 목적의식은 우리가 다른 사람들과 또 더 큰 무언가와 연결되어 있다고 느끼게 만든다. Thus, it’s no surprise that people who sing together have healthier minds and more readily participate in their communities. A few studies have reported that people who sang in choirs were more optimistic, less lonely, had stronger relationships, and were more likely to contribute positively to their communities than those who didn’t. The good news is that people can enjoy these benefits even when they’re singing with others online. Being together is the key.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• 분사구를 사용할 것
• 사역동사 make를 사용할 것
• 전치사구를 병렬 연결할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 20단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
feel, belonging, connect to, create, the sense, great, others, purpose, something, the moment
→ ______
answer: The sense of belonging and purpose created in the moment makes us feel connected to others and to something greater.
solution:
• 주어 The sense of belonging and purpose(소속감과 목적의식)가 ‘형성된’ 대상이므로 동사 create를 수동의 의미인 과거분사 created로 변형하여 쓴다.
• 동사 make를 주어의 핵심어 The sense에 수일치한 단수동사 makes로 변형하여 쓰고, ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/p.p.)’의 사역동사 구문으로 쓰이며, 목적어 us가 ‘느끼는 주체이므로 능동을 나타내는 동사원형 feel을 목적격보어로 이어 쓴다.
• 동사원형 feel에 이어지는 보어 자리에, 의미상 주어인 us가 다른 사람들과 ‘연결되었다’고 느끼는 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 형태의 형용사 connected와 전치사 to, 목적어 others를 쓴다. 등위접속사 and 뒤에 connected와 연결되는 전치사 to와 부정대명사 something을 쓰고, 형용사 great의 비교급 greater를 something 뒤에 이어 쓴다.

body:
Old pictures often depict people singing together in church, with their families at home or with companions at community events. Unfortunately, these scenes have become less common nowadays. There could be several reasons why singing in a group has become less common. First, we spend less time (A)[individually / in groups] these days and are more isolated. Technology has made it easier to enjoy music individually rather than in a larger setting. Instead of being played in a large setting and under social circumstances, music has become something enjoyed privately on our personal play devices. Second, our society is more diverse, so we don’t always know (B)[a variety of / the same] songs. The list of music that is common to different groups of people is becoming shorter. We might also worry more about our social image, and singing in front of others can make us feel (C)[awkward / comfortable]. Lastly, we have more entertainment options today than in the past when people gathered around the piano or the guitar just because it was fun to do so.
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: individually a variety of awkward
in groups the same awkward
in groups a variety of comfortable
individually the same awkward
in groups the same comfortable
solution:
(A) 앞에서 사람들이 함께 노래하는 모습이 흔했던 과거와 다르게 오늘날에 집단으로 노래하는 일이 줄어든 이유를 이어서 설명하고 있으므로, 집단으로 함께 보내는 시간이 더 적다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 in groups(집단으로)가 적절하다.
individually 개인적으로
(B) 오늘날 우리 사회가 더 다양해졌고 뒤에 공통으로 아는 음악의 목록이 더 짧아지고 있다고 언급되고 있으므로, 우리가 항상 똑같은 노래를 아는 건 아니라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 the same(똑같은)이 적절하다.
a variety of 다양한
(C) 집단으로 노래하는 것이 덜 흔해진 이유 중 하나로, 우리는 우리의 사회적 이미지를 더 걱정하기에 남들 앞에서 노래하는 것은 우리에게 어색한 기분이 들게 할 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 awkward(어색한)이 적절하다.
comfortable 편안한

body:
The communal nature of music remains and is vividly demonstrated at live concerts. Whether you’re in the crowd at the Mercury Lounge or Madison Square Garden, the point is to gather with people who love what you love.
(A) This creates a sense of belonging and a strong bond with the musician. Many musicians remember the first time their audience sang along with them.
(B) When you sing along to songs at a concert, you don’t just listen to the music; you participate in it, “completing” the musical experience.
(C) If the point wasn’t to gather or to share in the mass performance, you’d just stay home and listen to music by yourself.
Maybe it means they have reached the point in their career where they have become popular. Even singers with long, successful careers feel energized by the power of the crowd and get inspired for their next music project.
위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 라이브 콘서트에서 음악의 공동체적 특성이 생생하게 드러나며, 그 요점(the point)은 여러분이 사랑하는 것을 사랑하는 사람들이 함께 모인다는 것이라는 주어진 글 뒤에, 앞에서 제시한 공연의 목적(the point)을 반대로 가정하여 모이거나 대규모 공연에 함께 참여하는 것이 목적이 아니라면 집에서 혼자 음악을 들을 것이라고 언급함으로써 콘서트에서 사람들이 함께 모이는 이유를 강조하는 (C), 콘서트에서 노래를 따라 부르는 것이 단순히 음악을 듣는 것이 아니라 음악에 직접 참여하여 음악적 경험을 완성하는 것이라고 설명하는 (B), (B)에서 언급한 음악적 경험에 직접 참여하는 것을 This(이것)로 이어받아 이러한 참여가 소속감을 형성하고 음악가와 강한 유대감을 만들어 낸다고 설명하는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

• to부정사를 사용할 것

<보기>
heal, happy, feel, connect, can, sing, healthy, a way, and help
→ ______
answer: Singing with others can be a way to heal and help us feel connected, happy, and healthy.
solution:
• 동사 sing을 동명사 Singing으로 변형하고 쓰고 ‘다른 사람들과 함께’를 뜻하도록 with others를 이어 써서 주어부 Singing with others를 완성한다.
• 조동사 can과 be를 쓰고 주격보어 a way를 이어 쓴다. 명사구 a way를 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사구를 영작한다. ‘우리를 치유하고 우리에게 도움이 되는 방법’을 뜻하도록 heal을 to부정사 to heal로 변형하여 쓰고, 등위접속사 and, 동사원형 help, heal과 help의 공유목적어 us를 차례대로 쓴다.
• help는 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/to부정사)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이며, 단어 수 제한에 따라 목적어 us에 이어지는 목적격보어 자리에 동사원형 feel을 쓴다. ‘연결되고 행복하며 건강하다고 느끼는’을 뜻하도록 feel에 이어지는 보어 자리에 ‘A, B, and C‘의 병렬 구조가 되도록 형용사 connected, happy, 등위접속사 and, 형용사 healthy를 차례대로 쓴다.

When Aaron arrived at the orphanage, two men were playing a board game with bottle caps at the gate. One of the men recognized him and called out, “Good afternoon, Aaron!”
“Hello,” Aaron answered shyly.
“I’m Samuel. Did you come to visit Zambezi?”
“Zambezi?”
“It’s the name we gave the little elephant.”
So the elephant was alive! Aaron beamed, his heart beating ⓐfaster. Samuel motioned for him to follow. Zambezi lay on a bed of straw in a corner of a stall. He looked like a wrinkled bag of bones, covered by blankets. He seemed to be having ⓑtrouble breathing. (C) 주어 Aaron에 이어지는 과거 동사 saw와 등위 접속사 and로 병렬 연결되는 과거 동사 overheard가 적절하다.

body:
The sun was a glowing red ball in the eastern sky when Aaron left his family’s hut. Aaron headed to Lion’s Inn, (A)[where / which] he had been working for a few months. As Aaron approached the gate, he was startled by a strange noise. He couldn’t believe his eyes — a small elephant was flailing around in the swimming pool! The elephant held its trunk in the air and kicked wildly.
Aaron glanced around nervously for the mother elephant. But there were no other elephants in sight, and this one needed help fast. Aaron raced to the cottage where the gardener slept. “Help! Hurry!” he called. He ran to the pool shed and grabbed a rope and a rake. When he got back, the manager, the gardener, the cook, and other workers had gathered by the pool.
After Aaron threw the rake down on the deck, he jumped straight into the water. The little elephant snorted and splashed wildly. Aaron got close to it with the rope. One of the boys who worked in the kitchen jumped in, too. Together they were able to get the rope under the elephant’s belly. With the cook and the gardener (B)[pulled / pulling] from the edge, Aaron and the other boy finally managed to drag, pull, and push the exhausted animal onto the deck. He watched the elephant, lying on its side, shaking. It looked straight at Aaron and blinked.
A truck pulled up, and some men in uniform stepped out. Aaron saw them waving their arms and (C)[overheard / overhearing] bits and pieces of their conversation with the inn manager: “only one month old … found the mother … killed … poachers ….” The men loaded the elephant into the truck.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Upon reaching the entrance, Aaron was surprised by an unfamiliar sound and could hardly believe his eyes.
Realizing that the little elephant needed immediate help, Aaron rushed to the hut and asked for assistance.
By the time Aaron returned with a rope and a rake, several inn employees were already beside the pool.
After throwing the rake onto the deck, Aaron dived straight into the water as the young elephant trumpeted and splashed frantically.
The rescued baby elephant was so worn out that it lay on its side, unable to meet Aaron’s gaze.
solution:
요리사와 정원사, Aaron과 다른 소년은 기진맥진한 코끼리를 간신히 덱 위로 끌어 올렸고, 코끼리는 옆으로 누워 떨면서 Aaron을 바라보며 눈을 깜박였다고 언급하고 있으므로, ⑤ ‘구조된 아기 코끼리는 너무 지쳐서 그것은 옆으로 누운 채 Aaron의 시선을 마주할 수 없었다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 출입구에 도착하자마자, Aaron은 낯선 소리에 놀랐고 자신의 눈을 거의 믿을 수 없었다.
② 작은 코끼리에게 즉각적인 도움이 필요하다는 것을 깨닫고, Aaron은 오두막으로 서둘러 달려가 도움을 요청했다.
③ Aaron이 밧줄과 갈퀴를 가지고 돌아왔을 때는 여관 직원 여러 명이 이미 수영장 옆에 와 있었다.
④ 갈퀴를 덱 위로 던진 후, Aaron은 어린 코끼리가 코를 울리고 미친 듯이 첨벙거리는 동안 곧장 물속으로 뛰어들었다.

body:
Bezi was getting better each day. His sunken skin slowly gave way to a round belly, and his cheeks filled out, too. Before long, he was moving around more, even trying to leave his stall. (A)The other orphans approached curiously, prodding him all over with their trunks.
Eventually, Bezi was allowed to venture outside. (B)He seemed to love the older orphans, following them around the pen and imitating their behavior. (C)Imitating the behavior of other animals can sometimes prevent young animals from developing independent ways of responding to unfamiliar situations.
Bezi’s eyes lit up as he splashed in the mud. And whenever he spotted Aaron, he came running over to search for a bottle with his trunk.
(D)Aaron still sleeps near any little elephant that needs him, keeping watch and feeding him or her around the clock. (E)Aaron dreams of a time when all orphan elephants will roam the African plains as free, wild animals — when there will no longer be a need for elephant orphanages.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: Bezi는 날마다 더 좋아져 더 많이 움직이고 바깥으로 나가 다른 고아 코끼리들을 따라다니며 그들의 행동을 흉내 내고, Aaron은 여전히 자신을 필요로 하는 아기 코끼리들을 밤낮으로 돌보면서 모든 고아 코끼리들이 자유로운 야생 동물로 아프리카 평원을 돌아다닐 날을 꿈꾼다고 설명하고 있으므로, 다른 동물들의 행동을 모방하는 것의 단점을 언급한 (C) ‘다른 동물들의 행동을 모방하는 것은 때때로 어린 동물들이 낯선 상황에 대처하는 독자적인 방식을 발달시키는 것을 방해할 수 있다.’는 전체 글의 흐름과 관계없다.

body:
Aaron awoke from his thoughts when the head keeper found him and Samuel and said, “So, you are the boy who rescued Bezi from the pool. How would you like to work here? We’re short on workers, and ⓐit seems you’re good with animals.”
When Aaron went back home and told his mother about the job, she said, “Your father would be proud, as I am. We’ll miss you, but we’ll manage. And, of course, you’ll come home on your days off.” And just like that, his decision was made.
The first few nights at the orphanage ⓑwas not easy. Aaron hardly slept at all. With every snort Bezi gave, Aaron sat straight up, (A)______. He missed the familiar sounds and smells of home, especially his sister’s soft, rhythmic breathing as she slept near him. But it wasn’t long before he began to find comfort in the closeness of Bezi and the warm smell of straw.
Samuel and the other keepers showed him tricks to get Bezi to swallow pills and how to take blood for the veterinarian to check. Bezi was still very sick, ⓒwas slept most of the day in the quiet stable. But now, at least, he drank the bottles that the keepers offered him every few hours.
Aaron recorded the amounts ⓓthat Bezi drank. He held Bezi’s head as the veterinarian took his temperature or administered medicine. He even recorded the elephant’s bowel movements. He felt proud when Bezi finished his milk and covered him with a blanket at night. “I’m turning into an elephant mother,” he joked to Samuel.
But mothers worry, and so did Aaron. Each time he saw the veterinarian ⓔfrowns, Aaron’s stomach got tense. When Bezi spat out his medicine, Aaron feared that he’d never get better. One morning, he noticed that Bezi’s heartbeat was very, very slow compared to his own. Samuel reassured him ⓕwhom all elephants have a slower heartbeat than humans. But that didn’t stop Aaron from worrying. Bezi still had a fever. Aaron knew only too well that medicine couldn’t cure everything.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ, ⓕ이다.
ⓑ was → were (주절의 주어 The first few nights at the orphanage의 핵심 단어인 복수명사구 The first few nights에 수일치해야 하므로, was를 복수동사 were로 고친다.)
ⓒ was slept → sleeping (동사(was)가 있는 완전한 절(Bezi was still very sick)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로 흐름상 Bezi를 부연 설명하는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 분사구문의 의미상의 주어인 Bezi가 ‘잠을 자는’ 주체이므로 was sleeping을 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 sleeping으로 고친다.)
ⓔ frowns → frown 또는 frowning (과거동사 saw와 목적어 the veterinarian에 이어져 ‘see+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 것을 듣다)’의 지각동사의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리로, 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동일 때는 동사원형, 능동·진행일 때는 현재분사, 수동일 때는 과거분사가 쓰인다. 목적어 the veterinarian이 ‘얼굴을 찌푸리는’ 주체이므로, frowns를 능동을 나타내는 동사원형 frown 또는 능동·진행의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 frowning으로 고친다.)
*원래 지문에는 frown이 쓰였음
ⓕ whom → that (완전한 절(all elephants have a slower heartbeat than humans)을 이끌어 동사 reassured의 목적격 보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, whom을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ It seems (that) ~(~인 것 같다)의 문장 구조로, 완전한 절(you’re good with animals)을 이끄는 명사절 접속사 that이 생략되었고, 앞의 형식주어 it은 알맞다.
ⓓ 동사 drank의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끌고 선행사 the amounts를 수식하는 관계사절을 이끄는 목적격 관계대명사 that은 알맞다.

body:
G: Daehun, did you know that sunsets on Mars are different from those on Earth?
B: Really? You mean they’re not red and orange?
G: That’s right, they aren’t. Sunsets are somewhat blue on Mars.
B: Wow! Why is that?
G: It’s because of the Martian atmosphere. Unlike Earth’s atmosphere, it’s full of large dust particles.
B: How does that affect the sunset colors?
G: When the sun sets on Mars, these particles filter out the red light from the sun and allow only the blue light to reach our eyes.
B: Oh, that’s really surprising!
G: Plus, the sky on Mercury would look black during the day because the planet has virtually no atmosphere.
B: Interesting! I’m surprised to learn that each planet has such unique features.

다음 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Sunsets on Earth are generally red or orange.
The Martian atmosphere is full of large dust particles.
The dust particles in Mars’s atmosphere make its sunsets appear blue.
The light from the sun includes both red and blue light.
Mercury’s atmosphere blocks the red light coming from the sun.

body:
W: Today, we have Mr. Robert Smith, a botanist and astronaut, joining us from the International Space Station. Hi, Robert! How does Earth look from up there?
M: It’s shiny and blue, as always.
W: Sounds incredible. Can you explain what your mission is?

ⓐ Unbelievable! Why did you want to become an astronaut?
ⓑ I do plant growth experiments. I’ve been growing vegetables such as tomatoes and peppers here.
ⓒ I’ve always been interested in how plants grow in space.
ⓓ I see. What training did you go through to become an astronaut?

M: Well, I had to take several difficult training courses, such as the weightlessness experience and running in a space suit for six hours in a pool.
W: That’s amazing. What qualities do you think are necessary to become an astronaut?
M: Scientific knowledge is essential, but physical and mental health are just as important.

다음 주어진 대화에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 임무가 무엇인지 묻는 여자의 질문에 남자가 우주에서 식물 성장 실험을 하고 있다고 답하는 ⓑ, 이에 여자가 놀라움을 표현하며 우주비행사가 되고 싶었던 이유를 묻는 ⓐ, 남자가 식물이 우주에서 어떻게 자라는지에 항상 관심이 있었다고 그 이유를 설명하는 ⓒ, 이어 여자가 우주비행사가 되기 위해 어떤 훈련을 받았는지 묻는 ⓓ로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

body:
[1]
When we observe space from the ground, Earth’s atmosphere creates obstacles for our vision. It absorbs specific types of lights such as ultraviolet and infrared, causing distortions in our observations and making some objects beyond the atmosphere invisible. Consequently, the space we see from Earth’s surface can differ significantly from its actual appearance. To overcome these limitations, telescopes are launched into space beyond Earth’s atmosphere.
Space telescopes are specifically designed to capture a spectrum of light that is not visible on Earth. This capability provides us with a clear and uninterrupted view of celestial objects, allowing us to better observe stars, black holes, and galaxies located billions of light years away from Earth. The data and images gathered by space telescopes are invaluable to scientists, ⓐenabling them to study the birth and death of celestial bodies and their unique characteristics.
[2]
Thorough space exploration goes beyond remote observations and includes up-close examinations of celestial bodies, material collection, and on-site experiments. While human astronauts can be sent on these missions, it is often safer and more cost-effective ⓑuse robots. Robots can better withstand the harsh conditions of space, including extreme temperatures and high radiation levels ⓒthat can pose serious risks to human astronauts.
A variety of robots have ⓓbeen developed for space missions. Some are designed to land on celestial bodies, while others are built for flyby missions. Some robots remain in fixed positions, while others are engineered for mobility. Robots also come in a range of shapes, ⓔresembling those of spacecraft, vehicles, or even humans. They are categorized and named according to their specific functions.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓑ use → to use
(문장 맨 앞에 온 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어 자리이므로 동사원형 use를 명사적 용법의 to부정사 to use로 고친다.)

Among the various space telescopes in operation, the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, stands out as an ⓐunprecedented achievement in space technology. Orbiting approximately 600 kilometers above Earth’s atmosphere, Hubble has transmitted incredibly detailed images of space, ⓑrevolutionizing our understanding of the universe. It has played a crucial role in facilitating pioneering discoveries about the relationships between celestial bodies, the formation of galaxies, and the expansion of the universe. [1]
Probes are one notable type of space robots. These spacecraft-like robots are designed to capture photos and gather data without needing to land on celestial bodies. For example, the twin Voyagers launched in 1977 are historic probes. These probes successfully flew by the major outer planets of our solar system — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune — (A)[discovered / discovering] numerous fascinating details about them. Voyager 1 first entered interstellar space in 2012 and became the farthest human-made object from Earth.
[2]
Another widely recognized type of space robot is the rover, a robotic vehicle (B)[designed / was designed] to move across the surface of planets and moons to explore their environments. Equipped with various scientific instruments, rovers conduct experiments and investigations while in motion, functioning like roaming laboratories. An iconic example is Curiosity, (C)[which / where] landed on Mars in 2012. This car-sized rover made significant discoveries about Mars’s past. It found signs of a water stream on a crater’s floor and identified chemicals such as carbon in a powder sample drilled from a rock. ⓐ이러한 발견들은 과거 화성에 어떤 형태의 생명체가 존재했을지도 모른다는 가능성을 시사한다.

[1]
Since ancient times, we have looked to the sky with wonder, ⓐcurious about what lies beyond our world. This inherent desire to explore the universe has encouraged technological innovations that can aid us in this pursuit. Among these advancements are space telescopes and space robots, which ⓑhave paved the way for our journey toward understanding the mysteries of space.
[2]
When we observe space from the ground, Earth’s atmosphere creates obstacles for our vision. It absorbs specific types of lights such as ultraviolet and infrared, causing distortions in our observations and making some objects beyond the atmosphere invisible. Consequently, the space we see from Earth’s surface can differ significantly from its actual appearance. To overcome these limitations, telescopes are launched into space beyond Earth’s atmosphere.
Space telescopes are specifically designed to capture a spectrum of light that is not visible on Earth. This capability provides us with a clear and uninterrupted view of celestial objects, allowing us to better observe stars, black holes, and galaxies ⓒlocate billions of light years away from Earth. The data and images gathered by space telescopes are invaluable to scientists, enabling them to study the birth and death of celestial bodies and their unique characteristics.
Among the various space telescopes in operation, the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, stands out as an unprecedented achievement in space technology. ⓓOrbited approximately 600 kilometers above Earth’s atmosphere, Hubble has transmitted incredibly detailed images of space, revolutionizing our understanding of the universe. It has played a crucial role in facilitating pioneering discoveries about the relationships between celestial bodies, the formation of galaxies, and the expansion of the universe. Moreover, its breathtaking images have sparked people’s imaginations and made space exploration an even ⓔmore intriguing journey.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?

(명사구 stars, black holes, and galaxies(별과 블랙홀, 은하)를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, locate는 ‘위치하다, 위치시키다’라는 뜻의 타동사로 수식을 받는 대상인 수식을 받는 stars, black holes, and galaxies가 ‘위치한’ 대상이므로 locate는 수동의 의미인 과거분사 located로 고친다.)
ⓓ Orbited → Orbiting
(완전한 절(Hubble ~ space) 앞에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 Hubble이 ‘궤도를 그리며 도는’ 주체이며, orbit이 ‘궤도를 돌다’라는 뜻의 자동사로 쓰였으므로 Orbited는 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 Orbiting으로 고친다.)
