body:
Born in 1954, Sonia Sotomayor is an American lawyer. She is the first Latin-American Supreme Court justice in US history.
For each of you, different courses and topics you study will help you navigate your lives in different ways. Whichever way these are for you, I know that they will help you on your journey, because education empowers you to grow beyond the limits you once knew, and it takes you beyond the places and ways of thinking you already know and exposes you to the greater potential that exists in the world. My education taught me about the Supreme Court, a workplace beyond my wildest dreams as a child. But the value of an education diminishes unless you put it to use, particularly good use. Good use includes earning a living and supporting your families. But it also means something much more significant. It means contributing to the betterment of the community and world you live in. That betterment does not have to be in a big or public way like becoming a Supreme Court justice. My grandmother bettered her community by ensuring that no one around her ever went hungry. My mom as a practical nurse would give shots to neighbors who needed them or help others with blood pressure readings or changing of bandages. Just as I am sure you have learned, my family taught me to measure happiness not by what I do as work but by what I give to others. It is the most important lesson and the deepest source of meaning I have found in life.
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Education keeps people within the boundaries they are already familiar with.
As a child, Sotomayor had clearly pictured herself working at the Supreme Court.
According to Sotomayor, education becomes less valuable when it is not used well.
Sotomayor believes that improving one's community requires a highly visible role like a Supreme Court justice.
Sotomayor's family taught her to judge happiness by her career achievements.

⑤ Sotomayor의 가족은 그녀에게 자신의 직업적 성취로 행복을 판단하라고 가르쳤다. (→그녀의 가족은 자신이 직업으로서 무슨 일을 하는가가 아니라 다른 사람들에게 무엇을 베푸는가로 행복을 측정하라고 가르쳤다.)

body:
Number One. Seek joy, not happiness. What is happiness? Happiness is an emotional response to an outcome. Happiness demands a certain outcome. In other words, it depends on the outcome. If I win, I will be happy. If I don’t, I won’t. This kind of standard makes happiness something that we can’t sustain because we immediately raise the standard every time we achieve it. Therefore, if happiness is what you’re after, then you’re going to be disappointed frequently and be unhappy for much of your time. However, joy is a different thing. It’s not a reaction to a specific outcome. Joy is a constant feeling that we experience when we do what we are meant to do, regardless of the outcome.
Personally, as an actor, I used to have an attitude that focused on the outcome, thinking, “I need this film to be a box office success. I need my performance to be acknowledged.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor a means to a certain end, I began to enjoy my work and literally became happier. As soon as the daily act of making a movie or performing a role became its own reward for me, I received more box office successes and more awards than I ever had before. However, what I realized was that aside from the results, joy was always with me. Remember that joy is always “in process” and we are always making it.
다음 글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Career success is the most dependable source of lasting happiness.
Happiness and joy are similar in that both rely on achieving specific goals.
Enjoying our daily work is the surest way to achieve greater external success.
We should pursue joy in the process rather than happiness dependent on results.
We should keep raising our standards after reaching each goal to stay motivated.

body:
Number two. The process of elimination is the first step to finding our identity. In 1992, I got my first job as an actor. Initially, I only had three lines, but the director suggested giving me more scenes and lines. I was thrilled and agreed to the offer because it meant more screen time and a higher income. However, a few years ago, when I watched the film again, I realized that there were two scenes where my character, Wooderson, didn’t fit in. I shouldn’t have been there, and neither should Wooderson. It is just as important to know where we don’t belong as it is to know where we do.
So, the first step that leads to our identity in life is usually realizing who we are not. Defining ourselves by who we are not helps us truly understand who we are. You know that some friends you hang out with really don’t bring out the best in you. They may bully and gossip too much or engage in questionable behavior. You know that they really aren’t going to be there for you when you’re in trouble. Now, be assertive and stop giving them your time and energy. When you let them go, you’ll find yourself spending more time in more places that are healthier for you. By eliminating the things that are keeping you from your identity, you will only have important things left in front of you. Knowing who we are is hard. It’s really hard. So, eliminate who you are not, first. Then, you’re going to find where you need to be and who you truly are.
다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
Discovering our true self usually begins with (A)______ things that do not truly represent us, and (B)______ such things leaves us with only what really matters.
(A) (B)
choices: recognizing embracing
recognizing removing
ignoring embracing
hiding removing
ignoring analyzing

Number three. Give your fears credit. You know what? I try to scare myself at least once a day. I get butterflies in my stomach every morning before I go to work. I was nervous before I got here to speak tonight. I think fear is an asset because it increases our need to dare ourselves to overcome that fear. Suppose you have a fear of rejection. You want to ask somebody out, but you fear that he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed to admit them and give them the credit they deserve. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t deny that they exist, abandoning your opportunity to overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined to have to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, confront your fears and give them credit, and you will find the courage to overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.

G: Daehun, did you know that sunsets on Mars are different from those on Earth?
B: Really? You mean they’re not red and orange?
G: That’s right, they aren’t. Sunsets are somewhat blue on Mars.
B: Wow! Why is that?
G: It’s because of the Martian atmosphere. Unlike Earth’s atmosphere, it’s full of large dust particles.
B: How does that affect the sunset colors?
G: When the sun sets on Mars, these particles filter out the red light from the sun and allow only the blue light to reach our eyes.
B: Oh, that’s really surprising!
G: Plus, the sky on Mercury would look black during the day because the planet has virtually no atmosphere.
B: Interesting! ______ learn that each planet has such unique features.

how different atmospheric conditions affect the color of planets’ skies
the influence of solar distance on the temperatures of different planets
the way planetary rotation affects the length of day and night
the reasons behind the formation of dust storms on Mars

body:
Since ancient times, we have looked to the sky with wonder, curious about (A)[that / what] lies beyond our world. This inherent desire to explore the universe has encouraged technological innovations (B)[what / that] can aid us in this pursuit. Among these advancements are space telescopes and space robots, (C)[that / which] have paved the way for our journey toward understanding the mysteries of space.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: what / that / which
that / what / which

that / that / that
what / what / which
solution:
(A) ‘자동사+전치사구’ 구조의 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(lies beyond our world)을 이끌어 전치사 about의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하며, 문맥상 우리의 세계 너머에 ‘무엇이’ 있는지를 궁금해 하는 것이므로 의문사와 주어의 역할을 동시에 하여 명사절인 간접의문문을 이루는 의문대명사 what이 적절하다.
(B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(can ~ pursuit)을 이끌어 명사구 technological innovations를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 주격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.
(C) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(have ~ space)을 이끌어, 앞의 명사구 space telescopes and space robots(우주 망원경들과 우주 로봇들)를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.

When we observe space from the ground, Earth’s atmosphere creates obstacles for our vision. It absorbs specific types of lights such as ultraviolet and infrared, causing distortions in our observations and ⓐmade some objects beyond the atmosphere invisible. (A) To overcome these limitations, telescopes are launched into space beyond Earth’s atmosphere. (B)
Space telescopes are specifically designed to capture a spectrum of light that ⓑis not visible on Earth. (C) This capability provides us with a clear and uninterrupted view of celestial objects, ⓒallowing us to better observe stars, black holes, and galaxies located billions of light years away from Earth. (D) The data and images ⓓare gathered by space telescopes are invaluable to scientists, enabling them to study the birth and death of celestial bodies and their unique characteristics. (E)
Among the various space telescopes in operation, the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, ⓔstands out as an unprecedented achievement in space technology. Orbiting approximately 600 kilometers above Earth’s atmosphere, Hubble has transmitted incredibly detailed images of space, revolutionizing our understanding of the universe. It has played a crucial role in facilitating pioneering discoveries about the relationships between celestial bodies, the formation of galaxies, and the expansion of the universe. Moreover, its breathtaking images have sparked people’s imaginations and made space exploration an even more intriguing journey.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?

solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘결과적으로, 우리가 지구 표면에서 보는 우주는 실제 모습과 상당히 다를 수 있다.’라는 뜻으로, 앞의 내용으로 인한 결과를 나타내는 연결어 Consequently가 쓰였으므로, 이 문장 앞에는 지구 표면에서 관측한 우주의 모습이 실제 모습과 달라질 수 있는 원인이 제시되어야 한다. 따라서 지구의 대기가 우리 시야에 장애물을 만들어 관측에 왜곡을 일으키고 대기권 너머의 일부 물체들을 보이지 않게 한다는 내용 다음이자 한계를 극복하기 위해 망원경을 대기 너머의 우주로 발사한다는 내용 앞인 (A)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

To prepare for Hubble’s retirement, the James Webb Space Telescope was launched as its successor in 2021. Webb is a state-of-the-art space telescope with capabilities superior to those of any other telescope. It features a honeycomb-patterned mirror that is about three times larger in diameter than Hubble’s round-shaped mirror, resulting in an image collection area that is 6.25 times wider. Positioned 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, Webb orbits the Sun alongside Earth, while Hubble orbits Earth itself. Webb also specializes in capturing infrared light, which can pass through dusty regions more effectively than the visible light used by Hubble. These features enable Webb to offer a view of space with greatly enhanced clarity and minimal interference. As Webb continues its mission, it is expected to offer deeper insights into the birth of the universe and the evolutionary processes following the Big Bang.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the contrasting observational abilities of two space telescopes
the discovery of new planets through astronomical observations
the challenges of maintaining space telescopes over extended missions
the engineering challenges of designing a honeycomb-patterned mirror
the enhancement of astronomical observations through Webb's advanced technology

Thorough space exploration goes beyond remote observations and includes up-close examinations of celestial bodies, material collection, and on-site experiments. While human astronauts can be sent on these missions, it is often safer and more cost-effective to use robots. Robots can better withstand the harsh conditions of space, including extreme temperatures and high radiation levels that can pose serious risks to human astronauts.

body:
Probes are one notable type of space robots. These spacecraft-like robots are designed to capture photos and gather data without needing to land on celestial bodies. For example, the twin Voyagers ⓐlaunched in 1977 are historic probes. These probes successfully flew by the major outer planets of our solar system — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune — discovering numerous fascinating details about them. One of the Voyagers’ significant findings was the presence of highly active volcanoes on Io, one of Jupiter’s moons, ⓑmarking the first evidence of geological processes observed on other planets. After completing their planetary missions, these probes continued their journey beyond our solar system. Voyager 1 first entered interstellar space in 2012 and became the farthest human-made object from Earth.
Another widely recognized type of space robot is the rover, a robotic vehicle designed to move across the surface of planets and moons to explore their environments. ⓒEquipped with various scientific instruments, rovers conduct experiments and investigations while in motion, functioning like roaming laboratories. An iconic example is Curiosity, ⓓwhich landed on Mars in 2012. This car-sized rover made significant discoveries about Mars’s past. It found signs of a water stream on a crater’s floor and identified chemicals such as carbon in a powder sample drilled from a rock. These findings suggest the possibility ⓔwhich some form of life might have existed on Mars in the past.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 관계대명사 that을 두 번 사용할 것
• 배수사를 사용한 비교 표현을 두 번 사용할 것
• 분사구문을 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용하되, 필요시 변형할 것
• 각 빈칸에 한 단어씩 쓸 것 (숫자도 한 단어로 봄)
<보기>
6.25 times, large, result in, wide, feature, an image collection area, three times, a honeycomb-patterned mirror, about
→ It ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ in diameter than Hubble’s round-shaped mirror, ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______ ______.
answer: features a honeycomb-patterned mirror that is about three times larger, resulting in an image collection area that is 6.25 times wider
solution:
• 단수주어 It에 수일치한 단수동사 features와 목적어 a honeycomb-patterned mirror를 쓰고, 목적어인 a honeycomb-patterned mirror를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 영작하되 <조건>에 따라 관계대명사 that를 쓰고, 선행사에 수일치한 단수동사 is를 쓴 다음, 숫자 앞에서 ‘약, 대략’이라는 뜻을 나타내는 부사 about 뒤에 <조건>에서 언급한 배수사를 사용한 비교 표현인 three times larger를 이어서 쓴다.
• 완전한 절(It ~ mirror)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지고 있으므로 <조건>에 따라 분사구문으로 영작한다. 의미상 주어인 앞 절의 내용(It ~ mirror)이 ‘초래하는’ 주체이므로 ’~을 초래하다‘를 뜻하는 구동사 result in을 능동의 의미인 현재분사구 resulting in으로 변형하여 쓰고 전치사 in 뒤에 목적어인 an image collection area를 쓴다.
• 명사구 an image collection area를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 영작한다. 관계대명사 that과 선행사에 수일치한 단수동사 is를 쓰고, 배수사 6.25 times(6.25배)와 형용사 wide의 비교급 wider를 이어 쓴다.

All the philosophical dilemmas about whether translation “reflects” or instead “transforms” what’s in the original ⓐ[needs / need] to be swept aside. This is exactly the dichotomy ⓑ[that / what] Merleau-Ponty’s account of perception is trying to free us from: are we “seeing” objects or “constituting” them? Neither, because we perceive things in a world we live in and have the power ⓒ[to transform / transforms]: a chair is something we can go sit in; a mug is something we can pick up. (A) One of Merleau-Ponty’s many great metaphors is that perception neither finds the world nor creates it: it reveals it, which he expresses using the term révélateur, the developing fluid for photographs in a darkroom. (B) Photographic development involves a series of chemical reactions that require precise temperature and timing. (C) The act of seeing develops what’s in the world, like developing a photograph. (D) Likewise, a translation “develops the photograph” of the original text. (E) Translators don’t simply “recognize” what’s there, but nor are we “changing” it into anything it isn’t already, though we can be more or less aggressively interventionist in our darkroom. As a translator I take up the affordances of the original, moving through its world and ㉠______.

choices: what realizing go
what realized to go
that realized go

that realized to go
solution:

You want to ask somebody out, but you fear ⓑthat he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed to admit them and give them the credit they ⓒare deserved. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t deny that they exist, abandoning your opportunity ⓓto overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined to have to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, confront your fears and ⓔgive them credit, and you will find the courage to overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ are deserved → deserve (앞의 주어 they가 가리키는 fears가 타동사 deserve(~을 받을 만하다)의 주체이며, 명사구 the credit이 의미상 목적어에 해당하므로, they 이하는 앞에 목적격 관계대명사 which 또는 that이 생략된 채로 선행사인 the credit을 수식하는 관계사절이며, 능동태 타동사 deserve의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절의 형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 수동태 are deserved를 능동태 deserve로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ to부정사를 이루는 동사원형 scare의 목적어 자리이며, to부정사의 의미상 주어인 I와 동일한 대상이므로, 재귀 용법의 재귀대명사 myself는 알맞다.
ⓔ 동사원형으로 시작하는 앞의 명령문(confront your fears)과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되는 두 번째 명령문을 이끌어야 하므로, 동사원형 give는 알맞다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 다음과 같이 쓸 때, 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 문장을 완성하시오.
<조건>
• 명사절 접속사는 생략할 것
• 형용사적 용법의 to부정사를 한 번 사용할 것
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 사용할 것 (필요시 변형할 것)
• (1)은 4단어, (2)는 8단어로 영작할 것
<보기>
dare, increase, overcome, an asset, our need
I think (1) ______ because it (2) ______ that fear.
answer:
(1) fear is an asset
(2) increases our need to dare ourselves to overcome
solution:
(1) think의 목적어 자리에 <조건>에 따라 명사절 접속사 that은 생략하고 완전한 절이 이어지도록 ‘주어+be동사+보어’ 형태로 fear is an asset을 쓴다.
(2) because가 이끄는 절의 주어 it에 수일치하도록 increase를 단수동사 increases로 변형하고, 목적어로 명사구 our need를 쓴다. <조건>에 따라 형용사적 용법의 to부정사를 사용해 명사구 our need를 수식하는 to부정사구가 이어지도록 dare를 to부정사인 to dare로 변형한다. 이어서 ‘~을 부추겨서 …하게 하다’라는 뜻의 ‘dare+목적어+to부정사(구)’를 사용하되, to부정사인 to dare의 의미상 주어(우리)와 dare의 목적어가 동일한 대상이므로 재귀 용법의 재귀대명사 ourselves를 목적어 자리에 쓴 후, overcome을 to부정사인 to overcome으로 변형한다.

Born in 1954, Sonia Sotomayor is an American lawyer. She is the first Latin-American Supreme Court justice in US history.
For each of you, different courses and topics you study will help you navigate your lives in different ways. ⓐWhichever way these are for you, I know that they will help you on your journey, because education empowers you ⓑto grow beyond the limits you once knew, and it takes you beyond the places and ways of thinking you already know and ⓒexpose you to the greater potential that exists in the world. My education taught me about the Supreme Court, a workplace beyond my wildest dreams as a child. But the value of an education diminishes unless (A)______. Good use includes earning a living and supporting your families. But it also means something ⓓmuch more significant. It means contributing to the betterment of the community and world you live in. That betterment does not have to be in a big or public way like becoming a Supreme Court justice. My grandmother bettered her community by ensuring ⓔthat no one around her ever went hungry. My mom as a practical nurse would give shots to neighbors who needed them or help others with blood pressure readings or changing of bandages. Just as I am sure you have learned, my family taught me ⓕmeasure happiness not by what I do as work but by what I give to others. It is the most important lesson and the deepest source of meaning I have found in life.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓒ expose → exposes (노출시키는 주체가 주어 it이므로, 단수동사 takes가 이끄는 동사구 ‘takes ~ know’와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되는 동사구를 이끌도록 expose를 단수동사 exposes로 고친다.)
ⓕ measure → to measure (동사 teach는 ‘teach+목적어+목적격보어(~에게 …하도록 가르치다)’의 5형식 구문에서 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하므로, taught와 목적어 me에 이어진 목적격보어 자리의 동사원형 measure를 to부정사인 to measure로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ ‘~에게 …할 권한을 부여하다’라는 뜻으로 ‘empower+목적어+to부정사(구)’를 사용하므로, empowers와 목적어 you 뒤에 이어진 to부정사 to grow는 알맞다.
ⓓ -thing으로 끝나는 부정대명사는 형용사가 뒤에서 수식하며, much는 ‘훨씬’이라는 의미로 비교급을 강조할 수 있으므로, something 뒤에 비교급 강조 부사 much와 비교급 형태의 형용사 more significant가 이어진 형태의 much more significant는 알맞다.

body:
Number One. Seek joy, not happiness. What is happiness? Happiness is an emotional response to an outcome. Happiness demands a certain outcome. In other words, it depends on the outcome. If I win, I will be happy. If I don’t, I won’t. This kind of standard makes happiness something that we can’t sustain because we immediately raise the standard every time we achieve it. Therefore, if happiness is what you’re after, then you’re going to be disappointed frequently and be unhappy for much of your time. However, joy is a different thing. It’s not a reaction to a specific outcome. Joy is a constant feeling that we experience when we do what we are meant to do, regardless of the outcome.
Personally, as an actor, I used to have an attitude that focused on the outcome, thinking, “I need this film to be a box office success. I need my performance to be acknowledged.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor a means to a certain end, I began to enjoy my work and literally became happier. As soon as the daily act of making a movie or performing a role became its own reward for me, I received more box office successes and more awards than I ever had before. However, what I realized was that aside from the results, joy was always with me. Remember that joy is always “in process” and we are always making it.
윗글의 두 번째 단락에 드러난 ‘I’의 태도 변화로 알맞은 것은?
choices: indifferent to success → hungry for fame
eager for recognition → obsessed with awards
confident in his talent → doubtful of his ability
fixated on results → absorbed in the work itself
engrossed in the task itself → focused on results

body:
Number two. The process of elimination is the first step to finding our identity. In 1992, I got my first job as an actor. Initially, I only had three lines, but the director suggested giving me more scenes and lines. I was thrilled and agreed to the offer because it meant more screen time and a higher income. However, a few years ago, when I watched the film again, I realized that there were two scenes where my character, Wooderson, didn’t fit in. I shouldn’t have been there, and neither should Wooderson. It is just as important to know where we don’t belong as it is to know where we do.
So, the first step that leads to our identity in life is usually realizing who we are not. Defining ourselves by who we are not helps us truly understand who we are. You know that some friends you hang out with really don’t bring out the best in you. They may bully and gossip too much or engage in questionable behavior. You know that they really aren’t going to be there for you when you’re in trouble. Now, be assertive and stop giving them your time and energy. When you let them go, you’ll find yourself spending more time in more places that are healthier for you. By eliminating the things that are keeping you from your identity, you will only have important things left in front of you. Knowing who we are is hard. It’s really hard. So, eliminate who you are not, first. Then, you’re going to find where you need to be and who you truly are.
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: The director's offer of additional scenes was turned down.
Problems in some scenes were noticed as soon as the film was released.
Recognizing the places we don't fit in is regarded as less valuable than recognizing where we belong.
Letting go of friends who have a bad influence on us will lead us to healthier environments.
We are advised to find our real selves before removing what does not suit us.
solution:
여러분의 가장 좋은 면을 끌어내지 못하고, 너무 많이 괴롭히거나 험담을 할 수도 있는 친구들에게 시간과 에너지를 그만 쏟으라고 하며, 그들을 놓아줄 때 자신에게 더 건강한 곳에서 더 많은 시간을 보내게 될 것이라고 했으므로, ④ '우리에게 나쁜 영향을 미치는 친구들을 놓아주는 것은 우리를 더 건강한 환경으로 이끌 것이다.'는 일치하는 내용이다.
오답
① 추가 장면에 대한 감독의 제안은 거절되었다. (→‘I’는 신이 나서 그 제안을 수락했다.)
② 영화가 개봉되자마자 일부 장면의 문제점이 발견되었다. (→몇 년 전에 그 영화를 다시 보았을 때 자신의 캐릭터가 어울리지 않는 두 개의 장면이 있다는 것을 깨달았다.)
③ 우리가 어울리지 않는 곳을 인식하는 것은 우리가 속한 곳을 인식하는 것보다 덜 가치 있는 것으로 여겨진다. (→우리가 속하지 않는 곳을 아는 것은 우리가 속한 곳을 아는 것만큼 중요하다.)
⑤ 우리는 우리에게 맞지 않는 것을 제거하기 전에 우리의 진정한 자아를 찾으라는 조언을 받는다. (→먼저 자신이 아닌 존재를 제거할 때, 자신이 있어야 할 곳과 진정한 자신을 찾게 될 것이라는 조언을 받는다.)

body:
Number three. Give your fears credit. You know what? I try to scare myself at least once a day. I get butterflies in my stomach every morning before I go to work. I was nervous before I got here to speak tonight. I think fear is an asset because it increases our need to dare ourselves to overcome that fear. Suppose you have a fear of rejection. You want to ask somebody out, but you fear that he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed to admit them and give them the credit they deserve. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t deny that they exist, abandoning your opportunity to overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined to have to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, confront your fears and give them credit, and you will find the courage to overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.
I hope you find joy in the process of doing what you’re meant to do. Find your identity by eliminating who you are not. Move forward, overcoming your fears. You are the author of the book on your life. So even if you make mistakes, turn the page and just keep living. Thank you and good luck.
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Fear is something valuable that pushes us to challenge ourselves.
Denying our fears helps protect the chance to get over them.
Everyone is bound to face their greatest fear sooner or later.
Overcoming our fears allows us to become stronger and to value ourselves more.
Making mistakes is no reason to stop moving forward with our lives.

Born in 1954, Sonia Sotomayor is an American lawyer. She is the first Latin-American Supreme Court justice in US history.
For each of you, different courses and topics you study will help you navigate your lives in different ways. Whichever way these are for you, I know that they will help you on your journey, because education empowers you to grow beyond the limits you once knew, and it takes you beyond the places and ways of thinking you already know and exposes you to the greater potential that exists in the world. My education taught me about the Supreme Court, a workplace beyond my wildest dreams as a child. But the value of an education diminishes unless you put it to use, particularly good use. Good use includes earning a living and supporting your families. But it also means something much more significant. It means contributing to the betterment of the community and world you live in. That betterment does not have to be in a big or public way like becoming a Supreme Court justice. My grandmother bettered her community by ensuring that no one around her ever went hungry. My mom as a practical nurse would give shots to neighbors who needed them or help others with blood pressure readings or changing of bandages. Just as I am sure you have learned, my family taught me to measure happiness not by what I do as work but by what I give to others. It is the most important lesson and the deepest source of meaning I have found in life.

Hughie Erskine was a (A)[wonderful / wonderfully] good-looking man, with crisp brown hair, a sculpture-like profile, and grey eyes. He had every accomplishment except (B)[that / those] of making money. He lived on two hundred pounds a year (C)[what / that] an old aunt gave him. He had tried everything. He had gone to the stock exchange for six months. He had been a tea merchant for a little longer. Ultimately, he became nothing. He was a delightful, incompetent young man with a perfect profile and no profession.
To make matters worse, he was in love. The girl he loved was Laura Merton, the daughter of a retired colonel. Laura loved Hughie, too, and the colonel was very fond of him. However, he would not hear of any engagement. He would say “Come to me, my boy, ⓐ______, and we will talk about it.”

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) / (B) / (C)
choices: wonderful / that / what
wonderful / those / that
wonderfully / those / what
wonderfully / that / what
wonderfully / that / that
solution:
(A) 뒤의 형용사 good-looking을 수식하는 자리이므로 부사 wonderfully가 적절하다.
(B) 앞에 나온 단수명사 accomplishment를 대신하는 대명사 자리이므로 단수형 that이 적절하다.
(C) 선행사 two hundred pounds a year가 있고, 뒤에 gave의 직접목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절이 이어지므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다. what은 선행사를 포함하므로 앞에 별도의 선행사를 두지 않는다.

After some time, a servant came in and told Trevor that the frame maker wanted to speak to him.
“Don’t run away, Hughie,” he said as he went out. “I will be back in a moment.”
The old beggar took advantage of Trevor’s absence to rest for a moment on a bench that was behind him. He looked so exhausted and miserable that Hughie ______. Hughie reached into his pocket to see how much money he had. All he could find was a few coins. “Poor old fellow,” he thought to himself. “He needs money more than I do.” He walked across the studio and slipped a gold coin into the beggar’s hand.
The old man was startled, and a faint smile came across his dry lips. “Thank you, sir,” he said. “Thank you.”
When Trevor returned, Hughie said goodbye and left the studio, blushing a little at what he had done, and he walked home.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: wanted Trevor to finish the painting quickly
could not help feeling sorry for him
wondered whether the model was truly poor
felt uncomfortable staying alone with him
hoped to find a better model for Trevor
solution:
노인이 매우 지치고 비참해 보였고, 이어서 Hughie가 자신보다 노인에게 돈이 더 필요하다고 생각하며 금화를 건네므로, 빈칸에는 ② ‘Hughie는 그를 불쌍히 여기지 않을 수 없었다’가 가장 적절하다.
본문변형 could not help pitying him → could not help feeling sorry for him

① Hughie는 Trevor가 그림을 빨리 완성하기를 원했다
③ Hughie는 그 모델이 정말 가난한지 궁금해했다
④ Hughie는 그와 단둘이 있는 것이 불편했다
⑤ Hughie는 Trevor에게 더 나은 모델을 찾아 주기를 바랐다

body:
That night, about eleven o’clock, he wandered into a café and found Trevor sitting by himself.
“Well, Alan, did you get the picture finished all right?” he asked.
“Finished and framed, my boy!” answered Trevor.
(A)
“You told that old beggar about my private affairs?” cried Hughie, looking very red and irritated.
“My dear boy,” said Trevor, smiling. “That old beggar, as you call him, is one of the richest men in Europe. He could buy all of London tomorrow with the money in his account.”
(B)
“But he looks marvelous in them,” said Trevor. “I wouldn’t paint him in a fancy coat for anything. I’ll tell him about your offer, though. By the way, tell me how Laura is. The old model was quite interested in her.”
“What? Did you even tell him about her?” asked Hughie.
“Of course! He knows all about the strict colonel, the charming Laura, and the ten thousand pounds.”
(C)
“And, by the way, the old model you saw is quite curious about you. I had to tell him all about you: who you are, where you live, what your income is, and what prospects you have.”
(D)
“My dear Alan,” cried Hughie, “ⓐ나는 아마 집에 도착하면 그가 나를 기다리고 있는 것을 발견할 것이다. Poor old man! I wish I could do something for him. I think it is dreadful that anyone should be so miserable. I have piles of old clothes at home. Do you think he would care for any of them? His rags were falling to bits.”

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 그림을 완성했다고 답한 주어진 글에 이어, 같은 발화에서 늙은 모델이 Hughie를 궁금해해 그에 대해 다 말해야 했다고 덧붙이는 (C), 그 모델을 동정하며 헌 옷을 주고 싶어 하는 Hughie의 반응인 (D), (D)의 his rags를 them으로 받아 그 차림이 멋지다고 답하며 Laura 이야기까지 했다고 밝히는 (B), 사생활 누설에 분노하는 Hughie에게 그 거지가 유럽에서 가장 부유한 사람 중 한 명임을 알려 주는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• <보기>에 주어진 단어를 차례대로 사용할 것
• 12단어로 쓸 것
<보기>
probably, find, get
→ ______
answer: I will probably find him waiting for me when I get home.
solution:
• ‘나는 아마 ~을 발견할 것이다’는 미래시제 will과 부사 probably를 결합해 will probably find로 쓰고, probably는 조동사와 동사원형 사이에 둔다.
• ‘find+목적어+현재분사’(~가 …하고 있는 것을 발견하다) 구조에서 목적어 him이 ‘기다리는’ 주체이므로 목적격보어로 능동 의미의 현재분사 waiting을 써서 나타낸다.
• '집에 도착하면'은 시간을 나타내는 부사절이므로 미래의 일이라도 현재시제를 써서 when I get home으로 쓴다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (D)의 우리말을 주어진 <조건>에 알맞게 영작하시오.
<조건>
• understand, why, interest, know, all, so, be를 사용할 것(필요시 변형할 것)
• 간접의문문을 사용할 것
• 13단어로 쓸 것 (축약형은 한 단어로 셀 것)
→ ______
answer: I couldn't understand why he was so interested to know all about you
solution:
• '이해할 수 없었다'는 could의 부정형 couldn't 뒤에 understand를 써서 나타내고, understand의 목적어로 '왜 ~했는지'를 나타내는 간접의문문을 쓰므로 '의문사+주어+동사' 어순인 why he was so interested로 쓴다.
• 주어 he가 ‘관심을 가지게 된’ 대상이므로 과거분사형 형용사 interested로 변형하여 쓰고, 부사 so가 앞에서 수식하도록 배열한다.
• ‘~하는 데 관심이 있는’이라는 뜻이 되도록 형용사 interested를 뒤에서 수식하는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to know를 쓰고, ‘당신에 대한 모든 것’은 all about you로 쓴다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓘ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓔ were written → was written (‘전치사+관계대명사’인 on which 뒤에서 주어와 동사가 도치된 구조이며, 뒤에 이어지는 주어가 카드에 적힌 문구 하나이므로 단수동사 was로 고친다.)
ⓕ let → to let (‘tell+목적어+to부정사’(~에게 …하라고 말하다) 구조이므로, 목적어 the servant 뒤에 목적격보어로 to let을 쓴다.)
ⓗ sealing → sealed (수식 대상인 envelope가 ‘봉해진’ 대상이므로, 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 sealing을 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 sealed로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 주어 he가 옷을 ‘입은 상태’를 나타내므로 dressed는 적절하다.
ⓑ keep의 목적어로 쓰인 동명사 smiling과 등위접속사 and로 병렬을 이루므로 rubbing은 적절하다.
ⓒ는 형용사 interested 뒤에서 '~하고 싶어 하는'의 의미를 완성하는 to부정사이므로 to know가 쓰인 것은 어법상 적절하다.
ⓓ 주어 The best thing I can do에 동사 do가 포함되어 있어 주격보어 자리의 to부정사에서 to를 생략할 수 있으므로 원형부정사 go가 쓰인 것은 어법상 적절하다.
ⓖ 전치사 of의 목적어 자리이므로 동명사 addressing이 쓰인 것은 어법상 적절하다.
ⓘ 장소를 나타내는 Inside가 앞에 놓이면서 주어와 동사가 도치되었으며, 주어 a check가 단수이므로 was는 적절하다.

solution:
남작이 '늙은 거지가 보내는 결혼 선물'이라며 Hughie에게 만 파운드짜리 수표를 보내고 결혼 피로연에서 축사까지 한 내용의 글이다. 앞의 Millionaire models는 거지 모델 노릇을 한 남작처럼 '모델이 된 백만장자'를, 어순을 뒤집은 model millionaires는 '모범이 되는 백만장자'를 뜻하므로, 남을 위해 기꺼이 큰돈을 베푸는 부자는 모델이 된 부자보다 훨씬 더 드물다는 의미이다. 따라서 ④ '자신의 재산을 남에게 선의를 베푸는 데 쓰는 부자들은 찾기가 더 어렵다.'가 적절하다.

③ 부유한 사람들은 가난한 남자들의 결혼식에 좀처럼 참석하지 않는다.
⑤ 부유한 사람들은 거지들에게 좀처럼 돈을 주지 않는다.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Hughie was shocked to learn that he had given Baron Hausberg a gold coin.
Hughie felt foolish and believed that the Baron must think he was a fool.
Trevor burst out laughing when Hughie told him about giving the Baron a gold coin.
Trevor knew that Hausberg wanted his real identity to be revealed when Hughie came in.
Hughie thought Trevor should have told him that the old man was actually Baron Hausberg.
solution:
Trevor는 Hughie가 들어왔을 때 Hausberg가 자기 이름이 언급되는 것을 좋아할지 알지 못했다고 말했으므로, ④ 'Trevor는 Hughie가 들어왔을 때 Hausberg가 자신의 진짜 정체가 밝혀지기를 원한다는 것을 알고 있었다.'는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. (→Hausberg가 자기 이름이 언급되는 것을 좋아할지 알지 못했다고 말했다.)
오답
① Hughie는 자신이 Baron Hausberg에게 금화를 주었다는 것을 알고 충격을 받았다.
② Hughie는 자신이 바보 같다고 느꼈고, 남작이 틀림없이 자신을 바보로 여길 것이라고 생각했다.
③ Trevor는 Hughie가 남작에게 금화를 준 일을 이야기했을 때 웃음을 터뜨렸다.
⑤ Hughie는 Trevor가 그 노인이 실은 Baron Hausberg라고 말해 주었어야 했다고 생각했다.

One morning, Hughie dropped in to see a great friend of his, Alan Trevor. Trevor was a painter. He was a strange, rough fellow with a bushy red beard. However, when he took up the brush, he was a real master, and ⓐhis pictures were eagerly sought after.
When Hughie came into the studio, ⓑhe found Trevor putting the finishing touches on a wonderful life-size picture of a beggar. ⓒThe beggar was standing on a raised platform in a corner of the studio. He was a wrinkly old man with a pitiful expression. He wore a ragged brown cape, and he leaned on a rough stick with one hand ⓓwhile holding out his hat for donations with the other.
“What an amazing model!” said Hughie, as he shook hands with his friend. “ⓔHow miserable he looks! How much does the model get for posing?”
“A penny an hour.”
“And how much do you get for your painting, Alan?”
“Oh, I get two thousand pounds for this!”
“Well, I think the model should have a share,” cried Hughie, laughing. “He is working just as hard as you!”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때, 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: people eagerly sought after his pictures
ⓑ: he found that Trevor was putting the finishing touches on a wonderful life-size picture of a beggar
ⓒ: On a raised platform in a corner of the studio was standing the beggar.
ⓓ: while he was holding out his hat for donations with the other
ⓔ: What a miserable look he had!
solution:
현재의 모습을 나타내는 현재시제 looks를 사용했지만, 전환한 문장은 과거시제 had를 사용하여 과거의 모습을 나타내므로 원문과 같은 뜻이 되지 않는다. What a miserable look he had! 자체는 문법적으로 가능한 감탄문이다.
오답
ⓐ 구동사 seek after가 쓰인 수동태 문장 his pictures were eagerly sought after를 행위자인 일반 사람들(people)을 주어로 한 능동태로 바꾼 것이므로 전환이 적절하다.
ⓑ 'find+목적어+목적격보어' 구문에서 목적격보어로 쓰인 현재분사 putting을 that절로 바꾼 것으로, 주절의 동사 found가 과거시제이고 Hughie가 작업실에 들어갔을 때 Trevor가 그림을 마무리하고 있던 중이므로 과거진행형 was putting을 쓴 것은 적절하다.
ⓒ 장소를 나타내는 부사구 On a raised platform in a corner of the studio를 문장 앞에 두면서 동사 was standing을 주어인 명사구 the beggar 앞에 둔 도치 문장이므로 전환이 적절하다.

윗글을 아래와 같이 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
Seeing the model’s (A)______ appearance, Hughie felt that the model deserved a share of the money from Trevor’s (B)______ painting.
(A) / (B)
choices: elegant / tiny
pitiful / valuable
cheerful / expensive
miserable / ordinary
confident / unfinished
solution:
요약문 모델의 (A)측은한 모습을 본 Hughie는 모델이 Trevor의 (B)값진 그림에서 나온 돈의 몫을 받을 자격이 있다고 생각했다.

① 우아한 / 아주 작은
③ 밝은 / 값비싼
④ 비참한 / 평범한
